1064825.boardCall: Antipsychotic + fever 39.4 + generalized muscle rigidity + CK 2000 U/L -> neuroleptic malignant syndrome: discontinue risperidone
1064825.hinge: The immediate and most critical first step in managing neuroleptic malignant syndrome is immediate discontinuation of the offending dopamine-blocking antipsychotic agent.
1064825.trap: Benztropine treats acute dystonia and extrapyramidal symptoms, but worsens hyperthermia via anticholinergic mechanisms and is ineffective for NMS.

A.fit: Not here: treats dystonia; anticholinergic effects worsen hyperthermia in NMS

B.clue: Stopping the offending dopamine receptor antagonist
B.fit: Here: risperidone, temperature 39.4 C, rigidity, CK 2000 U/L

C.fit: Not here: reserved for refractory NMS after drug cessation and medical therapy

D.fit: Not here: indicated for severe acute kidney injury, not initial NMS step

E.fit: Not here: ineffective for acute life-threatening hyperthermic syndrome

nodes.text: Hyperthermia, lead-pipe rigidity, and elevated CK after risperidone suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Discontinue risperidone immediately.
Admit to intensive care for IV fluids, cooling, and renal and electrolyte monitoring.
**Marked rigidity with persistent hyperthermia despite cooling:** consider dantrolene.
**Persistent rigidity and autonomic instability despite drug withdrawal and supportive care:** consider bromocriptine or amantadine.
**Symptoms persist despite medical treatment or malignant catatonia is suspected:** consider electroconvulsive therapy.
Wait at least two weeks after recovery before cautiously restarting a lower-risk antipsychotic.

temperature is 39.4°C (103°F)
muscle rigidity in all the extremities
creatine kinase concentration of 2000 U/L

1064826.boardCall: Dichorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancy -> increased risk of preterm delivery
1064826.hinge: All multifetal pregnancies, regardless of chorionicity, have a dramatically increased risk of spontaneous preterm delivery (over 50% deliver before 37 weeks).
1064826.trap: Twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) only occurs in monochorionic twin gestations sharing a single placenta, not in dichorionic twins.

A.clue: Premature detachment of normally implanted placenta
A.fit: Not here: risk elevated with hypertension and trauma, preterm delivery far more common

B.clue: Intrauterine death of one or both fetuses
B.fit: Not here: elevated risk, but preterm delivery is the most frequent complication

C.clue: Failure of fetus to achieve growth potential
C.fit: Not here: common complication, but preterm delivery affects over 50% of twins

D.clue: Spontaneous onset of labor before 37 weeks
D.fit: Here: dichorionic-diamniotic intrauterine twin gestation

E.fit: Not here: requires monochorionic shared placenta, impossible in dichorionic twins

nodes.text: Twin gestations of any chorionicity carry an increased risk of preterm delivery.
Determine chorionicity and amnionicity on first-trimester ultrasound and follow fetal growth.
**Short cervix without dilation:** consult maternal-fetal medicine; avoid routine vaginal progesterone for twin gestation.
**Delivery expected within seven days at 24 to 33 weeks:** give antenatal betamethasone.
**Delivery imminent before 32 weeks:** add magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection.
**Dichorionic diamniotic gestation reaches 38 weeks without complications:** proceed with planned delivery.

1064827.boardCall: Medial ankle ulcer + weeping exudate + stasis dermatitis skin changes + palpable DP pulses -> stasis ulcer (venous ulcer)
1064827.hinge: An ulcer located over the medial malleolus with irregular borders, yellow exudate, surrounding bronze stasis pigmentation, and palpable distal pulses is a venous stasis ulcer.
1064827.trap: Decreased monofilament sensation suggests a neuropathic ulcer, but neuropathic ulcers occur on plantar pressure surfaces, not the medial ankle.

B.clue: Pale, punched-out distal ulcer, absent pulses
B.fit: Not here: dorsalis pedis pulses are 2+ bilaterally, ulcer is weeping
B.tempting: history of coronary disease and smoking

C.fit: Not here: medial ankle location, not on plantar weight-bearing surface

D.fit: Not here: medial malleolus location with classic venous stasis changes

E.clue: Irregular medial malleolar ulcer with hemosiderin deposition
E.fit: Here: enlarging painful ulcer on left ankle, Dorsalis pedis pulses 2+

nodes.text: Medial ankle ulcer with surrounding edema and hyperpigmentation: check ankle-brachial index (ABI)
Confirm venous etiology: ABI > 0.8 rules out significant arterial disease
Initiate multi-layer graduated compression bandaging + strict leg elevation
**Mixed arterial-venous disease present (ABI 0.5 to 0.8):** avoid high compression
**Non-healing ulcer after 6 weeks of compression:** perform duplex ultrasound
**Superficial venous reflux detected:** perform endovenous thermal ablation

1064828.boardCall: Short stature + delayed puberty at age 15 -> skeletal survey to assess epiphyseal closure before growth hormone
1064828.hinge: Growth hormone therapy can only promote linear growth if the epiphyseal growth plates remain open, assessed by bone age skeletal radiography.
1064828.trap: Chromosome analysis diagnoses Turner syndrome, but whether the patient can receive growth hormone depends strictly on whether epiphyses are open or fused.

A.fit: Not here: establishes etiology, but open epiphyses determine GH eligibility

B.clue: Epigenetic testing for growth restriction syndrome
B.fit: Not here: does not determine physiologic capacity for linear bone growth

C.clue: Provocative clonidine or arginine GH release test
C.fit: Not here: tests GH deficiency, but fusion of epiphyses precludes therapy

D.fit: Not here: evaluates ovarian failure, not epiphyseal responsiveness
D.tempting: evaluates absent menarche and pubic hair

F.clue: Radiographic bone age assessing growth plate patency
F.fit: Here: below 3rd percentile for height, no menarche at 15

algorithm.title: Evaluation of severe short stature and delayed puberty

nodes.text: Severe short stature (< 3rd percentile) + delayed puberty at 15: obtain bone age radiograph of hand
Assess epiphyseal growth plates: open epiphyses are mandatory for growth hormone responsiveness
**Epiphyses completely fused:** growth hormone therapy cannot promote linear growth; do not initiate
**Epiphyses open:** obtain karyotype (rule out Turner syndrome 45,XO) + check IGF-1
**Turner syndrome or GH deficiency present:** initiate recombinant human growth hormone therapy
Introduce low-dose estrogen therapy at bone age 12 to induce breast development

1064829.boardCall: Truncal obesity (BMI 37) + hypertension (165/100) + fasting hyperglycemia (130 mg/dL) -> metabolic syndrome
1064829.hinge: The constellation of truncal obesity, elevated blood pressure (>= 130/85), and elevated fasting glucose (>= 100 mg/dL) fulfills criteria for metabolic syndrome.
1064829.trap: Facial hair and truncal obesity can mimic Cushing syndrome from an adrenal/pituitary adenoma, but metabolic syndrome is the common unifying diagnosis.

A.clue: Autonomous adrenal cortisol or androgen hypersecretion
A.fit: Not here: no violaceous striae, easy bruising, or proximal muscle weakness
A.tempting: facial hair and truncal obesity mimic Cushing

B.clue: Clustering of abdominal obesity, hypertension, and dysglycemia
B.fit: Here: BMI is 37 kg/m², blood pressure 165/100, glucose 130

C.fit: Not here: classic features of metabolic syndrome without hypercortisolism signs

D.clue: Neuroendocrine tumor with ectopic ACTH secretion
D.fit: Not here: no cachexia, rapid muscle wasting, or severe hypokalemia

E.clue: Severe chronic hyperglycemia with microvascular damage
E.fit: Not here: single fasting glucose 130 requires confirmation; part of metabolic syndrome

algorithm.title: Metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria and management

nodes.text: Patient with central obesity: screen for metabolic syndrome criteria (requires >= 3 of 5 components)
Components: waist > 88 cm (women), BP >= 130/85, fasting glucose >= 100, TG >= 150, HDL < 50
Confirm diagnosis: patient exhibits obesity, hypertension, and fasting hyperglycemia
Prescribe comprehensive lifestyle modification: weight loss + 150 minutes weekly aerobic exercise
**Persistent hypertension >= 130/80:** initiate antihypertensive therapy with ACE inhibitor or ARB
**Persistent fasting hyperglycemia >= 126 mg/dL:** initiate metformin therapy

abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.scope: screening recommendations (men 65-75 who smoked), ultrasound imaging, surveillance intervals, elective repair thresholds, rupture
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.core: Older adult with abdominal aortic dilation may remain asymptomatic until expansion or rupture; sudden abdominal/back pain and hypotension require immediate vascular rescue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking strongest modifiable risk; older age, male sex, family history, hypertension, atherosclerosis
Women have higher rupture risk at smaller diameters; most aneurysms infrarenal
Existing AAA: **diameter and high BP** predict rupture; cholesterol, A1c do not

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental pulsatile expansile abdominal mass; localized persistent pain suggests symptomatic aneurysm
Rupture triad incompletely present; transient stability may reflect contained retroperitoneal hemorrhage
Blue toe/distal ischemia may result from mural thrombus embolization
Acute back pain unchanged by movement = **referred pain**; prevertebral calcification on x-ray; not disc disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medial elastin/collagen degradation → progressive enlargement; greater wall radius increases tension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Abdominal ultrasound** diagnoses AAA, generally diameter ≥3 cm; no contrast required
★ Stable suspected rupture or preoperative planning → **CT angiography**
Unstable suspected rupture → bedside ultrasound if immediate; no CT transport delaying surgery
Ultrasound detects aneurysm but cannot reliably exclude rupture; follow symptoms/hemodynamics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Rupture → **urgent vascular repair**, IV access, blood products; avoid delaying for complete workup
Permissive hypotension during transfer/resuscitation until hemorrhage control when clinically feasible
★ Elective repair: **≥5.5 cm men, ≥5.0 cm women**, symptoms; **not if short life expectancy** (metastatic cancer)
Rapid growth ≥0.5 cm/6 months → repair consideration; endovascular versus open based on anatomy/fitness
Smaller asymptomatic lesions → ultrasound surveillance below; refer vascular surgery, manage cardiovascular risks

rows.label: Complications
items: Rupture, thrombosis, distal embolization; repair → AKI, bowel ischemia, endoleak after EVAR
Aortoenteric fistula after prior graft: herald GI bleed → catastrophic hemorrhage; urgent evaluation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **one-time ultrasound men 65–75 who ever smoked**; selectively screen never-smoking men
Women never smoked/no family history → no screening; women smokers/family history → USPSTF evidence insufficient
Smoking cessation, BP control, statin for atherosclerotic disease; lifelong imaging follow-up after EVAR

rows.label: Mimics
items: Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; shock atypical
Aortic dissection: abrupt chest/back pain, possible pulse deficits or branch ischemia

abdominal-trauma.name: Abdominal trauma
abdominal-trauma.scope: Blunt abdominal trauma (splenic/hepatic laceration, FAST exam, CT scan), penetrating abdominal trauma (stab, gunshot, peritonitis, exploratory laparotomy indications)
abdominal-trauma.core: Abdominal injury after collision, fall, stabbing, or gunshot: hemodynamic status and peritoneal signs determine imaging versus immediate operation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, seat-belt compression, lower rib fractures; anticoagulation increases bleeding risk
Stab wounds may spare viscera; bullets frequently injure multiple structures

rows.label: Clues
items: LUQ pain or referred left shoulder pain → splenic injury; RUQ tenderness → hepatic injury
Distention, ecchymoses, abdominal wall marks; initially benign examination does not exclude bowel injury
★ **Rigidity, rebound, persistent hypotension**, or evisceration → urgent operative assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Solid-organ disruption → intraperitoneal hemorrhage; mesenteric injury → ischemia or delayed perforation
Retroperitoneal injury may produce little intraperitoneal free fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **FAST** at bedside during resuscitation; detects free fluid, not organ-specific injury
★ Stable → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**; evaluate solid organs, bowel, retroperitoneum
Negative FAST with ongoing shock → search thorax/pelvis, repeat assessment; do not assume safety
Stable anterior stab → local wound exploration or serial examination/CT; trajectory guides evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, large-bore IV access, warmed blood products; massive transfusion for hemorrhagic shock
★ Unstable + positive FAST, peritonitis, or ongoing transfusion need → **exploratory laparotomy**; no CT delay
Stable splenic/hepatic injury → monitored nonoperative care; blush, transient response → angioembolization (older questions: laparotomy)
Enteric contents, uncontrolled bleeding → operation; transperitoneal gunshot → **laparotomy** even if stable; selected stabs observed
Suspected bowel perforation → ceftriaxone + metronidazole, trauma surgery; free subdiaphragmatic air → **laparotomy**, no CT

rows.label: Complications
items: Delayed splenic rupture, abscess, bile leak, abdominal compartment syndrome
Missed hollow-viscus injury → sepsis; splenectomy → overwhelming encapsulated bacterial infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Restraints, airbags, injury-prevention counseling
★ After splenectomy → **pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib vaccines**; fever requires urgent antibiotics

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pelvic hemorrhage: unstable pelvis, negative abdominal FAST
Tension pneumothorax: unilateral absent breath sounds, obstructive shock

abdominal-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established trauma assessment and management principles.

acid-base-disorders.name: Acid-base disorders
acid-base-disorders.scope: Metabolic acidosis (anion gap, non-anion gap), metabolic alkalosis (saline-responsive vs saline-resistant), respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, Winter formula, mixed disorders
acid-base-disorders.core: Identify the primary pH disturbance, test expected compensation, then investigate the anion gap or urine chloride to locate the cause.

rows.label: Definition
items: Acidemia: pH <7.35; alkalemia: >7.45; normal pH can hide opposing primary disorders
Metabolic: primary HCO3 change; respiratory: primary PaCO2 change

rows.label: Formula
items: ★ **AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3)**; usual normal ≈8–12, laboratory dependent
Hypoalbuminemia correction: add 2.5 to AG per 1 g/dL albumin below 4
★ **Winter: expected PaCO2 = 1.5 × HCO3 + 8 ±2**

rows.label: Interpret
items: HCO3 12 → expected PaCO2 26 ±2; measured 40 → additional respiratory acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis: expected PaCO2 ≈40 + 0.7 × (HCO3 − 24), ±5
Respiratory HCO3 change per 10 PaCO2: acidosis +1 acute/+4 chronic; alkalosis −2 acute/−4 chronic

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Alkalosis: **urine Cl <20 mmol/L** → saline-responsive; ≥20 → diuretics/mineralocorticoids
ΔAG exceeds HCO3 fall → additional alkalosis; smaller ΔAG → additional non-gap acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Compensation never overshoots; values outside expected range imply **mixed disorder**
Salicylates often cause respiratory alkalosis plus high-gap acidosis; near-normal pH is deceptive
Diarrhea/RTA: non-gap acidosis; distal RTA: urine pH >5.5, hypokalemia; renal failure: either gap pattern

acid-base-disorders.evidence: Established physiologic formulas; no guideline involved.

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

acute-leukemias.name: Acute leukemias
acute-leukemias.scope: Acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, bone marrow biopsy, Auer rods
acute-leukemias.core: Rapid marrow replacement produces cytopenias and circulating immature cells; acute promyelocytic leukemia with coagulopathy demands immediate treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior cytotoxic treatment/radiation, benzene, myelodysplasia → AML
Down syndrome increases childhood leukemia risk; ALL predominates in children

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, fever/infections, bruising, bone pain; WBC may be high, normal or low
Hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy; T-ALL → mediastinal mass and airway/SVC compression
★ Bleeding with prolonged PT, low fibrinogen → suspect **APL-associated DIC**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clonal immature myeloid or lymphoid expansion displaces normal hematopoiesis
Blast differentiation arrest; cell turnover predisposes to urate/phosphate release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/differential and smear → bone marrow biopsy**, flow cytometry, cytogenetics
Usually ≥20% marrow/blood blasts; defining genetic abnormalities permit some AML diagnoses below threshold
BMP, uric acid, LDH, coagulation profile; lumbar puncture for ALL CNS evaluation after stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected APL → **ATRA immediately**, then arsenic trioxide-based regimen; correct coagulopathy aggressively
Febrile neutropenia → IV cefepime; symptomatic cytopenias → blood-product support
AML → cytarabine/daunorubicin; less-fit adults → azacitidine/venetoclax; selected patients → allogeneic transplant
ALL → vincristine/steroid/asparaginase-based chemotherapy + intrathecal methotrexate; BCR-ABL-positive → add imatinib
★ Tumor-lysis prevention → hydration/allopurinol; high risk → **rasburicase**, contraindicated with G6PD deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Leukostasis: respiratory distress/confusion → urgent cytoreduction; tumor lysis → AKI, arrhythmias
Treatment → opportunistic infection, infertility, cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukemoid reaction: mature neutrophilia with toxic granulation, reactive trigger
Aplastic anemia: hypocellular marrow without blast expansion

acute-leukemias.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

acute-otitis-media.name: Acute otitis media
acute-otitis-media.scope: Bulging erythematous tympanic membrane, impaired mobility, oral amoxicillin first-line, amoxicillin-clavulanate, tympanostomy indications
acute-otitis-media.core: Acute otalgia with middle-ear effusion and a bulging tympanic membrane identifies acute otitis media; age, laterality, and severity guide antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young age, daycare, viral URI, tobacco smoke exposure, absent breastfeeding
Craniofacial abnormalities and eustachian tube dysfunction increase recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: Ear tugging, fever, irritability, poor feeding; spontaneous perforation causes new otorrhea
★ **Postauricular swelling/tenderness, protruding pinna** → mastoiditis
Erythematous membrane alone, especially during crying, insufficient for diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: URI-related eustachian edema traps fluid; pneumococcus, nontypeable H influenzae, Moraxella commonly infect middle ear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pneumatic otoscopy**: reduced mobility supports effusion; moderate/severe bulging or nonexternal otorrhea diagnostic
Mild bulging requires recent otalgia or intense erythema; no effusion → no AOM diagnosis
Tympanometry if effusion uncertain; no routine imaging/cultures; suspected mastoiditis → **contrast CT temporal bones/head**
Failure after 48–72 h → repeat examination; persistent effusion alone does not mean antibiotic failure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Acetaminophen or ibuprofen** for pain regardless of antibiotic decision
★ When treating → **amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day**; 10 days if <2 years or severe
Recent amoxicillin within 30 days, purulent conjunctivitis, or amoxicillin failure → amoxicillin-clavulanate
Selected older nonsevere cases → 5–7 days; severe illness/complication or oral intolerance changes regimen
★ Recurrent AOM **≥3/6 months or ≥4/12 months** → tube evaluation; effusion required at candidacy assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Conductive hearing loss, membrane perforation, mastoiditis, rare intracranial infection
Effusion ≥3 months → hearing assessment; tubes considered for bilateral persistent fluid with hearing difficulty

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pneumococcal/influenza vaccination, breastfeeding, smoke avoidance; no routine prophylactic antibiotics
Observe speech/hearing development in recurrent disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Otitis media with effusion: fluid, retracted gray membrane, no acute inflammation → **observe, no antibiotics**
Otitis externa: canal inflammation, pain with tragus/pinna movement
Referred dental/TMJ pain: normal middle-ear examination

adjustment-disorder.name: Adjustment disorder
adjustment-disorder.scope: Identifiable psychosocial stressor within 3 months, marked distress or functional impairment, resolution within 6 months, psychotherapy
adjustment-disorder.core: Disproportionate distress or functional impairment beginning within 3 months of an identifiable stressor, without meeting criteria for another disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Relationship loss, illness, job loss, relocation, school difficulty; limited social support or coping resources
Prior psychiatric illness, ongoing adversity, cumulative stress; assess cultural context and expected responses

rows.label: Clues
items: Anxiety, depressed mood, mixed emotions, or conduct disturbance linked temporally to the event
★ Symptoms resolve within **6 months after stressor/consequences end**; may persist with ongoing stress
Sleep difficulty, worry, withdrawal, reduced performance; impairment exceeds an expected adaptive response

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress-related maladaptive coping and emotional dysregulation; no required traumatic exposure or unique biomarker

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical chronology** plus functional assessment; clarify symptoms before and after the stressor
★ Screen **suicidality**, substance use, mania, psychosis; investigate medical causes suggested by history
Full major-depressive syndrome takes precedence even when triggered by a clear life event
Reassess persistence, escalating severity, or loss of temporal connection; diagnosis may change over time

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Brief psychotherapy**, problem solving, CBT, coping skills; strengthen support and reduce modifiable stress
Address sleep routines, daily structure, school/work accommodations and practical resources
Medication usually unnecessary; severe acute anxiety/insomnia → brief **benzodiazepine** (older exams); SSRIs take weeks
Suicidal intent, inability to maintain safety, or severe deterioration → urgent psychiatric assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Self-harm, suicide risk, substance misuse, occupational or academic decline
Persistent symptoms may evolve into major depression, anxiety disorder, or another defined condition

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early transition support, coping skills, follow-up until recovery; involve trusted supports with consent

rows.label: Mimics
items: Major depression: ≥2 weeks, ≥5 symptoms including depressed mood/anhedonia
PTSD/acute stress disorder: qualifying trauma plus intrusion/avoidance; PTSD >1 month, acute stress 3 days–1 month
Normal grief: fluctuating loss-focused sadness with preserved self-worth and adaptive function
GAD: ≥6 months of multi-domain worry, not tied to one recent stressor

adjustment-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR teaching.

adrenal-insufficiency.name: Adrenal insufficiency
adrenal-insufficiency.scope: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease), secondary adrenal insufficiency, cosyntropin stimulation test, morning serum cortisol, hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement, adrenal crisis
adrenal-insufficiency.core: Weight loss, fatigue, orthostasis, and hyponatremia, or unexplained pressor-resistant shock after illness or interruption of glucocorticoids.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: autoimmune destruction, TB, bilateral hemorrhage, metastases; associated autoimmune thyroid disease
★ Secondary: **prolonged glucocorticoids**, pituitary disease/surgery/apoplexy; abrupt withdrawal risks crisis
Crisis triggers: infection, trauma, surgery, missed replacement, vomiting

rows.label: Clues
items: Anorexia, abdominal pain, nausea, weakness; hypoglycemia, eosinophilia
Crisis: fever, confusion, severe volume depletion; symptoms may worsen rapidly during intercurrent illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortisol deficiency reduces vascular catecholamine response and increases ADH
Primary gland failure removes mineralocorticoids; secondary disease retains renin–angiotensin-driven aldosterone

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **8 AM cortisol + ACTH**; very low cortisol supports, clearly high values argue against insufficiency
★ Equivocal basal cortisol → **cosyntropin (ACTH) stimulation**; inadequate assay-specific peak confirms impaired reserve
Traditional stimulated cutoff ≈18 µg/dL; newer assays may use ≈14–15; interpret laboratory standard
Primary → 21-hydroxylase antibodies, selected adrenal CT; secondary → pituitary evaluation/MRI
Recent pituitary injury may initially show normal cosyntropin response; clinical suspicion still matters

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → draw blood if feasible, **IV hydrocortisone + isotonic saline**, dextrose for hypoglycemia
Do not wait for confirmatory results; treat precipitant and correct electrolytes carefully
Coexisting hypothyroidism → glucocorticoid replacement before levothyroxine to avoid decompensation

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → arrhythmia, circulatory collapse, death; chronic undertreatment → impaired function
Excess replacement → osteoporosis, diabetes, Cushingoid features

rows.label: Prevention
items: Stress-dose plan, emergency injectable hydrocortisone, medical alert ID; taper prolonged systemic steroids
Vomiting prevents absorption → parenteral replacement and urgent evaluation; teach sick-day plans to caregivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: SIADH: euvolemia, normal potassium and cortisol reserve
Sepsis: infection may coexist and trigger crisis
Hypothyroidism: bradycardia, cold intolerance, weight gain

table.title: Primary versus secondary
rows: Low/inappropriately normal ACTH; potassium usually normal

adrenal-insufficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching; cortisol cutoffs are assay dependent.

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

advance-directives-and-surrogates.name: Advance directives and surrogate decisions
advance-directives-and-surrogates.scope: Living will, DNR/DNI orders, health care proxy, substituted judgment, best interests, advance care planning
advance-directives-and-surrogates.core: Follow the capable patient's current wishes; when capacity is absent, use valid directives and authorized surrogate judgment.

rows.label: Principle
items: Autonomy persists after incapacity through documented preferences and legally authorized decision-makers
Substituted judgment: patient's known values; best interests: benefits/burdens when preferences unknown

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Confirm capacity, directive validity, clinical applicability, and designated **health care proxy**
★ Apply the patient's instructions over conflicting surrogate preferences
Discuss goals, code status, surrogate early; terminal sole caregiver → plan **child guardianship**

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ **DNR limits CPR**; do not automatically withhold antibiotics, analgesia, nutrition, or other treatment
Dementia diagnosis, mild test errors, or disagreement ≠ incapacity; capacity is decision-specific
★ **Surrogate cannot compel contraindicated treatment** → withhold it; ethics consult unnecessary

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Capable patient may revise prior instructions; current informed choices control
No directive/proxy → adult next of kin; none eligible (minor relative) → **court guardian**
Clear directive/reported wishes/proxy–team agreement → no consult; unresolved conflict → ethics, court

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **DNI and DNR differ**; clarify acceptable ventilation and perioperative plans
Proxy needs no terminal illness; dementia tube-feeding request → review lack of benefit, harms
Surrogate conveys patient's known wishes, not own beliefs; missing paperwork doesn't block them

table.title: Documents and authority
rows: Durable health care power of attorney
Current medical order limiting specified intervention
Portable treatment orders for serious illness

advance-directives-and-surrogates.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics framework; document validity and surrogate hierarchy depend on jurisdiction.

airway-management.name: Airway management
airway-management.scope: Indications for endotracheal intubation (GCS <= 8, airway protection, respiratory failure), rapid sequence intubation, bag-valve-mask ventilation, difficult airway
airway-management.core: Secure the airway when oxygenation, ventilation, or protection fails; preparation and rescue oxygenation determine safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Facial/neck trauma, burns, angioedema, obesity, limited jaw opening or cervical mobility
Shock, severe hypoxemia, metabolic acidosis increase peri-intubation collapse risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **GCS ≤8**, absent protective reflexes, recurrent aspiration, apnea → assess need for definitive airway
Stridor, fatigue, rising CO₂, refractory hypoxemia, inability to handle secretions → impending failure
GCS alone imperfect: reversible intoxication without ventilation/protection failure may permit closely monitored observation
Toxic sore throat, drooling, stridor → epiglottitis: laryngoscopy + intubation in OR before imaging/cultures

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Upper-airway obstruction, depressed drive, or respiratory muscle failure prevents effective gas exchange
Induction/positive pressure reduces sympathetic tone and venous return, worsening hypotension

rows.label: Dx
items: Continuous pulse oximetry, ECG, BP; assess mouth opening, neck anatomy, aspiration risk
★ Confirm tracheal placement with **persistent waveform capnography**, then auscultation and chest radiograph for depth
Do not rely on chest movement, oxygen saturation, or auscultation alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Position, suction, **preoxygenate**; prepare BVM, supraglottic device, video laryngoscope, and surgical rescue
Two-person BVM with airway adjunct and oxygen; oral adjunct only without gag reflex
RSI: etomidate/ketamine + rocuronium/succinylcholine; provide immediate postintubation analgesia and sedation
★ Predicted difficult airway → awake intubation strategy; **cannot intubate/cannot oxygenate or shattered midface/mandible → cricothyrotomy**
Avoid succinylcholine: hyperkalemia, denervation, established major burns, neuromuscular disease, malignant hyperthermia risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Esophageal intubation, aspiration, dental injury, hypoxemia, cardiac arrest
Positive-pressure ventilation → barotrauma; prolonged ventilation → pneumonia, laryngeal injury
Right-mainstem tube → occludes right upper lobe bronchus → **alveolar collapse** (atelectasis), not air trapping
Prolonged intubation → **tracheomalacia**: dynamic expiratory collapse, localized wheeze, exertional dyspnea; not asthma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize **hemodynamics before induction**, use attempt limits and explicit backup plan
Head-of-bed elevation, oral care, daily sedation/ventilator liberation assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic hyperventilation: preserved oxygenation/protection, respiratory alkalosis
Compensatory Kussmaul breathing: metabolic acidosis; losing minute ventilation can cause abrupt deterioration

airway-management.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency airway principles.

allergic-rhinitis.name: Allergic rhinitis
allergic-rhinitis.scope: Seasonal and perennial rhinitis, bluish boggy turbinates, allergic shiners, intranasal glucocorticoids, oral antihistamines, allergen avoidance
allergic-rhinitis.core: Recurrent sneezing, nasal itching, and clear rhinorrhea after allergen exposure, often accompanied by itchy watery eyes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atopy, asthma, eczema, family history; occupational allergen exposure
Seasonal: tree, grass, weed pollens; perennial: dust mites, pets, indoor molds

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pale bluish boggy turbinates**, allergic shiners, transverse nasal crease
Congestion, postnasal drip, mouth breathing; symptoms impair sleep, school, or work
Fever, purulent unilateral drainage, epistaxis, or focal pain warrants another explanation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links mast-cell IgE → histamine release; late eosinophilic inflammation sustains obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis** from reproducible exposure pattern and examination
Uncertain diagnosis, persistent symptoms, or immunotherapy planning → skin-prick or serum allergen-specific IgE testing
Positive sensitization test requires matching exposure history; total IgE and imaging are not routine
Unilateral obstruction → inspect for foreign body, structural lesion, or mass

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent or congestion-dominant disease → **intranasal fluticasone**; direct spray away from septum
Mild intermittent disease → cetirizine or loratadine; intranasal azelastine offers rapid relief
Incomplete control → intranasal steroid + intranasal antihistamine; saline irrigation as adjunct
★ Refractory, confirmed sensitization → **allergen immunotherapy** with allergy specialist
Avoid sedating first-generation antihistamines in older adults; decongestant sprays >3 days → rebound congestion

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, reduced concentration, eustachian tube dysfunction, recurrent sinus symptoms
Intranasal steroid misuse → epistaxis; systemic decongestants → hypertension, tachycardia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Allergen reduction**: mattress encasements, hot-wash bedding, moisture control, exposure-directed pet avoidance
Close windows during high pollen periods; avoid tobacco smoke and personal irritants

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral URI: short course, malaise, possible fever
Nonallergic rhinitis: odor/temperature triggers, little itching, negative sensitization testing
Rhinitis medicamentosa: chronic topical vasoconstrictor use with rebound blockage

allergic-rhinitis.evidence: Not checked online; established rhinitis diagnostic and treatment principles.

alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.scope: SERPINA1 gene mutation (PiZZ phenotype), panacinar basilar emphysema in young nonsmokers, liver cirrhosis/hepatoma, PAS-positive diastase-resistant globules, serum AAT level and phenotype
alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.core: Premature obstructive lung disease with unexplained liver disease or a family history suggests inherited alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal codominant **SERPINA1** variants; PiZZ phenotype causes severe deficiency
Smoking, secondhand smoke, occupational dust and fumes accelerate pulmonary injury

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Young nonsmoker with **basilar panacinar emphysema**, exertional dyspnea, and persistent airflow obstruction
Neonatal cholestasis or adult hepatic dysfunction; liver and lung disease may occur independently
Hyperinflation, diminished breath sounds; advanced disease → hypoxemia and right-heart strain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deficient circulating antiprotease → unopposed neutrophil elastase and alveolar wall destruction
Misfolded protein retained in hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum → cellular injury, fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serum AAT level** → phenotype or genotype confirmation; acute inflammation can falsely elevate levels
Test all adults with COPD, unexplained bronchiectasis, or unexplained chronic liver disease
Spirometry establishes obstruction; chest CT defines distribution; LFTs and ultrasound assess hepatic injury
★ Liver biopsy, if obtained: **PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules**; not required for routine diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Smoking cessation** plus inhaled bronchodilators; pulmonary rehabilitation and oxygen for qualifying chronic hypoxemia
IV AAT augmentation for selected nonsmokers with severe deficiency and established emphysema; specialist selection
Augmentation does not treat liver injury; decompensated cirrhosis → liver transplantation
End-stage pulmonary disease despite treatment → lung transplantation evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension, recurrent respiratory infections
Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma; hepatic cancer surveillance once cirrhosis develops

rows.label: Prevention
items: Offer genetic counseling and testing to first-degree relatives; genotype rather than level alone
Influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal vaccines; hepatitis A/B vaccination with liver disease
Avoid excess alcohol and hepatotoxic exposures; monitor pulmonary function and liver tests

rows.label: Mimics
items: Smoking-related emphysema: predominantly upper-lobe centriacinar destruction
Cystic fibrosis: bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, elevated sweat chloride
Other cirrhosis: viral, alcohol, metabolic causes without the characteristic inherited pulmonary pattern

alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established AAT deficiency diagnosis and management.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.scope: Upper and lower motor neuron signs, bulbar symptoms, preserved sensation, EMG/NCS findings, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, riluzole, edaravone, end-of-life planning
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.core: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs in multiple regions, usually with preserved sensation and sphincter function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle/older adulthood, male sex; mostly sporadic, minority familial
Family history of motor neuron disease or frontotemporal dementia supports inherited susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Atrophy, fasciculations + hyperreflexia/spasticity** within affected regions; asymmetric limb onset common
Bulbar disease: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue wasting; pseudobulbar affect may accompany corticobulbar dysfunction
Orthopnea, morning headache, weak cough → ventilatory weakness; inward abdominal motion on inspiration → **diaphragmatic paralysis**
Ocular movement and sensation usually spared; some patients develop executive or behavioral impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Degeneration of corticospinal neurons and anterior horn/bulbar motor neurons; denervation spreads progressively

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical progression + EMG/NCS**: widespread **fibrillation potentials**, sharp waves, chronic denervation; sensory conduction normal
MRI brain/spine to exclude structural mimics; targeted B12, thyroid, CK, and other studies
Assess FVC, inspiratory strength, nocturnal gas exchange, swallow function, nutrition; no single definitive blood test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Riluzole** modestly prolongs survival; edaravone may slow functional decline in selected patients
★ **Noninvasive ventilation** for symptomatic respiratory weakness improves comfort and survival
Swallow/nutrition support; discuss gastrostomy before severe respiratory decline; cough-assist and secretion management
Baclofen for spasticity, communication devices, physical/occupational support; multidisciplinary specialty care
Early shared planning for ventilation, feeding, advance directives, hospice; discuss choices before communication declines

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure is usual terminal event; aspiration, malnutrition, falls, immobility
Depression, caregiver burden; frontotemporal impairment may affect decision-making capacity

rows.label: Prevention
items: No primary prevention; aspiration/fall precautions, vaccination, nutritional support, respiratory surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical myelopathy: sensory level, sphincter changes, compressive MRI lesion
Myasthenia gravis: fatigable ocular weakness, no UMN signs
Multifocal motor neuropathy: conduction block, IVIG response

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.evidence: Not checked online; established ALS diagnosis and supportive-treatment teaching.

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated
Epinephrine: α1 reverses vasodilation/edema, β2 reverses bronchoconstriction; albuterol alone misses edema and shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Profound shock or refractory hypotension → titrated IV epinephrine plus **isotonic boluses**; beta-blocker use → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Undiluted IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

anorectal-disorders.name: Anorectal disorders
anorectal-disorders.scope: Anal fissure, internal and external hemorrhoids, anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, pruritus ani, topical vasodilators, fiber, sitz baths
anorectal-disorders.core: Anal pain, bleeding, swelling, or drainage requires inspection and focused examination; pain pattern distinguishes fissure, thrombosis, and infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constipation, straining, pregnancy, prolonged sitting; Crohn disease, diabetes, immunosuppression increase infection risk
Irritant soaps, moisture, fecal seepage contribute to pruritus ani

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion, fever, spreading erythema, crepitus** → evaluate necrotizing perineal infection urgently
Posterior midline fissure common; lateral/multiple fissures suggest Crohn disease, infection, or malignancy
Internal hemorrhoids lie above dentate line; prolapse may require manual reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fissure causes internal sphincter spasm and local ischemia; hemorrhoids represent enlarged vascular cushions
Cryptoglandular infection creates abscess; persistent epithelialized tract can become a fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspection first**, gentle DRE/anoscopy when tolerable; do not force painful fissure examination
Deep pain without visible lesion → CT/MRI for occult abscess; recurrent fistula → pelvic MRI
Rectal bleeding with anemia, weight loss, bowel change, or screening indication → colon evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fiber, fluids, stool softening, **sitz baths**; fissure → topical anesthetic, nitroglycerin or diltiazem
Refractory chronic fissure → botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy after continence-risk assessment
Internal hemorrhoids persisting despite conservative measures → rubber-band ligation; advanced prolapse → surgery
★ Abscess → **incision and drainage**; antibiotics added for cellulitis, systemic illness, or immunosuppression
Fistula → colorectal surgery; painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid within 72 hours → consider excision

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess recurrence, fistula, sepsis; sphincter injury → fecal incontinence
Chronic bleeding → iron deficiency; pruritus → excoriations and secondary infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid straining and prolonged toilet sitting; gentle cleansing, dry skin, barrier ointment for seepage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anal cancer: persistent irregular ulcer/mass or large wart-like lesion, biopsy required
Proctitis: urgency, tenesmus, mucous discharge
Pinworm: nocturnal itch, especially children; tape test

table.title: Local patterns
rows: Tearing defecation pain; bright blood on paper
Recurrent purulent drainage from external opening

anorectal-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established colorectal teaching.

antidepressants.name: Antidepressants
antidepressants.scope: SSRIs, SNRIs, bupropion, mirtazapine, tricyclic antidepressants (anticholinergic toxicity, urinary retention, arrhythmia), MAO inhibitors, adverse effects (serotonin syndrome)
antidepressants.core: SSRIs usually start depression treatment; choose alternatives by accompanying symptoms, adverse effects, and overdose risk.

rows.label: Use
items: SSRIs/SNRIs: depression, anxiety; duloxetine also neuropathic pain
Bupropion: smoking cessation; mirtazapine: poor appetite with insomnia
TCAs/MAOIs: resistant depression; TCAs also neuropathic pain

rows.label: Mechanism
items: SSRIs: serotonin reuptake blockade; SNRIs/TCAs: serotonin + norepinephrine reuptake blockade
Bupropion: norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake blockade; mirtazapine: α2 antagonism
MAOIs: reduced monoamine degradation

rows.label: Adverse
items: SSRIs: GI upset, SIADH, bleeding; SNRIs: ↑BP; mirtazapine: sedation/weight gain; bupropion: activating
★ SSRI **sexual dysfunction** → **lower dose** first; other SSRIs rarely help; bupropion minimal
TCAs: constipation, urinary retention, conduction toxicity; MAOIs: orthostatic hypotension

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ Bupropion lowers seizure threshold: **seizure or eating disorders**; CYP inhibitors raise levels
TCAs: urinary retention, glaucoma, conduction disease; anticholinergic delirium in older adults
TCA therapy with QTc/QRS prolongation → **stop TCA**, no waiting for levels

rows.label: Interactions
items: MAOI + tyramine/sympathomimetics → hypertensive crisis → **phentolamine** (α-blocker)
MAOI + SSRI/tramadol → serotonin syndrome; washout generally 14 days, after fluoxetine 5 weeks
Fluoxetine/paroxetine inhibit CYP2D6 → ↑TCA levels, toxicity

rows.label: Monitor
items: Mood, suicidality early in young adults; monitor adherence and functioning
Abrupt stop → **discontinuation**: flu-like aches, headache, dizziness, electric paresthesias, nausea, tremor
Response over 4–6 weeks; taper to stop, especially paroxetine and venlafaxine

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Serotonin syndrome**: clonus, fever/agitation → stop drugs, benzodiazepines; cyproheptadine
★ TCA overdose: Na⁺-channel blockade → **wide QRS**, arrhythmia, seizures → IV sodium bicarbonate
Bipolar depression: antidepressant monotherapy may provoke mania

antidepressants.evidence: Not checked online; established pharmacology and prescribing safety.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

aortic-dissection.name: Aortic dissection
aortic-dissection.core: Sudden maximal chest or back pain with vascular or neurologic deficits suggests aortic dissection, even without widened mediastinum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long-standing hypertension → **medial degeneration** in older adults; bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation
Marfan/vascular Ehlers-Danlos, pregnancy, cocaine, aortic instrumentation or aneurysm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Abrupt severe pain**, pulse/BP asymmetry, syncope, focal neurologic deficit
New aortic regurgitation murmur; limb ischemia or abdominal pain from branch-vessel malperfusion
Hypotension suggests rupture, tamponade, severe regurgitation, or coronary involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear → blood separates medial layers, creating false lumen
Propagation compromises branch arteries or ruptures into pericardium/pleura

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable → **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis**; unstable or unable to leave resuscitation → bedside TEE
Chest radiograph may show widened mediastinum but normal film does not exclude dissection
ECG/troponin may mimic MI; high suspicion requires aortic imaging before antithrombotics
Examine bilateral arm pressures, femoral pulses, neurologic status, renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV esmolol or labetalol** + opioid analgesia; target HR 60–80 and SBP <120 if perfusion maintained
Persistent hypertension after rate control → nicardipine or nitroprusside; avoid vasodilator before beta blockade
★ **Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis** when dissection suspected
Tamponade from dissection → immediate surgical team; routine pericardiocentesis can worsen hemorrhage

rows.label: Complications
items: Aortic rupture, hemothorax, tamponade, MI, stroke, paraplegia, mesenteric/renal ischemia
Late aneurysmal dilation or recurrent dissection despite initial successful treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lifelong **BP control and surveillance CTA/MRA**; beta-blocker-based regimen
Avoid heavy isometric lifting; screen first-degree relatives for familial aortopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute coronary syndrome: pressure-like pain, no pulse deficit; coexistence possible
PE: pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, right-heart strain
Esophageal rupture: vomiting followed by pain and subcutaneous emphysema

aortic-dissection.evidence: Not checked online; established aortic emergency principles.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

atheroembolic-disease.name: Atheroembolic disease
atheroembolic-disease.scope: Cholesterol crystal embolization, vascular procedures, livedo reticularis, blue toe syndrome, acute kidney injury, eosinophilia and hypocomplementemia, supportive management
atheroembolic-disease.core: Delayed kidney injury plus livedo reticularis or painful blue toes after arterial instrumentation suggests cholesterol crystal embolization.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Extensive aortic atherosclerosis, older age, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, peripheral arterial disease
★ Recent **angiography, vascular surgery**, or aortic manipulation; occasionally spontaneous plaque disruption
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis may precipitate embolization but do not establish the diagnosis alone

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Intact distal pulses** despite digital ischemia; multifocal skin findings
Creatinine rises days to weeks after exposure rather than immediately
Eosinophilia, hypocomplementemia, elevated ESR; urinalysis often bland or mildly proteinuric/hematuric
Retinal cholesterol plaques, abdominal pain, GI bleeding, or neurologic deficits indicate additional organs involved

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Plaque rupture releases cholesterol crystals into small arteries and arterioles
Mechanical occlusion plus foreign-body inflammation → progressive downstream tissue injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Characteristic clinical pattern often sufficient; review procedure timing and multisystem signs
Uncertain diagnosis → **skin biopsy** of accessible affected tissue; renal biopsy if needed
Histology: empty needle-shaped cholesterol clefts within occluded vessels; crystals dissolve during processing
Assess renal function, electrolytes, urinalysis; ultrasound excludes coincident obstructive renal injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Supportive care**: manage BP, volume, electrolytes; dialysis for conventional urgent indications
High-intensity statin and vascular risk reduction; antiplatelet treatment for underlying atherosclerotic indications
Avoid further aortic instrumentation when possible; no routine thrombolysis or anticoagulation for crystal emboli
Continue anticoagulation only for compelling separate indications; routine corticosteroids lack established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent kidney dysfunction, dialysis dependence, digital necrosis, bowel ischemia
Extensive systemic embolization → multiorgan failure and death

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, lipid/BP/diabetes control; minimize unnecessary arterial procedures in severe aortic disease
Use less invasive vascular evaluation when sufficient; monitor renal function after high-risk interventions

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contrast-associated AKI: onset within 24–72 hours, usually improves; no systemic embolic skin signs
Acute arterial thromboembolism: abrupt limb ischemia with diminished pulses
Vasculitis: inflammatory vessel injury, often active urine sediment; biopsy lacks cholesterol clefts

atheroembolic-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established cholesterol-embolization teaching.

atrial-fibrillation.name: Atrial fibrillation
atrial-fibrillation.scope: Rate and rhythm control, stroke prevention (CHA2DS2-VASc), unstable AF, embolic complications
atrial-fibrillation.core: Disorganized atrial activation produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm and left atrial appendage thromboembolism risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, hypertension, heart failure, coronary disease, obesity, sleep apnea
Hyperthyroidism, alcohol binges, infection, postoperative stress, mitral valve disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, exercise intolerance, dyspnea; sometimes incidental or first detected after stroke
★ **Hypotension, ischemic chest pain, pulmonary edema, altered mentation** → unstable AF
Very rapid irregular wide-complex rhythm suggests preexcitation; ordinary AV nodal blockers can be dangerous

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary-vein ectopic triggers plus atrial remodeling sustain reentry
Loss of atrial contraction reduces filling; persistent tachycardia can impair LV function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG: absent discrete P waves**, variable RR intervals; document rhythm rather than pulse alone
TSH, electrolytes, renal function; transthoracic echocardiogram for ventricular function and structural disease
Intermittent symptoms → ambulatory rhythm monitoring; assess reversible triggers

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → **synchronized cardioversion**; do not delay for anticoagulation or TEE
Stable rate control: metoprolol or diltiazem; avoid diltiazem/verapamil with reduced EF
Decompensated HF: digoxin or amiodarone; preexcited AF: procainamide or cardioversion, no AV nodal blockers
Rhythm control for symptoms, early disease, or HF: cardioversion, selected antiarrhythmics, catheter ablation
★ Duration ≥48 hours/unknown: **3 weeks anticoagulation or TEE** before elective cardioversion; ≥4 weeks afterward

rows.label: Complications
items: **Top risk factor for cardioembolic stroke**, above age/hypertension; limb/gut emboli; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy
Anticoagulant bleeding; rhythm drugs may cause proarrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Long-term anticoagulation: **CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2 men/≥3 women**; consider one point lower
Apixaban/other DOAC preferred; mechanical valve or moderate/severe rheumatic mitral stenosis → warfarin
Weight reduction, BP/OSA treatment, limit alcohol
Aspirin no substitute for anticoagulation; adding aspirin to warfarin/DOAC → **more bleeding**, no added stroke protection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atrial flutter: sawtooth atrial activity, often regular 2:1 conduction
Multifocal atrial tachycardia: ≥3 P-wave morphologies, isoelectric intervals

atrioventricular-block.name: Atrioventricular block
atrioventricular-block.scope: First-degree, second-degree Mobitz type I (Wenckebach), second-degree Mobitz type II, third-degree (complete) AV block, atropine, pacemaker indications
atrioventricular-block.core: Impaired atrial-to-ventricular conduction ranges from harmless delay to complete dissociation; symptoms and level of block determine urgency and pacing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age-related conduction fibrosis, MI, beta blockers, verapamil/diltiazem, digoxin, hyperkalemia
Lyme carditis, infiltrative disease, myocarditis, cardiac surgery; high vagal tone causes benign nodal delay

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, exertional intolerance, presyncope/syncope; cannon A waves with AV dissociation
★ Hypotension, confusion, ischemic discomfort, acute heart failure → **symptomatic unstable bradycardia**
Wide QRS and slow escape suggest distal disease; narrow escape may still be dangerous

rows.label: Pathophys
items: AV-nodal block often responds to vagal withdrawal; His–Purkinje failure risks unpredictable progression and asystole

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **12-lead ECG** establishes conduction pattern; continuous monitoring for significant block
Review drugs, electrolytes, ischemia; targeted Lyme testing with exposure; echo for structural disease
2:1 block cannot be labeled Mobitz I versus II from ratio alone; assess QRS and localization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → airway/oxygen if needed, IV access, **atropine** while preparing pacing
★ Atropine ineffective or distal high-grade block → **transcutaneous pacing**, then temporary transvenous pacing
Epinephrine/dopamine infusion can bridge to pacing; confirm electrical and mechanical capture
Stop AV-nodal blockers and correct reversible cause; do not wait for atropine in deteriorating infranodal disease
Permanent pacing for acquired Mobitz II, high-grade, or complete block without reversible cause, even asymptomatic

rows.label: Complications
items: Adams–Stokes syncope, low-output failure, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death
Pacemaker implantation → infection, pneumothorax, lead problems; prolonged RV pacing may impair LV function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, ischemia/electrolyte treatment; asymptomatic first-degree or nodal Mobitz I usually observation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blocked premature atrial beat: early hidden P wave, noncompensatory pause
Sinus arrest: absent P waves during pause
AV dissociation from VT: ventricular tachycardia drives rhythm

table.title: ECG distinction
rows: Progressive PR lengthening, then dropped QRS
Constant conducted PR, sudden dropped QRS

attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria across two settings, behavioral rating scales from parents and teachers, behavioral therapy, stimulant pharmacotherapy
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.core: Persistent developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity–impulsivity causing functional impairment across settings, with childhood onset.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, prematurity, prenatal tobacco/alcohol exposure; symptoms may persist into adulthood
Learning disorders, anxiety, oppositional behavior, sleep problems and substance use commonly coexist

rows.label: Clues
items: Inattention: lost items, distraction, disorganization; hyperactivity: fidgeting, leaving seat, excessive talking
Impulsivity: interrupting, difficulty waiting; presentations can be inattentive, hyperactive–impulsive, or combined
Academic difficulty alone insufficient; assess family, peer, driving, and workplace function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Altered dopamine/norepinephrine executive-control signaling; inconsistent performance does not imply deliberate behavior

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥6 symptoms per domain**, or ≥5 if age ≥17; duration ≥6 months
★ Several symptoms **before age 12**, present in ≥2 settings, with impairment; exclude better explanations
Parent and teacher DSM-based rating scales, such as Vanderbilt; interview child and evaluate comorbidities
Check vision/hearing, sleep, learning needs; no routine EEG, neuroimaging, or laboratory diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Ages 4–5: **parent-training behavioral management** first; methylphenidate for persistent moderate/severe impairment
★ Age ≥6: **methylphenidate or amphetamine** plus behavioral/classroom intervention and educational supports
Atomoxetine, extended-release guanfacine/clonidine when stimulants unsuitable, ineffective, or diversion concerning
Before prescribing: personal/family cardiac history, BP/HR, height/weight; ECG only if cardiac concern
Titrate to function and adverse effects; monitor appetite, sleep, growth, BP, misuse; reassess across settings

rows.label: Complications
items: Injury, academic failure, relationship problems; untreated impairment increases later substance-use risk
Stimulants → appetite suppression, insomnia, tachycardia; atomoxetine → suicidality warning, rare liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Routines, sleep, positive reinforcement, school accommodations; secure medication against diversion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Absence seizures: brief stereotyped unresponsiveness with abrupt recovery
Anxiety: attention disrupted by worry
Sleep apnea: snoring, poor sleep, daytime behavioral dysfunction

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-skin-growths.name: Benign skin growths
benign-skin-growths.scope: Seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma, acrochordon, lipoma, epidermoid cyst
benign-skin-growths.core: Slow-growing, stable superficial lesions usually need reassurance; morphology guides recognition, while atypical change requires tissue diagnosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging → keratoses; friction, obesity, insulin resistance → skin tags
Minor trauma may precede dermatofibroma; blocked follicular openings favor epidermoid cysts
Lipomas often sporadic or familial; multiple lesions do not automatically imply malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Most lesions asymptomatic; irritation, snagging, cosmetic concern may prompt consultation
★ **Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding**, fixation, or new irregular pigment → reassess diagnosis
Deep, painful, enlarging soft-tissue mass, especially >5 cm → evaluate for sarcoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Benign keratinocyte, fibrous, adipose, or follicular proliferation; no inherent need for oncologic excision
Ruptured keratin cyst → sterile inflammation; erythema alone does not prove bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical examination**; compare with surrounding skin and prior photographs
