items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

dermatophyte-infections.name: Dermatophyte infections
dermatophyte-infections.scope: Tinea capitis, tinea corporis, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, onychomycosis, potassium hydroxide preparation, oral and topical antifungals
dermatophyte-infections.core: Keratin-invading fungi cause scaly skin lesions or infected hair/nails; the anatomic site determines topical versus systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Warm humid conditions, occlusive footwear, shared showers, wrestling, infected animals or contacts
Diabetes, immunosuppression; childhood favors scalp infection; nail disease increases with age

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus and peripheral scaling; steroid exposure may distort borders and suppress inflammation
★ **Boggy tender scalp plaque** → kerion; inflammatory disease risks permanent scarring alopecia
Interdigital maceration/fissures can become bacterial entry sites

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton digest keratin in stratum corneum, hair, and nails
**T rubrum** most common on skin/nails; capitis → **T tonsurans** (endothrix)
Follicular/deep involvement prevents topical agents from reaching the infected reservoir

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **KOH preparation of active edge** → branching septate hyphae; obtain before systemic treatment when uncertain
Scalp: hair/plucked scale microscopy and culture; nail: clipping KOH, PAS, or fungal culture
Wood lamp detects only selected organisms; negative fluorescence does not exclude tinea
Refractory/widespread infection → reassess diagnosis, adherence, resistance; fungal culture can guide further care

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Limited skin disease → **topical terbinafine** or clotrimazole; continue beyond clinical clearing
★ Hair infection → **oral griseofulvin or terbinafine**; adjunct selenium sulfide/ketoconazole shampoo reduces spread
Nail infection → confirm fungus, then oral terbinafine; baseline liver assessment; counsel slow regrowth
Avoid topical corticosteroid monotherapy or steroid-antifungal combinations; extensive disease may require oral antifungal

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary cellulitis, persistent nail dystrophy, recurrent infection from untreated reservoirs
Oral antifungals: hepatotoxicity, drug interactions; griseofulvin contraindicated during pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Keep feet dry**, change socks, avoid shared towels/combs, disinfect sports gear
Treat symptomatic contacts/pets and coexisting tinea pedis (autoinfects groin → recurrence); avoid barefoot communal-shower exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candida intertrigo: satellite pustules, scrotal involvement
Psoriasis: sharply demarcated plaques, nail pitting; alopecia areata: smooth nonscaly patches

table.title: Site clues
rows: Broken hairs, black dots, patchy alopecia, occipital nodes
Annular plaque, advancing border, central clearing
Thick yellow brittle nail, subungual debris

dermatophyte-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatophyte diagnosis and site-based treatment.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative
False negatives → low sensitivity, an intrinsic test property; NPV varies with prevalence

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in; LR− <0.1 rules out; **LR 1** → no information

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect
ROC point nearest **upper-left corner** → best combined sensitivity and specificity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

diverticular-disease.name: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.scope: Diverticulosis, acute diverticulitis, complicated diverticulitis (abscess, perforation, fistula), CT imaging, antibiotic therapy
diverticular-disease.core: Diverticulosis can bleed without pain; inflamed diverticula cause focal abdominal pain, with CT distinguishing uncomplicated disease from abscess or perforation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, smoking, low physical activity; regular NSAID use
Immunosuppression increases severity and can blunt fever or peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Left lower quadrant tenderness, fever, leukocytosis, altered bowel habits
★ **Pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial UTI** → colovesical fistula
Peritoneal signs, hypotension, persistent vomiting → complicated disease requiring hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosa/submucosa herniate through muscular weak points at penetrating vessels
Diverticular inflammation causes localized microperforation; adjacent vessel erosion causes arterial bleeding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected first/severe episode → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**
Colonic wall thickening and pericolic stranding support inflammation; assess abscess, free air, obstruction
★ **Avoid colonoscopy during acute inflammation**; perforation risk
Colonoscopy after recovery for complicated disease, alarm findings, or overdue cancer screening; usually wait 6–8 weeks

rows.label: Tx
items: Low-risk uncomplicated disease: oral hydration, analgesia, advance diet as symptoms improve; antibiotics selective
★ Frail, immunocompromised, systemically ill, or complicated → **antibiotics** covering gram-negatives/anaerobes
Outpatient: amoxicillin-clavulanate (older exams: ciprofloxacin/metronidazole); severe: ceftriaxone/metronidazole or pip-tazo
Small abscess: antibiotics; larger accessible abscess, often >3 cm → percutaneous drainage
★ Peritonitis, uncontrolled sepsis, obstruction → **urgent surgery**; fistula → elective resection after stabilization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, free perforation, stricture, fistula; recurrence does not automatically require colectomy
Severe diverticular hemorrhage may require colonoscopic hemostasis or angiographic embolization

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fiber-rich diet after recovery, exercise, weight management, smoking cessation
No need to avoid nuts, seeds, popcorn; avoid regular NSAIDs when possible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Colon cancer: progressive symptoms, weight loss, iron deficiency; can coexist
Ischemic colitis: sudden cramping then hematochezia, vascular risk
IBS: recurrent pain without fever or objective inflammation

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation
Familial hypercholesterolemia: **defective LDL-receptor uptake** → isolated high LDL, clear plasma; high TG: milky plasma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history
High total cholesterol alone → full lipid panel before treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD (CAD, stroke, PAD) or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk
Adolescent obesity + moderate LDL → **calorie reduction/lifestyle first**; statin only if severe or persistent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after diet/drug change**, then every 3–12 months; high despite diet → statin
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation
Corpus luteum progesterone sustains pregnancy until ~10 weeks; removal earlier → **progesterone supplementation**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
Stable, unlocated pregnancy, falling hCG → serial hCG until negative; no methotrexate
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG omits routine testing earlier; older exam questions may expect Rh typing

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue
Subchorionic hematoma: bleeding without cramping; viable intrauterine pregnancy, perichorionic collection
Normal early pregnancy: spotting, 5-week sac, hCG ~1,000, simple corpus luteum cyst; embryo not yet expected

eating-disorders.name: Eating disorders
eating-disorders.scope: Anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, refeeding syndrome, medical complications, hospitalization criteria
eating-disorders.core: Disordered intake or compensatory behaviors require assessment of medical instability, suicidality, and malnutrition at any body size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescence, dieting, weight stigma, perfectionism, trauma; psychiatric comorbidity and family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Restrictive disease: cold intolerance, lanugo, bradycardia, orthostasis, menstrual suppression; amenorrhea not required
Purging: parotid hypertrophy, **raised amylase**, enamel erosion, knuckle calluses; hypokalemic hypochloremic alkalosis
★ **Syncope, arrhythmia, hypothermia or severe electrolyte abnormalities** → urgent stabilization

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Starvation suppresses gonadal axis and reduces cardiac mass; vomiting causes chloride/volume depletion
Refeeding insulin surge shifts phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical interview plus weight trajectory, vitals/orthostatics, **ECG, electrolytes, Mg, phosphate**
Binge: loss of control plus unusually large intake; bulimia/BED require episodes ≥weekly for 3 months
Assess suicide risk, substance use, exercise, laxatives; normal BMI does not exclude severe disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Medical admission for instability: e.g., HR <50, BP <90/60, severe electrolyte disturbance or acute food refusal
★ Refeeding → **thiamine**, nutritional rehabilitation, serial phosphate/K/Mg and cardiac monitoring
Adolescent anorexia → family-based treatment; adults → eating-disorder-focused psychotherapy; medication alone insufficient
Bulimia → CBT plus fluoxetine; avoid bupropion because of seizures
BED → CBT; lisdexamfetamine for selected adults, monitor misuse/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → osteoporosis, infertility; cardiac failure, arrhythmic death; purging → arrhythmias, esophageal injury
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, respiratory failure, edema, delirium; high suicide mortality
Severe starvation → **hypoalbuminemia** with pitting edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early recognition of growth/weight-trajectory changes; reduce weight-based stigma; relapse follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: increased appetite with tremor and heat intolerance
GI malabsorption: involuntary weight loss without weight/shape-driven restriction

eating-disorders.evidence: Guideline framework checked 2026-10-30: [APA eating disorders guideline, 2023](https://www.psychiatry.org/psychiatrists/practice/clinical-practice-guidelines/eating-disorders); thresholds: established clinical teaching.

table.title: Diagnostic distinction
rows: Restriction or purging + weight-gain fear/distorted self-image

elder-abuse-and-neglect.name: Elder abuse and neglect
elder-abuse-and-neglect.scope: Physical abuse, psychological abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, clinical red flags, reporting to adult protective services
elder-abuse-and-neglect.core: Unexplained injury, unmet basic needs, intimidation, or loss of financial control warrants private assessment, safety planning, and mandated reporting.

rows.label: Principle
items: Respect autonomy while protecting vulnerable adults; decision-making capacity is specific to the decision
Dependence, cognitive impairment, isolation, caregiver strain, and coercion increase vulnerability
Genital laceration/bleeding in dependent elder → suspect sexual abuse

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview separately**; ask about safety, threats, caregiving, finances, basic needs
★ Stabilize injuries; assess cognition, capacity, suicidality, immediate danger, and safe disposition
★ Document quotes/findings; report suspected abuse to **Adult Protective Services**

rows.label: Don't
items: Do not confront the suspected abuser before arranging safety or disclose confidential plans unnecessarily
Do not require proof, a confession, or patient permission when reporting is legally mandatory
Poverty, accidental bruises, informed treatment refusal alone → insufficient evidence of neglect

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Immediate danger → emergency services; suspected crime may require police reporting
Capacitated adult can usually decline services; mandatory reporting may still apply under state law
Incapacity with unsafe care → protective intervention, surrogate review, possible emergency guardianship

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Inconsistent histories, different injury ages**, delayed care, controlling caregiver → investigate
Malnutrition, pressure injuries, medication deprivation → neglect; forced signatures → exploitation
Psychological abuse may leave no physical marks; arrange social work and confidential follow-up

elder-abuse-and-neglect.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; reporting statutes vary by jurisdiction.

endemic-mycoses.name: Endemic mycoses
endemic-mycoses.scope: Histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis, geographic distribution, itraconazole, amphotericin B
endemic-mycoses.core: Inhaled dimorphic fungi cause pneumonia after geographic exposure; immunosuppression increases dissemination, while morphology distinguishes organisms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Soil disruption, construction, outdoor work; Histoplasma exposure to bird/bat-enriched soil
HIV, TNF inhibitors, transplant; pregnancy particularly increases severe coccidioidomycosis risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Subacute fever, cough, fatigue, weight loss; nodules or adenopathy may resemble TB/malignancy
Histoplasma dissemination → hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, mucosal lesions or adrenal involvement
Blastomyces → verrucous/ulcerative skin lesions, bone disease
Coccidioides → erythema nodosum/arthralgia; dissemination to skin, bone or meninges

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inhaled environmental spores convert to tissue forms; cellular immunity restricts extrapulmonary spread

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Exposure geography + chest imaging** → organism-directed testing
Histoplasma urine/serum antigen particularly useful in disseminated disease; tissue shows intracellular small yeasts
Coccidioides serology with confirmatory testing; tissue spherules contain endospores
Blastomyces broad-based budding yeast on tissue; culture confirms; antigen cross-reacts with Histoplasma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Mild self-limited pulmonary histoplasmosis → **observation** in immunocompetent patients
Persistent/worsening histoplasmosis or nonsevere blastomycosis → itraconazole
★ Severe/disseminated histoplasmosis or blastomycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B**, then itraconazole
Uncomplicated cocci often observation; prolonged/severe illness or high-risk host → fluconazole
★ Coccidioidal meningitis → **lifelong fluconazole**; severe nonmeningeal disease → amphotericin induction

rows.label: Complications
items: Histoplasma → fibrosing mediastinitis; disseminated disease → organ failure
Amphotericin → nephrotoxicity, low K/Mg; azoles → liver injury and drug interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Dust exposure reduction/respiratory protection; selected profoundly immunosuppressed patients → antifungal prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB: acid-fast testing and mycobacterial culture
Sarcoidosis: noninfectious granulomas; exclude fungi before immunosuppression
Sporotrichosis: thorn/soil inoculation in gardeners → hand papule, **ascending lymphocutaneous nodules**; not inhaled

endemic-mycoses.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [IDSA histoplasmosis 2025](https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/histoplasmosis-2025/); other mycoses: established teaching.

endometrial-cancer.name: Endometrial cancer
endometrial-cancer.scope: Endometrial hyperplasia, endometrioid adenocarcinoma, uterine sarcoma (leiomyosarcoma, carcinosarcoma, radiation risk), unopposed estrogen, biopsy, staging
endometrial-cancer.core: Postmenopausal bleeding warrants endometrial evaluation; chronic unopposed estrogen drives hyperplasia and endometrioid carcinoma.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, chronic anovulation/PCOS, nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause, estrogen without progestin
Tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome; prior pelvic radiation increases uterine sarcoma risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Abnormal uterine bleeding, watery/bloody discharge; pelvic pain or enlarged uterus with advanced disease
Growing postmenopausal uterine mass → consider sarcoma; growth rate alone cannot establish malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Postmenopausal adipose aromatase: **androstenedione → estrone**, unopposed estrogen
Atypical hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia: premalignant lesion with frequent concurrent carcinoma
Serous/clear-cell cancers: aggressive, estrogen-independent; carcinosarcoma classified as high-grade carcinoma
Leiomyosarcoma: malignant myometrial smooth muscle, usually de novo rather than transformation of benign leiomyoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AUB at **≥45 years**, or younger with persistent bleeding/estrogen risks → endometrial biopsy
★ ACOG 2026: most postmenopausal bleeding → **TVUS plus tissue sampling**
Classic ≤4 mm reassurance rule changed; persistent bleeding always requires histology, regardless of thickness
Insufficient/negative blind biopsy with continued symptoms → hysteroscopy-directed biopsy; Pap does not exclude disease
Surgical staging assesses myometrial/cervical invasion, nodes, extrauterine spread; sarcoma can escape endometrial sampling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Operable carcinoma → **total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy**, sentinel-node assessment
Advanced/high-risk disease → stage-directed radiation and systemic treatment; carboplatin/paclitaxel commonly used
Suspected sarcoma → intact uterine removal; avoid uncontained morcellation

rows.label: Complications
items: Anemia, metastasis, recurrence; lymph-node surgery → lymphedema

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Weight management; add **progestin to systemic estrogen** when uterus intact; evaluate Lynch families

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginal atrophy: thin friable mucosa; malignancy still needs exclusion
Leiomyoma: usually premenopausal, well-circumscribed smooth-muscle mass

table.title: Hyperplasia
rows: Progestin, often levonorgestrel IUD; repeat sampling
Hysterectomy; selected fertility preservation: progestin + serial biopsies

endometrial-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG bleeding update 2026](https://www.acog.org/news/news-releases/2026/04/acog-publishes-updated-guidance-evaluation-postmenopausal-bleeding), [EIN consensus](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-consensus/articles/2023/09/management-of-endometrial-intraepithelial-neoplasia-or-atypical-endometrial-hyperplasia); other content established teaching.

esophageal-atresia-and-tracheoesophageal.name: Esophageal atresia and tracheoesophageal fistula
esophageal-atresia-and-tracheoesophageal.scope: Esophageal atresia, tracheoesophageal fistula types, VACTERL association, coiled nasogastric tube on chest x-ray
esophageal-atresia-and-tracheoesophageal.core: A newborn with excessive oral secretions, choking and cyanosis during feeds requires evaluation for esophageal atresia or tracheoesophageal fistula.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prenatal polyhydramnios and small/absent stomach bubble suggest impaired fetal swallowing
Associated anomalies: **VACTERL**—vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheoesophageal, renal and limb defects

rows.label: Clues
items: Frothy drooling, feeding-associated respiratory distress, recurrent desaturation or aspiration
★ **Nasogastric/orogastric tube cannot pass** into stomach; avoid repeated forceful attempts
Abdominal distention suggests airway-to-stomach communication; isolated atresia often has gasless abdomen
H-type fistula: esophagus patent, delayed recurrent pneumonia or cough with liquids

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal foregut separation leaves esophageal discontinuity and/or connection to trachea
Secretions pool proximally; distal communication permits reflux aspiration and gastric inflation during ventilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Gentle radiopaque tube placement → **chest/abdominal radiograph showing proximal coiling**
Distal bowel gas supports distal fistula; absent gas favors no distal connection
Routine contrast feeding unnecessary in classic atresia; aspiration can worsen lung injury
Suspected H-type → carefully supervised contrast esophagram and bronchoscopy
Echocardiography before surgery; assess anus, kidneys, spine and limbs for associated anomalies

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, head elevation, continuous proximal pouch suction**, IV fluids and pediatric surgical referral
Secure airway if respiratory failure; minimize bag-mask ventilation because fistula can inflate stomach
★ Definitive → **fistula ligation and esophageal anastomosis** after stabilization
Long-gap atresia → staged nutritional and reconstructive plan; aspiration pneumonia → IV antibiotics
Feeding resumed after postoperative assessment of repair integrity and swallowing safety

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration pneumonia, anastomotic leak/stricture, recurrent fistula, reflux and dysmotility
Associated tracheomalacia can cause persistent noisy breathing, cyanotic spells or recurrent respiratory infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Prenatal recognition enables delivery planning; aspiration precautions until repaired
Long-term monitoring for dysphagia, reflux, growth failure and recurrent respiratory symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Choanal atresia: cyanosis improves with crying; nasal catheter obstructed
Laryngeal cleft: aspiration with patent esophagus
Pyloric stenosis: later nonbilious vomiting without tube coiling

table.title: Anatomic patterns
rows: Most common; proximal pouch + bowel gas

esophageal-atresia-and-tracheoesophageal.evidence: Not checked online; established neonatal surgical teaching.

esophageal-cancer.name: Esophageal cancer
esophageal-cancer.scope: Adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, Barrett esophagus and smoking risks, progressive solid dysphagia, upper endoscopy with biopsy, endoscopic ultrasound staging
esophageal-cancer.core: Progressive dysphagia to solids then liquids with unintentional weight loss.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking increases risk of both histologies; alcohol especially increases squamous cancer risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Odynophagia, retrosternal discomfort, iron deficiency anemia or hoarseness; early lesions often silent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor narrows lumen; submucosal lymphatics facilitate early longitudinal and nodal spread

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Upper endoscopy with biopsy** for progressive dysphagia or alarm features
★ CT and FDG-PET/CT assess distant disease; **endoscopic ultrasound** stages wall depth and regional nodes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Selected superficial mucosal cancers → endoscopic resection; ablate residual Barrett mucosa when present
★ Locally advanced resectable distal adenocarcinoma → perioperative FLOT plus surgery in many patients
Neoadjuvant chemoradiation plus surgery or definitive chemoradiation in selected squamous cancers
Unresectable or metastatic → systemic therapy; stent or radiation for dysphagia palliation

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, malnutrition, bleeding, tracheoesophageal fistula, metastases

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and alcohol reduction; surveillance for established Barrett esophagus

rows.label: Mimics
items: Achalasia: solids and liquids affected from onset; manometry confirms after excluding obstruction
Peptic stricture: long reflux history, gradual solid dysphagia; biopsy excludes malignancy

esophageal-cancer.evidence: Checked NCI Esophageal Cancer Treatment PDQ.

esophageal-motility-disorders.name: Esophageal motility disorders
esophageal-motility-disorders.scope: Achalasia, diffuse esophageal spasm, hypercontractile esophagus, Zenker diverticulum, manometry, barium swallow
esophageal-motility-disorders.core: Dysphagia to solids and liquids from onset suggests impaired motility; progressive solids-first dysphagia suggests mechanical obstruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Achalasia often idiopathic; Chagas disease can destroy enteric ganglia
Older age predisposes to Zenker diverticulum; opioids can produce spastic motility patterns

rows.label: Clues
items: Achalasia: regurgitated undigested food, nocturnal cough, weight loss
★ Zenker: **halitosis, cervical gurgling, aspiration**, retained food hours after eating
Spastic disorders: intermittent dysphagia and squeezing chest pain; hot/cold liquids may provoke

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Achalasia: loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons → impaired LES relaxation and absent peristalsis
Zenker: cricopharyngeal dysfunction → mucosal herniation through Killian triangle

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Esophageal symptoms → **upper endoscopy** to exclude stricture/cancer before motility testing
★ **High-resolution manometry** confirms functional disorder after structural disease excluded
Barium swallow defines emptying; suspected Zenker → **barium study before endoscopy**
Rapid weight loss, older onset or difficult LES passage → evaluate pseudoachalasia with CT/endoscopic ultrasound
Chest pain → exclude ACS before labeling esophageal spasm

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Achalasia → pneumatic dilation, Heller myotomy + fundoplication, or **POEM**
Botulinum toxin for achalasia when procedural risk precludes durable treatment
Spastic disorders → remove opioid trigger, treat reflux; diltiazem or nitrates for persistent symptoms
Symptomatic Zenker → **cricopharyngeal myotomy + diverticulectomy** or endoscopic septotomy; no dilation or blind NG tube

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition; longstanding achalasia → increased squamous cancer risk
Dilation/myotomy → perforation; myotomy, especially POEM → gastroesophageal reflux

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eat slowly, chew thoroughly, remain upright after meals to reduce regurgitation/aspiration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Esophageal cancer: progressive solids-first symptoms; obstructing lesion
Scleroderma: hypotensive LES with reflux, distal aperistalsis

table.title: Manometry and contrast findings
rows: Impaired LES relaxation; absent normal peristalsis

esophageal-motility-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG achalasia guideline](https://gi.org/guideline/diagnosis-and-management-of-achalasia/); other disorders established teaching.

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

fetal-growth-restriction.name: Fetal growth restriction
fetal-growth-restriction.scope: Symmetric vs asymmetric FGR, uteroplacental insufficiency, chromosomal anomalies, congenital infections, umbilical artery Doppler surveillance, oligohydramnios
fetal-growth-restriction.core: Estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile requires evaluation for placental dysfunction and fetal disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal hypertension, preeclampsia, renal/vascular disease, smoking, cocaine, malnutrition, prior affected pregnancy
Aneuploidy, structural anomalies, CMV; multiple gestation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height lag >3 cm, decreased movement, oligohydramnios; sometimes abnormal maternal placental disease markers
★ **EFW <3rd percentile** indicates severe disease; normal-size parents do not establish constitutional smallness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental resistance reduces oxygen/nutrients; redistribution preserves cerebral over abdominal growth
Low fetal renal perfusion reduces urine production and fluid volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ultrasound biometry using reliable dating → detailed anatomy; serial growth generally every 3–4 weeks
★ **Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks**; absent (AEDV)/reversed (REDV) diastolic velocity → intensified surveillance
Weekly NST after viability; increase frequency with Doppler deterioration or maternal comorbidity
Early <32 weeks, unexplained or anomalous → offer amniocentesis/microarray; CMV PCR if amniocentesis chosen
Do not order indiscriminate TORCH panels without exposure or suggestive findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reversed flow → **hospitalization**, corticosteroids, frequent cardiotocography, delivery planning
Anticipated preterm birth → betamethasone; magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks
Nonreassuring testing/maternal deterioration → earlier delivery; absent/reversed flow may favor cesarean
Bed rest, sildenafil, and LMWH solely to treat/prevent FGR provide no established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, intrapartum intolerance, neonatal hypoglycemia, hypothermia, polycythemia; later metabolic/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tobacco/drug cessation, maternal disease control; low-dose aspirin when preeclampsia-risk criteria met

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates: early ultrasound establishes gestational age
Constitutionally small fetus: reassuring interval growth and normal Doppler without placental disease

table.title: Patterns and delivery in otherwise stable disease
rows: Often later placental insufficiency; patterns overlap

gastroenteritis.name: Gastroenteritis
gastroenteritis.scope: Viral gastroenteritis (rotavirus, norovirus), foodborne illness, bacterial enteritis, traveler's diarrhea (ETEC), oral rehydration therapy, dehydration assessment
gastroenteritis.core: Acute vomiting and diarrhea usually need hydration and selective testing; shock, blood, focal pain, or systemic toxicity changes the approach.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sick contacts, contaminated food/water, travel, childcare or institutional outbreaks
Infants, older adults and immunocompromised people have greater dehydration or invasive-infection risk
Pet reptiles → nontyphoidal Salmonella; young infants prone to bacteremia

rows.label: Clues
items: Watery stools and diffuse cramps favor noninvasive disease; fever or dysentery suggests inflammatory enteritis
Mild dehydration: thirst, dry mouth, reduced urine; children → fewer wet diapers, absent tears
★ Lethargy, delayed capillary refill, tachycardia, hypotension → **severe dehydration/shock**
Toddler + high fever, bloody diarrhea, **seizure** → Shigella; HUS appears days later with hemolysis/AKI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intestinal secretion or epithelial injury causes water/electrolyte losses
Sodium–glucose cotransport remains functional, allowing oral rehydration despite ongoing diarrhea

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Mild self-limited illness → **no routine stool tests**
Stool PCR/culture and Shiga toxin for bloody diarrhea, high fever, severe pain or sepsis
Electrolytes/creatinine for severe dehydration; C difficile testing after antibiotics or healthcare exposure
Persistent >14 days or relevant travel → evaluate parasites; focal/peritoneal pain → imaging for surgical cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oral rehydration solution**, frequent small volumes; continue breastfeeding and usual diet
Shock/severe dehydration or failed oral intake → IV isotonic crystalloid; reassess perfusion
Ondansetron can enable oral hydration; avoid juice/soda as primary replacement
Moderate/severe travelers’ diarrhea → azithromycin; suspected STEC → no antibiotics
Loperamide only selected adults with afebrile nonbloody diarrhea; avoid children and inflammatory disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Prerenal AKI, metabolic acidosis, electrolyte abnormalities; postinfectious lactose intolerance
STEC → HUS with hemolysis, low platelets and AKI; invasive bacteria → bacteremia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Handwashing with soap/water, food safety, **rotavirus vaccination** in infancy
Norovirus outbreaks: environmental disinfection; food handlers remain off work ≥48 hours after symptoms resolve

rows.label: Mimics
items: Appendicitis/intussusception: localized or episodic severe pain disproportionate to diarrhea
DKA: hyperglycemia, ketones; IBD: persistent bloody diarrhea and weight loss

table.title: Common noninvasive enteritis
rows: Vomiting followed by substantial watery diarrhea

gastrointestinal-bleeding.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
gastrointestinal-bleeding.scope: Upper GI bleeding (PUD, varices, Mallory-Weiss), lower GI bleeding (diverticular, angiodysplasia, hemorrhoids), fluid and transfusion thresholds, endoscopy
gastrointestinal-bleeding.core: Hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia → assess hemodynamics before localizing; brisk upper bleeding can present as bright red rectal blood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: NSAIDs/H pylori → ulcers; cirrhosis → varices; forceful retching → mucosal tear
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets increase severity; older age favors diverticula or angiodysplasia

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Syncope, orthostasis, shock** signal major loss; initial hemoglobin may remain normal
Epigastric pain supports ulcer; painless bleeding favors vascular sources
Recurrent occult loss → iron deficiency
**Melena**, elevated BUN/creatinine ratio → upper source; bilious NG aspirate argues against upper bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal injury, portal-pressure collaterals, or fragile vessels rupture into GI lumen
Volume depletion → reduced perfusion; ongoing bleeding may require massive transfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Two large-bore IVs, CBC, type/cross, coagulation tests**, serial hemoglobin; resuscitate before procedures
Upper source → EGD within 24 hours after stabilization; suspected varices → within 12 hours
★ Ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia → **CT angiography → embolization** if active extravasation
Stable lower bleeding → bowel preparation and nonemergent colonoscopy; routine <24-hour colonoscopy adds no benefit
Rectal bleeding mixed with stool, age ≥45 → colonoscopy; negative FOBT does not exclude neoplasia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crystalloid initially; stable nonischemic adults → **RBC transfusion at hemoglobin <7 g/dL**
Exsanguination or post-crystalloid shock → **RBCs** regardless of hemoglobin, not vasopressors; cardiac ischemia → higher threshold
Severe anticoagulant bleeding → drug-specific reversal; uncontrolled varices → balloon tamponade as temporary bridge only
Failed endoscopy → IR/surgery; massive unlocalized lower bleeding → **total abdominal colectomy**, not segmental
Suspected ulcer → IV PPI; endoscopic hemostasis for active bleeding/visible vessel, then high-dose PPI

rows.label: Complications
items: Rebleeding, aspiration, myocardial ischemia, AKI; variceal bleeding → infection
Massive transfusion → hypocalcemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy; embolization → bowel ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eradicate H pylori and confirm cure; avoid NSAIDs; PPI for high-risk users
After variceal control: nonselective beta-blocker plus repeat banding; recurrent bleeding → TIPS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron/bismuth: dark stool without blood loss
Hemoptysis: coughing frothy blood rather than vomiting
Swallowed epistaxis: nasal source on examination

table.title: Source-specific branches
rows: Postretching tear; Boerhaave instead: chest pain, crepitus
Liver trauma + jaundice; blood from ampulla

gastrointestinal-bleeding.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG lower GI bleeding 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735555/), [ACS transfusion guidance 2025](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009).

genitourinary-trauma.name: Genitourinary trauma
genitourinary-trauma.scope: Posterior urethral injury, anterior urethral injury, bladder rupture, retrograde urethrography, renal trauma, testicular trauma
genitourinary-trauma.core: Hematuria or inability to void after trauma requires localization of urinary injury before instrumentation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pelvic fracture → posterior urethra/bladder; straddle injury → anterior bulbar urethra
Deceleration, flank impact or penetrating wounds → renal/collecting-system injury
Blunt scrotal trauma → testicular rupture; empty bladder better protected than distended bladder
Hysterectomy/pelvic surgery → ureteral ligation: flank pain, fever, unilateral hydroureteronephrosis; not pyelonephritis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Blood at urethral meatus**, retention, perineal/scrotal hematoma or high-riding prostate → urethral injury
Gross hematuria with pelvic fracture → suspect bladder rupture
Flank ecchymosis, tenderness or lower rib fractures suggest renal injury
Scrotal swelling, bruising and loss of normal contour suggest testicular rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pelvic shearing disrupts membranous urethra; direct compression splits the bulbar segment
Intraperitoneal urine leakage irritates peritoneum; blood loss can cause shock despite modest hematuria

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected urethral injury → **retrograde urethrogram before Foley**; no blind repeated attempts
★ Stable gross hematuria + pelvic fracture → **retrograde CT/plain cystography**
Blunt flank trauma → **urinalysis**; stable, no hematuria → **no further testing** unless high-energy deceleration
Stable gross hematuria, or microscopic + hypotension → contrast CT abdomen/pelvis with delayed images, not laparotomy
Testicular injury → Doppler ultrasound; absent flow or high clinical suspicion → immediate exploration

rows.label: Tx
items: Hemodynamic instability → trauma resuscitation and urgent operative/angiographic hemorrhage control
Urethral disruption → urology, suprapubic drainage or selected endoscopic realignment
★ **Intraperitoneal bladder rupture → surgical repair**; uncomplicated extraperitoneal rupture → catheter drainage
Stable renal injuries → observation; ongoing arterial bleeding → selective embolization
Testicular rupture → urgent exploration, repair and removal of nonviable tissue

rows.label: Complications
items: Urethral stricture, erectile dysfunction, incontinence; urinary extravasation → infection or urinoma
Delayed renal bleeding, hypertension or kidney loss; testicular atrophy and infertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective equipment; safe catheter technique; follow-up for stricture after urethral injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Testicular torsion: absent flow with spermatic-cord twist; also surgical emergency
Nontraumatic stone: colicky flank pain without injury mechanism

glomerulonephritis.name: Glomerulonephritis
glomerulonephritis.scope: Nephritic syndrome, poststreptococcal GN, IgA nephropathy, rapidly progressive GN (anti-GBM, ANCA), lupus nephritis, RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria quantification, kidney biopsy
glomerulonephritis.core: Glomerular inflammation causes hematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, edema, and reduced filtration; rapidly rising creatinine demands urgent evaluation for crescentic disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent streptococcal pharyngitis/skin infection, systemic autoimmunity, small-vessel vasculitis
IgA nephropathy often follows mucosal infection; anti-GBM pulmonary bleeding risk increases with smoking

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs** identify a glomerular bleeding source
Tea-colored urine, oliguria, periorbital swelling; nephrotic-range protein loss can coexist
★ **Hemoptysis + AKI** → pulmonary–renal syndrome; rapidly progressive disease may initially lack systemic symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune complexes, basement-membrane antibodies, or pauci-immune vascular injury inflame glomerular capillaries
Crescent formation compresses capillary tufts → rapid, potentially irreversible loss of filtration
Reduced filtration → sodium/water retention → **volume overload**, edema, hypertension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Urinalysis/microscopy → **creatinine, electrolytes, urine protein/creatinine ratio**; monitor urine output
C3/C4, ANA/dsDNA, ANCA, anti-GBM; ASO/anti-DNase B when poststreptococcal disease suspected
★ **Kidney biopsy** for rapidly progressive AKI, substantial persistent proteinuria, or uncertain systemic GN
Typical childhood poststreptococcal course may not require biopsy; persistent low C3 beyond 8 weeks warrants reassessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Salt restriction, loop diuretics for overload, BP control; ACE inhibitor/ARB for persistent proteinuria when stable
★ Pulmonary–renal/RPGN → **urgent nephrology, steroids + immunosuppression** before irreversible decline
Anti-GBM: plasma exchange + cyclophosphamide; ANCA: rituximab/cyclophosphamide; plasma exchange only selected severe cases
Lupus: biopsy-directed mycophenolate/cyclophosphamide + steroids; poststreptococcal disease mainly supportive

rows.label: Complications
items: Hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, hypertensive emergency, CKD; dialysis for refractory life-threatening derangements
Immunosuppression → infection, cytopenias, infertility with cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP/proteinuria, avoid nephrotoxins, follow renal function and urine findings

rows.label: Mimics
items: ATN: muddy-brown casts after ischemia/toxins
Urologic bleeding: isomorphic RBCs, clots, no RBC casts

glomerulonephritis.evidence: Not checked online; established nephrology teaching.

graft-versus-host-disease.name: Graft-versus-host disease
graft-versus-host-disease.scope: Acute GVHD (maculopapular rash, secretory diarrhea, hyperbilirubinemia), chronic GVHD (sclerotic skin, lichenoid changes, sicca syndrome), donor T-cell mediated attack, methylprednisolone
graft-versus-host-disease.core: Multisystem injury from donor immune cells after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HLA mismatch, unrelated donor, older recipient, peripheral blood graft; prior acute disease increases chronic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Acute: rash often begins on face, ears, palms or soles; severe cases blister or desquamate
★ Chronic: reduced joint range from fasciitis; new airflow obstruction suggests bronchiolitis obliterans

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Donor **T cells** recognize recipient alloantigens; epithelial injury acutely, dysregulated immunity and fibrosis chronically

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Classify by manifestations; day 100 alone does not distinguish acute from chronic disease
Stage acute disease by rash extent, bilirubin, and diarrhea volume or severe GI symptoms
Exclude infection and drug toxicity; biopsy affected tissue when uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: Limited skin disease → topical corticosteroids; supportive fluids, nutrition and infection surveillance
★ Significant acute disease → systemic **methylprednisolone**
Moderate or severe chronic disease → systemic prednisone; steroid-refractory acute or chronic disease → ruxolitinib

rows.label: Complications
items: Fluid and protein loss, skin contractures, irreversible airflow obstruction, opportunistic infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Post-transplant cyclophosphamide or calcineurin inhibitor-based prophylaxis by transplant protocol
Irradiated cellular blood products for at-risk recipients prevent transfusion-associated GVHD

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome: painful hepatomegaly, weight gain and ascites early after transplant
C difficile colitis: toxin-positive stool without characteristic skin or liver involvement

graft-versus-host-disease.evidence: Checked EBMT consensus recommendations on GVHD prophylaxis and management (2024).

head-and-neck-cancer.name: Head and neck cancer
head-and-neck-cancer.scope: Oral cavity cancer, laryngeal cancer, pharyngeal cancer, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, tobacco and alcohol risk, HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma
head-and-neck-cancer.core: Persistent hoarseness, unilateral throat/ear symptoms, a nonhealing oral lesion, or an adult neck mass requires malignancy evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, alcohol: each independent, dose-dependent squamous cancer risk, synergistic together; betel nut in some populations
HPV exposure drives many oropharyngeal cancers; EBV associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral ulcer or red/white plaque persisting >2–3 weeks; dysphagia, odynophagia, weight loss
★ **Adult persistent lateral neck mass** may be metastatic carcinoma, even when cystic
Unilateral referred otalgia with normal otoscopy; hemoptysis or stridor indicates advanced local disease
Nasopharyngeal disease → unilateral serous otitis, epistaxis or cranial neuropathy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal squamous transformation and lymphatic spread; field carcinogenesis produces synchronous/second primary tumors

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Direct visualization and biopsy** of mucosal lesion; flexible nasolaryngoscopy for inaccessible sites
Neck mass → contrast CT/MRI plus **fine-needle aspiration**; avoid initial open biopsy
Oropharyngeal tumor → p16/HPV testing; staging imaging assesses regional nodes and distant metastases
Persistent hoarseness → laryngoscopy; no prolonged empiric reflux treatment when malignancy clues present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway compromise/stridor → **secure airway** with ENT/anesthesia support
Early localized cancer → surgery or radiation according to site and function
Locally advanced → combined surgery/radiation with cisplatin-based systemic treatment or definitive chemoradiation
Nasopharyngeal cancer → chemoradiation; recurrent/metastatic disease → systemic treatment, often checkpoint inhibitor

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, airway obstruction, malnutrition, carotid bleeding; nodal/distant metastases
Radiation → xerostomia, dental decay, osteoradionecrosis; surgery → speech/swallow impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Smoking/alcohol cessation, HPV vaccination; dental assessment before head/neck radiation
Swallowing rehabilitation, nutrition support; surveillance for recurrence and second primary cancer

rows.label: Mimics
items: Laryngitis: brief postviral hoarseness resolving with recovery
Branchial cleft cyst: benign developmental lesion; new adult cystic mass still needs cancer exclusion

head-and-neck-cancer.evidence: Neck-mass evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [AAO-HNS adult neck-mass guideline](https://www.entnet.org/quality-practice/quality-products/clinical-practice-guidelines/evaluation-of-the-neck-mass-in-adults/); oncology: established teaching.

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles or wheeze (cardiac asthma), dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Low effective volume → baroreceptor-driven nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease
Alveolar flooding → V/Q mismatch, widened A-a gradient, hypoxemia
High-output HF: severe anemia, AV fistula (larger fistula → more shunt); HF signs with **normal/high EF**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Congested HFrEF → loop diuretic + **ACE inhibitor/ARNI first**; beta-blocker/MRA once compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI: 36-hour washout
MRA: eGFR >30, K <5; never ACE inhibitor + ARB; EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD
HFrEF foundation drugs lower mortality; loop diuretics, nitrates alone, digoxin relieve symptoms only

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain
ARDS: diffuse infiltrates, no cephalization; massive crystalloid + **cephalization/perihilar fullness** → volume overload

table.title: Chronic phenotypes
rows: Sacubitril/valsartan (or ACEi/ARB), carvedilol/metoprolol succinate, spironolactone, dapagliflozin

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

hematuria.name: Hematuria
hematuria.scope: Microscopic hematuria, gross hematuria, dipstick confirmation with urine sediment, glomerular vs extraglomerular workup, cystoscopy and CT urography indications
hematuria.core: Urinary RBCs require localization to glomerular versus urologic bleeding, then malignancy evaluation based on risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Urothelial cancer: older age, smoking, aromatic amines, pelvic radiation, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Clues
items: Clots favor urologic bleeding; edema and hypertension suggest nephritis
★ Painless visible bleeding → malignancy concern even if transient
Colicky flank pain suggests stone; dysuria and urgency favor infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Glomerular capillary injury permits RBC passage; tubular transit distorts RBCs and forms casts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive dipstick → **urine microscopy**; ≥3 RBC/hpf on properly collected specimen defines microhematuria
★ RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria or renal dysfunction → nephrology plus risk-based urologic evaluation
★ Unexplained gross bleeding → **cystoscopy + CT urography**; MR urography if contrast CT contraindicated
Assess age, sex, smoking, RBC count and gross bleeding history; anticoagulation does not change evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: UTI → antibiotics, then repeat microscopy after resolution; persistent RBCs → risk-stratified workup
Clot retention → large-bore three-way Foley, irrigation, urgent urology

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive AKI from clots; anemia with sustained bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation to reduce future urothelial cancer risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria: positive heme with absent RBCs
Food or phenazopyridine discoloration: red urine with negative heme

table.title: Microscopic hematuria workup by malignancy risk
rows: Same anatomic workup as gross bleeding

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hyperbilirubinemia.name: Hyperbilirubinemia
hyperbilirubinemia.scope: Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, unconjugated vs conjugated, biliary atresia
hyperbilirubinemia.core: Fractionate bilirubin first: indirect elevation reflects production or conjugation problems; direct elevation requires assessment of hepatobiliary excretion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fasting, illness or dehydration triggers Gilbert jaundice; family history suggests inherited bilirubin disorders
Persistent infant jaundice can reflect biliary atresia even after initially reassuring appearance

rows.label: Clues
items: Indirect bilirubin is albumin-bound and absent from urine; direct bilirubin can darken urine
★ Infant **pale/acholic stools**, dark urine, hepatomegaly → obstructive cholestasis
Pruritus, pale stools and elevated alkaline phosphatase suggest impaired bile flow
Severe neonatal indirect elevation with lethargy, poor feeding or abnormal tone → bilirubin neurotoxicity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heme breakdown yields unconjugated pigment; hepatic UGT conjugation enables biliary elimination
Unbound unconjugated bilirubin crosses the immature blood–brain barrier; conjugated bilirubin does not cause kernicterus
Large hematoma/cephalhematoma resorption → bilirubin overproduction, indirect jaundice

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Total/direct bilirubin**, AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase/GGT; CBC/reticulocytes/LDH for suspected hemolysis
Isolated mild indirect elevation with normal liver tests and no hemolysis → Gilbert diagnosis
★ Jaundice beyond 2 weeks → fractionate; **direct ≥1 mg/dL at 2–4 weeks** → urgent referral
Infant cholestasis → ultrasound; biliary atresia assessment may require biopsy and operative cholangiography
Adult conjugated elevation with pain/obstruction → RUQ ultrasound before advanced duct imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected biliary atresia → urgent pediatric hepatology/surgery; **early Kasai portoenterostomy**
Severe neonatal indirect, even Coombs-positive → **phototherapy** first; exchange: failure, critical level, encephalopathy
Crigler–Najjar I → intensive phototherapy, definitive liver transplant; type II responds to phenobarbital
Gilbert, Dubin–Johnson and Rotor → reassurance once competing pathology excluded
Cholestasis → nutritional support, fat-soluble vitamins and cause-specific treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Indirect neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → acute encephalopathy/kernicterus
Untreated atresia → cirrhosis, portal hypertension, liver failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Inspect stool color and fractionate persistent infant jaundice; never label conjugated jaundice physiologic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hemolysis: anemia, reticulocytosis, low haptoglobin; newborn ABO: mother O, baby A/B, Coombs-positive
Choledochal cyst: cystic/dilated extrahepatic ducts on ultrasound
Physiologic jaundice: indirect, after 24 h, peaks days 3–5, thriving; transient UGT immaturity
Breast-milk jaundice: indirect, thriving; direct elevation excludes it

hyperbilirubinemia.evidence: Infant referral checked 2026-10-30: [AAP 2025](https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/pdfDownload/31302); inherited syndromes established teaching.

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation
High filtered calcium exceeds tubular reabsorption → **hypercalciuria** → calcium stones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **Denosumab** (favored, esp renal limitation/refractory) or **IV zoledronic acid/pamidronate** for sustained malignancy control
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.name: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.scope: Chronic and gestational HTN, preeclampsia, HELLP, eclampsia
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy-associated hypertension; maternal organ injury or placental dysfunction signals danger even without substantial proteinuria.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior preeclampsia, chronic HTN, CKD, diabetes, SLE/APS, multifetal gestation
Nulliparity, obesity, age ≥35, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, visual disturbance, RUQ/epigastric pain, dyspnea; edema nonspecific
★ Severe features: **platelets <100,000/µL**, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, transaminases ≥2× normal
Other severe features: pulmonary edema, refractory neurologic symptoms
Presentation through **6 weeks postpartum**; eclampsia/HELLP possible without prior HTN

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling → placental ischemia → systemic endothelial injury, vasospasm, capillary leak

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BP ≥140/90**, either component, twice ≥4 h apart; severe ≥160/110 confirmed within minutes
CBC/platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, urine protein; fetal growth US + antenatal testing
Proteinuria: **≥300 mg/24 h** or protein/creatinine ≥0.3; dipstick 2+ only if quantification unavailable
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria/end-organ injury → superimposed preeclampsia; HELLP: smear, LDH ≥600 IU/L

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent severe BP ≥15 min → **IV labetalol/hydralazine** or immediate-release oral nifedipine within 30–60 min
★ Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia → **magnesium sulfate** through 24 h postpartum; airway before delivery
Chronic HTN ≥140/90 → oral labetalol/extended-release nifedipine; avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs
Mg toxicity: areflexia/hypoventilation → stop infusion, **IV calcium gluconate**; oliguria → reduce dose

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, abruption, DIC, AKI, hepatic hematoma/rupture; fetal growth restriction, prematurity, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High risk or multiple moderate risks → **aspirin 81 mg/day**, start 12–28 wk, ideally before 16
Postpartum BP review within 72 h if severe, otherwise 7–10 days; long-term cardiovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP: profound thrombocytopenia/hemolysis, persists after delivery
Acute fatty liver: hypoglycemia, jaundice, marked coagulopathy
Epilepsy: established seizure disorder; evaluate alternative causes despite obstetric context

table.title: Classification and delivery
rows: Before 20 wk or persists >12 wk postpartum
After 20 wk + proteinuria OR severe features
Severe BP alone sufficient; <34 stable → betamethasone
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Deliver after stabilization, any gestational age

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, lid lag, onycholysis, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults: apathetic
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → **Doppler ultrasound** or radioiodine uptake (not if pregnant/lactating)
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, mild hypercalcemia, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity
Pregnancy: thionamides/TRAb cross placenta → **fetal goiter**, impaired swallowing, polyhydramnios

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing
Orbital pseudotumor: involves muscle bellies and tendons; Graves spares tendons

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema, acropachy (clubbing)
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, oxytocin; **hypotonic IV D5W**, postoperative state, exercise + excess water
Pulmonary/CNS disease; **small cell lung cancer** (ectopic ADH); heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality
Massive water intake, often psychiatric illness; urine osmolality below serum still favors polydipsia, even if >100

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration
Low effective volume (heart failure, cirrhosis, diarrhea) → baroreceptor ADH release; total-body sodium high in edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
