Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cerebral salt wasting: neurosurgical patient, hypovolemic, high urine Na; SIADH euvolemic
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.name: Hypothesis testing and statistical tests
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.scope: Null and alternative hypotheses, Type I and Type II errors, statistical power, confidence intervals, p-values, t-tests (paired, unpaired), ANOVA, chi-square, Pearson correlation
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.core: Hypothesis tests quantify incompatibility with a null model; confidence intervals describe effect estimates and uncertainty.

rows.label: Definition
items: H0: no difference/association; H1: specified difference or association
★ **α**: false-positive probability; Type I error rejects a true null
★ **β**: false-negative probability; Type II error misses a real effect

rows.label: Formula
items: Power = **1 − β**; increases with sample size, effect size, α, lower variability
95% CI ≈ estimate ± 1.96 × standard error; plausible range for true effect

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **p-value**: probability of equally/more extreme data assuming H0; not probability H0 true
95% CI excludes 0 for differences or 1 for ratios → two-sided p <0.05

rows.label: Use when
items: Pearson r: linear association between continuous variables; range −1 to +1
Ordinal/non-normal independent data → Mann–Whitney; paired → Wilcoxon signed-rank

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Nonsignificant ≠ equivalent; statistical significance ≠ clinical importance
Repeated comparisons inflate false positives; prespecify outcomes or adjust α
Correlation neither establishes causation nor detects every nonlinear relationship

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.scope: Hashimoto thyroiditis, subclinical hypothyroidism, myxedema coma, autoimmune associations, levothyroxine dosing, TSH monitoring
hypothyroidism.core: Insufficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism, causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hashimoto autoimmunity, family history of autoimmune disease; thyroid surgery/radioiodine, iodine deficiency/excess
Lithium, amiodarone, postpartum thyroiditis; pituitary surgery/radiation or mass
Congenital primary → **thyroid dysgenesis** most common, not lymphocytic thyroiditis

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight gain, bradycardia, hoarseness, heavy menses, hyperlipidemia; hyponatremia in severe disease
★ **Hypothermia, altered mentation, hypoventilation, hypotension** → myxedema coma
Autoimmune clustering: type 1 diabetes, pernicious anemia, adrenal insufficiency, celiac disease
Infant: macroglossia, umbilical hernia, prolonged jaundice, hypotonia, large fontanelle → **TSH/free T4**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced hormone activity lowers thermogenesis and cardiac output; glycosaminoglycan deposition produces nonpitting edema
Hashimoto: lymphocytic infiltration; firm painless goiter, even if euthyroid; **anti-TPO/antithyroglobulin** antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH and free T4** establish hormone deficiency and localize the level of dysfunction
Positive anti-TPO predicts progression from subclinical disease; ultrasound unnecessary without nodule/goiter concern
Recheck mild isolated TSH elevation after transient illness resolves; exclude medication interference

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Levothyroxine**; healthy young adult approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day; older/CAD start 12.5–25 mcg/day
Fasting, apart from calcium/iron; TSH at 6–8 weeks; **persistently high → increase dose**, even if asymptomatic
Central disease: titrate using free T4; evaluate/replace cortisol before thyroid hormone
Subclinical, untreated: generally start at TSH ≥10; consider symptoms, antibodies, pregnancy at lower values
★ Myxedema: **IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone**, airway support, cautious fluids/passive warming; treat trigger

rows.label: Complications
items: Dyslipidemia, infertility, pericardial effusion, neuropathy; severe disease → respiratory failure
Excess replacement → AF, angina, bone loss; rapid correction in CAD can precipitate ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Pregnancy: early **TSH monitoring**, usually increase existing replacement promptly; use pregnancy-specific targets
Monitor stable replacement at least annually; address adherence/absorption before escalating doses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Depression, dementia, psychosis: normal TSH; hypothyroidism itself can cause reversible cognitive or psychiatric symptoms
Euthyroid sick syndrome: acute systemic illness, often low T3; avoid routine hormone replacement

hypothyroidism.evidence: Not checked online; established thyroid replacement and endocrine emergency teaching.

impetigo.name: Impetigo
impetigo.scope: Nonbullous impetigo (honey-colored crusts), bullous impetigo, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, topical mupirocin, oral cephalexin, poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis risk
impetigo.core: Contagious superficial bacterial infection causes crusted erosions or fragile blisters, usually in children; lesion extent determines topical versus oral treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Preschool age, warm humid weather, crowding, close contact, shared towels
Skin-barrier disruption from eczema, insect bites, minor trauma, scabies; nasal staphylococcal carriage

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Nonbullous: vesicles/pustules rupture → **honey-colored crusts**, often around nose/mouth
★ Bullous: **flaccid superficial bullae**, collarette scale; intertriginous/truncal distribution common
Usually localized with little systemic illness; high fever, toxicity, diffuse tenderness require broader evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonbullous disease: S aureus and/or group A streptococci infect superficial epidermis
Bullous disease: staphylococcal exfoliative toxin cleaves desmoglein 1; bacterial growth remains localized

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical diagnosis**; no routine blood tests
Culture exudate when recurrent, extensive, treatment-resistant, outbreak-associated, or MRSA suspected
Deep punched-out crusted ulcer → ecthyma, extending into dermis; consider oral treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: Gently cleanse with soap/water, soften crusts; cover lesions and trim nails
★ Few localized lesions → **topical mupirocin for 5 days**
★ Numerous lesions, outbreaks, ecthyma → **oral cephalexin or dicloxacillin for 7 days**
Suspected/confirmed MRSA → culture-directed clindamycin, doxycycline, or TMP-SMX; account for age and streptococcal coverage
Streptococci alone on culture → oral penicillin; reassess spread or failure to improve

rows.label: Complications
items: Cellulitis, lymphangitis, deeper ulceration with scarring; systemic infection uncommon
**Poststreptococcal GN** can follow skin infection; antibiotics do not reliably prevent it
Acute rheumatic fever classically follows streptococcal pharyngitis rather than uncomplicated impetigo

rows.label: Prevention
items: Handwashing, separate towels, avoid scratching, treat underlying eczema/scabies
Avoid contact sports while contagious; repeated infections may prompt household/colonization assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV: grouped painful vesicles, recurrent distribution; eczema herpeticum: monomorphic punched-out erosions
Contact dermatitis: prominent itch, exposure-shaped rash, no bacterial crust initially
Staphylococcal scalded skin: diffuse tender peeling, systemic toxin effect, often sterile bullae

increased-intracranial-pressure.name: Increased intracranial pressure
increased-intracranial-pressure.scope: Cushing triad, papilledema, ventriculoperitoneal shunt malfunction, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, herniation syndromes, hyperosmolar therapy
increased-intracranial-pressure.core: Progressive headache, vomiting, or depressed consciousness from raised intracranial pressure requires rapid distinction between mass effect, hydrocephalus, and idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trauma, intracranial bleeding, tumor, cerebral edema, CNS infection, obstructed CSF flow
VP shunt: blockage (most common) or infection; IIH: obesity, reproductive-age women, tetracyclines, retinoids/vitamin A supplements

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning/Valsalva headache, papilledema, diplopia from sixth-nerve palsy; infants may have bulging fontanelle
★ **Cushing triad**: hypertension/widened pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations; late, compensatory; treat ICP, not BP
Uncal herniation → ipsilateral fixed dilated pupil, contralateral weakness; tonsillar herniation → respiratory arrest
IIH: pulsatile tinnitus, transient visual obscurations; shunt failure: recurrent headache, vomiting, lethargy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fixed skull volume: excess tissue, blood, or CSF raises pressure after compensatory reserve exhausted
Cerebral perfusion pressure = MAP − ICP; falling perfusion worsens ischemia and edema
IIH: **impaired CSF resorption** at arachnoid granulations; ventricles normal/small, no obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unstable/acute deficit → **noncontrast head CT**; papilledema with stable suspected IIH → MRI + MRV
★ **No LP before excluding mass effect/obstructive hydrocephalus** when concerning signs present
IIH: normal imaging aside from supportive findings → **LP**: normal CSF composition, opening pressure ≥25 cm H₂O
Shunt failure → head imaging, shunt series, urgent neurosurgery; normal ventricular size does not exclude obstruction
Recent shunt revision + fever + neutrophilic CSF → **shunt infection**, not community meningitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Herniation concern → **airway/intubation first**, head elevation, IV **hypertonic saline or mannitol**, urgent neurosurgery
Avoid hypoxia/hypotension; brief controlled hyperventilation only as bridge for impending herniation
Hydrocephalus → CSF drainage/shunt revision; mass lesion → definitive decompression
Dexamethasone for tumor-associated vasogenic edema; no corticosteroids for traumatic brain injury
IIH → weight loss + acetazolamide; threatened vision → optic nerve fenestration or CSF diversion

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent visual loss, ischemic injury, herniation, death
Hyperosmolar agents → electrolyte/renal disturbances; CSF devices → infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid causative drugs in IIH; follow visual fields and optic discs
Shunt education: prompt evaluation for recurrence or fever; injury prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Migraine: normal fundus and no progressive focal/mental-status findings
Cerebral venous thrombosis: venous obstruction on MRV, not idiopathic disease

increased-intracranial-pressure.evidence: Not checked online; established neurocritical care and IIH diagnostic principles.

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; Roth spots retinal; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common
Estrogen → proliferative endometrium; LH surge → ovulation
Corpus luteum **progesterone** → secretory endometrium, ↑basal body temperature

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ Ovulatory + normal semen → **HSG** (tubes) before laparoscopy; saline sonography: cavity; avoid in pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Anovulation/PCOS → **letrozole**, clomiphene alternative; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

inflammatory-bowel-disease.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
inflammatory-bowel-disease.scope: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, extraintestinal manifestations (erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis), toxic megacolon, colorectal cancer risk, biologic therapy
inflammatory-bowel-disease.core: Chronic relapsing intestinal inflammation: Crohn disease affects any gastrointestinal segment; ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, young adulthood; smoking worsens Crohn disease
NSAIDs and enteric infections can precipitate flares

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, anemia; children may have growth failure
Arthritis, uveitis; PSC particularly associated with UC
Erythema nodosum: tender nonulcerating nodules; **pyoderma gangrenosum**: rapid painful violaceous ulcer, purulent base
★ Severe colitis: fever, tachycardia, frequent bloody stools; distention, colon >6 cm → **toxic megacolon**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysregulated mucosal immune response to intestinal microbiota in genetically susceptible hosts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stool **C. difficile** testing and cultures before attributing worsening diarrhea to inflammation
Fecal calprotectin supports intestinal inflammation; **ileocolonoscopy with biopsies** confirms
Suspected small-bowel disease or abscess → CT/MR enterography; avoid capsule with suspected stricture
Partial SBO, suspected stricture → enterography; older exam questions may expect **water-soluble small-bowel follow-through**
Fulminant colitis → abdominal radiograph and limited sigmoidoscopy; avoid full colonoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe UC → hospitalization, **IV methylprednisolone**, fluids, VTE prophylaxis
Steroid-refractory severe UC → infliximab or cyclosporine; perforation or megacolon → urgent colectomy
★ Moderate/severe flare without obstruction or abscess → **prednisone** induces remission only; **never maintenance**
Crohn abscess → antibiotics and drainage before immunosuppression
UC with colorectal cancer → **total proctocolectomy**, not segmental colectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Fistulas (enterovaginal → vaginal flatus), strictures, obstruction in Crohn; colectomy does not cure Crohn
Terminal ileal Crohn → B12 deficiency, **bile salt malabsorption** → steatorrhea
Colonic disease → colorectal cancer; active inflammation → venous thromboembolism

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Colonic disease → surveillance colonoscopy beginning about **8 years** after onset; PSC → immediately
Vaccinate and screen TB/HBV before biologics; smoking cessation for Crohn

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no bleeding, weight loss or inflammatory markers
Ischemic colitis: abrupt pain followed by hematochezia, vascular risk

table.title: Distribution and outpatient treatment
rows: RLQ mass, cobblestones, perianal disease, granulomas
Bloody diarrhea, tenesmus; friability, crypt abscesses, pseudopolyps

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

invasive-fungal-infections.name: Invasive fungal infections
invasive-fungal-infections.scope: Invasive aspergillosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), mucormycosis, candidemia, amphotericin B, voriconazole, systemic corticosteroids
invasive-fungal-infections.core: Fungal syndromes range from allergic airway disease to lethal tissue invasion; immune status and imaging guide testing and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged neutropenia/transplant → molds; DKA, glucocorticoids or iron overload → mucormycosis
Central lines, TPN, abdominal surgery, broad antibiotics → invasive Candida
ABPA: asthma or cystic fibrosis; hypersensitivity rather than tissue invasion
Old TB cavity → **aspergilloma**: mobile fungus ball, air crescent, hemoptysis; colonization, not invasion

rows.label: Clues
items: Invasive aspergillosis: fever despite antibiotics, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, pulmonary nodules
★ **Black nasal/palatal eschar**, facial pain, ophthalmoplegia → rhinocerebral mucormycosis
Candidemia: sepsis, persistent positive blood cultures; metastatic eye, heart or deep-organ infection
ABPA: recurrent wheeze, brown mucus plugs, fleeting pulmonary infiltrates

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Angioinvasive molds cause vascular thrombosis, infarction and necrosis
Candida translocates through damaged gut or colonizes intravascular devices, then disseminates hematogenously

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected mold pneumonia → **chest CT**, bronchoscopy/BAL or tissue biopsy
Aspergillus galactomannan in serum/BAL; β-D-glucan supports several fungi but usually negative in mucormycosis
Necrotic sinus lesion → urgent endoscopic biopsy for histology/culture; do not await blood cultures
Candidemia → repeat blood cultures until clear; assess source and metastatic foci
ABPA: Aspergillus-IgE + total IgE ≥500 IU/mL; two of eosinophilia, Aspergillus-IgG, CT bronchiectasis/infiltrates

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aspergillosis → **voriconazole** or isavuconazole; evaluate interactions and liver function
★ Mucormycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B + urgent surgical debridement**; correct DKA/immunosuppression
Candidemia → echinocandin such as micafungin; step down to fluconazole when stable, susceptible and cleared
Remove implicated line when feasible; uncomplicated candidemia → ≥14 days after clearance and symptom resolution
ABPA → prednisolone or itraconazole; recurrent flares → both; avoid steroids for untreated invasive disease

rows.label: Complications
items: CNS dissemination, massive hemoptysis, blindness, endocarditis; high mortality if treatment delayed
Amphotericin → AKI, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia; voriconazole → visual effects, hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Selected high-risk prolonged neutropenia → posaconazole prophylaxis; line hygiene and antibiotic stewardship

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum: necrotic skin lesions with bacterial sepsis
Bacterial abscess: pyogenic cultures; malignancy: tissue without invasive organisms

ischemic-stroke-and-tia.name: Ischemic stroke and TIA
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.scope: TIA (including amaurosis fugax), ischemic stroke, acute management (tPA, thrombectomy), secondary prevention, risk factors
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.core: Abrupt focal neurologic loss from cerebral ischemia; transient monocular blindness means retinal embolism from the ipsilateral carotid.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Hypertension: greatest modifiable risk factor**; smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, carotid atherosclerosis
Atrial fibrillation, recent MI, endocarditis, arterial dissection

rows.label: Clues
items: **Broca** nonfluent, poor repetition, intact comprehension; **Wernicke** fluent paraphasias, poor comprehension, no insight
Crossed: **Weber** ipsilateral CN III, contralateral hemiparesis (midbrain); lateral pons: ipsilateral full-face palsy, deafness
★ **Last known well** establishes treatment timing; symptom discovery time may differ
TIA: resolved deficit without acute infarction, often embolic; urgent evaluation despite normal examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thromboembolism or small-vessel occlusion → infarct core surrounded by salvageable penumbra
Reperfusion preserves threatened tissue but increases hemorrhagic transformation risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Fingerstick glucose + **noncontrast head CT** first; normal early CT does not exclude ischemia
CTA head/neck for large-vessel occlusion; MRI diffusion for small infarcts or diagnostic uncertainty
ECG, telemetry, carotid imaging; echocardiography for suspected cardiac emboli

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling deficit, eligible ≤4.5 hours → **alteplase or tenecteplase**; imaging-selected extended windows possible
Thrombolysis: BP <185/110 before, <180/105 after; exclude bleeding and significant anticoagulant effect
★ Large-vessel occlusion → **mechanical thrombectomy**, selected cases through 24 hours; do not delay thrombolysis
No reperfusion: generally allow BP ≤220/120; oxygen for hypoxemia; swallow assessment before oral intake
Aspirin after hemorrhage excluded; after thrombolysis, wait 24 hours and repeat imaging

rows.label: Complications
items: Cerebral edema, aspiration, venous thrombosis, seizures, disability

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Minor noncardioembolic stroke/high-risk TIA → short **aspirin + clopidogrel**, then single antiplatelet
AF/cardioembolic → oral anticoagulation, timing by infarct/bleeding risk; noncardioembolic → antiplatelet only
Symptomatic carotid stenosis 70–99% → endarterectomy when eligible; selected 50–69% also benefit
Long-term antiplatelet (aspirin allergy → clopidogrel); undertreated hypertension → **intensify antihypertensives**; high-intensity statin

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypoglycemia: deficit reverses with glucose
Migraine aura: spreading positive symptoms; seizure: witnessed convulsion followed by Todd paralysis

table.title: Vascular localization
rows: Occipital: contralateral homonymous hemianopia; macular sparing
Diplopia, vertigo, dysarthria, ataxia, crossed/bilateral signs, coma
Vertigo; ipsilateral Horner/face/ataxia/palate; contralateral body pain-temperature

measures-of-association.name: Measures of association
measures-of-association.scope: Relative risk (RR), odds ratio (OR), attributable risk (AR), absolute risk reduction (ARR), number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH), hazard ratio
measures-of-association.core: Relative measures describe proportional associations; absolute measures incorporate baseline risk and determine treatment benefit or harm.

rows.label: Definition
items: CER = control event rate; EER = experimental event rate
Two-by-two table: exposed events/non-events a/b; unexposed events/non-events c/d
Relative risk reduction (RRR; vaccine efficacy) = (CER − EER)/CER = 1 − RR

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ Ratio null = **1**; risk-difference null = **0**
★ Hazard ratio compares instantaneous event rates over time; not cumulative risk ratio
NNT/NNH require specified outcome and follow-up duration; always round up

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ RR: cohort/RCT; OR: case-control and logistic regression
Attributable risk: excess incidence among exposed attributable to exposure, assuming causality
HR: survival analysis with censoring; constant interpretation assumes proportional hazards

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Use proportions, not percentage numbers, in reciprocal calculations
OR approximates RR only with rare outcomes; common outcomes exaggerate relative association
Association alone cannot establish causality; confounding can distort every measure

measures-of-association.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

measures-of-disease-frequency.name: Measures of disease frequency
measures-of-disease-frequency.scope: Incidence, prevalence, cumulative incidence, incidence rate, attack rate, case fatality rate, mortality rate
measures-of-disease-frequency.core: Disease frequency requires a numerator, eligible denominator, and time frame; new events, existing disease, and deaths answer different questions.

rows.label: Definition
items: Population at risk excludes people already affected or unable to develop the outcome
Person-time sums observation until disease, death, loss to follow-up, or study end

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Prevalence ≈ incidence × average duration** in steady state; compatible time units
Longer survival increases existing disease burden even without more new diagnoses
Cumulative incidence is probability; incidence density has inverse-time units

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Variable follow-up/open cohort → **person-time denominator**; fixed cohort/interval → risk
Prevalence → service planning; attack rate → outbreak food/exposure investigation
Primary prevention → fewer new cases → monitor **incidence**, not prevalence

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case fatality denominator: cases; mortality denominator: population**
Deaths attributed to disease ÷ all deaths = proportionate mortality, not mortality rate
Cross-sectional surveys cannot directly establish incidence or temporal causation

table.title: Independent examples
rows: Current cases ÷ population at one time
New outbreak cases ÷ exposed at-risk people

measures-of-disease-frequency.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
Psychological safety enables reporting; accountability and system improvement can coexist
Effective communication: bedside verbal handoff with patient → real-time feedback, shared mental model

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Stabilize and mitigate harm**, notify supervising clinician, preserve relevant clinical information
★ Disclose facts, consequences, **apology**, treatment/prevention plans; update uncertainties
★ Report through institutional safety system; document clinical facts and disclosure in medical record

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid concealment, altered records, premature blame, or speculation about causation
Do not rely on education alone when workflow permits predictable repeated errors
Do not trust result delivery alone (fax, mail); **test-tracking log** verifies receipt, review, follow-up

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Reckless impairment/dangerous conduct → remove from unsafe duties; institutional escalation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Root cause analysis**: retrospective system investigation; identify multiple contributors
Failure mode and effects analysis: prospective hazard assessment before harm
Handoff: standardized I-PASS/SBAR, pending tasks, contingency plans, receiver synthesis/read-back

table.title: Event classification
rows: Unanticipated death/serious harm/life-saving rescue; prompts RCA
Upstream scheduling/staffing flaw; fix system, not individual

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.evidence: Not checked online; established patient-safety terminology and ethical disclosure principles.

meningitis.name: Meningitis
meningitis.scope: Bacterial meningitis, viral meningitis, fungal/cryptococcal meningitis, CSF interpretation, empiric antimicrobial therapy, chemoprophylaxis
meningitis.core: Fever, headache and meningeal symptoms require prompt CSF evaluation when safe; suspected bacterial meningitis demands antibiotics without imaging-related delay.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adults: **S. pneumoniae** most common; seeded by pneumonia, otitis, sinusitis, CSF leak, asplenia
Neonates: GBS, E. coli, Listeria; older adults/immunocompromised: additional Listeria risk
Crowding/asplenia → meningococcus; advanced HIV/transplant/chemotherapy → Cryptococcus

rows.label: Clues
items: Neck stiffness, photophobia, vomiting; infants may show poor feeding, irritability or bulging fontanelle
★ Petechiae/purpura with shock → **meningococcemia**; absence of rash does not exclude
Confusion, seizure or focal deficit raises encephalitis, raised-pressure or complicated infection concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Organisms reach meninges hematogenously or through contiguous spread/CSF defect; inflammation increases edema and pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Blood cultures → LP** with opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein, Gram stain/culture and PCR
CT before LP for focal deficit, papilledema, new seizure, marked consciousness impairment or significant immunocompromise
★ If LP delayed: cultures then **immediate antibiotics**; CT cannot rule out every pressure hazard
Cryptococcus: subacute, high opening pressure ± CN VI palsy, CSF antigen; TB studies if lymphocytic, low glucose

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult empiric → **vancomycin + ceftriaxone**; add ampicillin if >50 or immunocompromised
Neonate → ampicillin + cefotaxime; avoid ceftriaxone in neonates
Dexamethasone before/with first antibiotic when pneumococcal meningitis suspected; narrow treatment by organism
Cryptococcal meningitis → liposomal amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole; serial therapeutic LPs for pressure
Uncomplicated viral meningitis → supportive care; suspected HSV encephalitis → IV acyclovir

rows.label: Complications
items: Hearing loss, seizures, hydrocephalus, stroke, cognitive impairment; meningococcus → DIC/adrenal hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Meningococcal contacts within 7 days of onset → **rifampin or ceftriaxone**; droplet isolation until 24 hours treated
Hib prophylaxis for qualifying households/childcare; no routine pneumococcal contact antibiotics
Pneumococcal, Hib and meningococcal vaccination; correct recurrent CSF leaks

rows.label: Mimics
items: SAH: thunderclap headache; CT/LP hemorrhagic findings
Encephalitis: parenchymal dysfunction, focal deficits or prominent behavioral change

meningitis.evidence: Contact prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [CDC meningococcal guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/surv-manual/php/table-of-contents/chapter-8-meningococcal-disease.html); empiric regimens established teaching.

menopause.name: Menopause
menopause.scope: Perimenopause, menopause transition, vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, HRT
menopause.core: Menopause is 12 months without menses from ovarian follicle depletion; manage bothersome symptoms according to uterine status and hormone-treatment risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Natural transition typically in late 40s–50s; smoking, oophorectomy, chemotherapy or pelvic radiation accelerate onset
Menopause before 40 suggests primary ovarian insufficiency and requires a separate evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Perimenopause: variable cycles, skipped periods, fertility remains; isolated irregularity → **reassurance**, no biopsy
Vasomotor episodes: abrupt heat, flushing, sweating, disturbed sleep; mood symptoms can coexist
Genitourinary syndrome: dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency and recurrent UTIs; pale thin friable mucosa
Urogenital estrogen loss: **negative cultures**, possible sterile pyuria; friable mucosa → spotting, postcoital bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ↓Follicles → ↓estradiol/inhibin and ↑FSH; hypothalamic thermoregulatory changes drive hot flashes
Urogenital estrogen deficiency thins epithelium, raises vaginal pH and changes flora

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms at **≥45 years → clinical diagnosis**; routine FSH unnecessary
Unexpected amenorrhea → pregnancy test; earlier menopause → FSH/estradiol and targeted thyroid/prolactin evaluation
Postmenopausal bleeding → endometrial evaluation; do not attribute to normal transition
Hormonal contraception alters bleeding/FSH interpretation; amenorrhea on contraception alone does not establish menopause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Bothersome hot flashes, low risk, generally <60 or within 10 years → **systemic estrogen**
★ Intact uterus → **add progestogen**; hysterectomy → estrogen alone usually sufficient
Avoid systemic hormones with unexplained bleeding, estrogen-sensitive cancer, prior VTE/stroke/MI or active liver disease
Hormones unsuitable → **venlafaxine, paroxetine or gabapentin**; selected fezolinetant requires liver monitoring
★ Isolated GSM → lubricants/moisturizers then **low-dose vaginal estrogen**; routine progestogen generally unnecessary

rows.label: Complications
items: Bone loss, fracture, sexual dysfunction; oral systemic estrogen increases VTE/stroke risk
Combined systemic hormones can increase breast cancer risk; unopposed uterine estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium/vitamin D, smoking cessation; age/risk-based osteoporosis screening
Hormone treatment not for primary cardiovascular/dementia prevention; reassess symptoms and risks periodically
Continue contraception during transition until menopause criteria met; menopausal hormones do not prevent pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent heat intolerance, tachycardia, suppressed TSH
Pregnancy: positive hCG despite irregular cycles

mesenteric-ischemia.name: Mesenteric ischemia
mesenteric-ischemia.scope: Acute mesenteric ischemia, chronic mesenteric ischemia, ischemic colitis, CTA abdomen, colonoscopy
mesenteric-ischemia.core: Intestinal hypoperfusion causes severe abdominal pain; early examination and lactate may appear deceptively reassuring.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: AF, recent MI, valvular disease → embolism; diffuse atherosclerosis → arterial thrombosis
Shock, heart failure, vasopressors → nonocclusive ischemia; hypercoagulability → mesenteric venous thrombosis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion** to abdominal examination; sudden onset especially with embolism
Nausea, diarrhea, later bloody stool; guarding/rebound suggests transmural infarction
Right-sided colonic disease or severe pain without bleeding → investigate proximal mesenteric occlusion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen supply failure injures mucosa before serosa; bacterial translocation and necrosis follow
Collateral flow usually protects intestine until acute major occlusion or multivessel chronic disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CTA abdomen/pelvis with arterial and venous phases** immediately for suspected acute ischemia
Do not delay lifesaving contrast imaging solely because of renal dysfunction
CBC, metabolic panel, lactate/ABG; **rising lactate** → severe hypoperfusion; normal early value does not exclude disease
Avoid colonoscopy with peritonitis, perforation, or suspected gangrene; minimal insufflation when safe

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute mesenteric: NPO, **IV saline, piperacillin-tazobactam, unfractionated heparin**; urgent vascular/surgical consult
★ **Peritonitis or infarcted bowel → emergency laparotomy**, resect nonviable bowel and restore flow
Arterial occlusion without peritonitis → urgent endovascular/open revascularization based on anatomy and expertise
Nonocclusive disease → restore perfusion, reduce vasoconstrictors; selected catheter-directed papaverine
Isolated mesenteric venous thrombosis without infarction → anticoagulation

rows.label: Complications
items: Bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis, multiorgan failure, death
Short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection; reperfusion injury, recurrent thrombosis
Ischemic colitis can heal with segmental stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Anticoagulate AF when eligible**; smoking cessation, statin, atherosclerotic risk reduction
Treat low-flow triggers promptly; thrombophilia evaluation for selected venous thrombosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infectious colitis: exposure/fever, stool pathogen identification
Pancreatitis: epigastric/back pain with lipase elevation
Perforated viscus: early rigid abdomen/free air; bowel obstruction: transition point on CT
Aortoenteric fistula: months-years after aortic graft, herald then massive upper GI bleed

table.title: Chronic disease versus colonic ischemia
rows: Postprandial pain, food fear, weight loss
Cramps then hematochezia; older, low-flow, post-AAA repair
Fluids, bowel rest; ceftriaxone/metronidazole if moderate/severe

mesenteric-ischemia.evidence: Colonic disease checked 2026-10-30: [ACG colon ischemia guideline](https://acgcdn.gi.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/ACG-Colon-Ischemia-Guideline-Summary.pdf); acute mesenteric treatment: established emergency framework.

metabolic-syndrome.name: Metabolic syndrome
metabolic-syndrome.scope: Diagnostic criteria (abdominal obesity, hypertension, impaired fasting glucose, hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL), insulin resistance pathophysiology, cardiovascular risk, lifestyle modifications
metabolic-syndrome.core: Cluster of central adiposity and cardiometabolic abnormalities identifying elevated diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sedentary lifestyle, excess caloric intake, aging, family history of type 2 diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ Visceral adiposity → insulin resistance, increased hepatic VLDL production and compensatory hyperinsulinemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Any 3 of 5** criteria; central obesity not mandatory; relevant treatment counts for metabolic criteria
Measure waist, blood pressure, fasting glucose and fasting lipid panel
Use population-specific waist thresholds where available

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Initial **weight loss and exercise**: target 5–10% weight loss and ≥150 minutes/week moderate activity
Mediterranean-style eating pattern; reduce refined carbohydrates and sugar-sweetened beverages
★ Treat individual risks: statin by ASCVD risk, antihypertensives by BP, diabetes therapy when diagnostic

rows.label: Complications
items: Type 2 diabetes, coronary disease, stroke, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reassess glycemia and cardiovascular risk over time; offer structured diabetes prevention for prediabetes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cushing syndrome: wide violaceous striae, easy bruising, proximal weakness
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH in primary disease

metabolic-syndrome.evidence: Checked American Heart Association metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria.

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production
Preterm birth → low stores, screen toddlers; infant microcytosis → **dietary history** for excess cow's milk

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV, preserved hemoglobin, high RBC count, **normal RDW** (Mentzer <13) suggest thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release; cytokines blunt **erythropoietin**
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead
Microcytosis + afebrile pain crisis, at-risk ancestry → **smear** for sickled cells (sickle–β-thalassemia)

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool
Four-gene α-deletion → **Hb Barts** (γ4) → severe fetal anemia, hydrops fetalis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

mood-stabilizers.name: Mood stabilizers
mood-stabilizers.scope: Lithium (therapeutic range, toxicity, hemodialysis, tremor, nephrogenic DI, hypothyroidism), valproate (hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, teratogenicity), carbamazepine, lamotrigine (Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
mood-stabilizers.core: Match the drug to bipolar phase; narrow therapeutic windows, organ toxicity, interactions, and pregnancy risks drive selection.

rows.label: Use
items: Lithium: mania, maintenance, reduced suicide risk; valproate/carbamazepine: acute mania
Lamotrigine: bipolar depression prevention; ineffective for acute mania

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Lithium alters intracellular signaling; anticonvulsants reduce excitatory neurotransmission

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Lithium: **nephrogenic DI**, hypothyroidism, hyperparathyroidism; fine tremor → **propranolol**
Valproate: hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, thrombocytopenia, weight gain
★ **Lamotrigine rash → stop immediately**; Stevens-Johnson risk increases with rapid titration

rows.label: Avoid
items: Valproate in pregnancy: neural tube defects, impaired neurodevelopment; carbamazepine also teratogenic
Lithium: severe renal impairment, dehydration; pregnancy counseling includes fetal cardiac risk

rows.label: Interactions
items: Thiazides, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, NSAIDs increase lithium; volume depletion worsens toxicity
Carbamazepine: CYP induction, reduced contraceptive efficacy; valproate increases lamotrigine levels

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Lithium **12-hour trough**: maintenance usually 0.6–1.0; acute mania 0.8–1.2 mEq/L
Renal function, TSH, calcium; valproate CBC/LFTs; carbamazepine CBC, sodium, LFTs
Carbamazepine: HLA-B*1502 testing with relevant Asian ancestry; agranulocytosis, SIADH, severe rash

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Lithium toxicity: coarse tremor, ataxia, confusion → stop lithium, IV saline
**Hemodialysis**: seizures/coma, life-threatening arrhythmia, or renal impairment with lithium >4 mEq/L
Consider dialysis: >5 mEq/L, confusion, or clearance >36 hours to <1; monitor rebound

multiple-gestation.name: Multiple gestation
multiple-gestation.scope: Dichorionic diamniotic (lambda sign), monochorionic diamniotic (T-sign), monochorionic monoamniotic, twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS), selective FGR, delivery timing recommendations
multiple-gestation.core: Chorionicity and amnionicity determine twin-specific surveillance, complications, and delivery timing; establish both on first-trimester ultrasound.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dizygotic twins: ovulation induction/assisted reproduction, maternal age, family history
Monozygotic splitting timing determines placental and sac sharing

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterus larger than dates, exaggerated pregnancy symptoms; ultrasound confirms fetal number
★ Shared placenta with **oligohydramnios/polyhydramnios sequence** → TTTS; small/absent donor bladder
Selective FGR: one small twin, discordant estimated weights; assess each umbilical artery Doppler

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental vascular anastomoses permit imbalanced flow in monochorionic twins
Donor hypovolemia reduces urine; recipient hypervolemia increases urine and cardiac strain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **First-trimester ultrasound** identifies shared placenta and intertwin membrane
Monochorionic diamniotic → ultrasound **every 2 weeks from 16 weeks** for fluid/bladders
Serial growth in all twins; Doppler and more frequent assessment when growth discordance develops
TTTS donor deepest pocket ≤2 cm, recipient ≥8 cm; staging incorporates bladder, Doppler, hydrops

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ TTTS stages II–IV at 16–26 weeks → **fetoscopic laser ablation** of placental anastomoses
Asymptomatic stage I → at least weekly surveillance; refer fetal intervention center if progression/symptoms
★ Diamniotic twins with **first twin cephalic** may deliver vaginally with experienced team
Monoamniotic twins → cesarean; fetal deterioration, preeclampsia, or severe growth issues may require earlier delivery

rows.label: Complications
items: Preterm birth, preeclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, postpartum hemorrhage
Monoamniotic cord entanglement; monochorionic co-twin death can cause surviving twin neurologic injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention; optimize iron/nutrition; single-embryo transfer reduces iatrogenic multiples

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates/macrosomia: enlarged uterus but singleton on imaging
Twin anemia-polycythemia sequence: discordant MCA velocities without major fluid imbalance

neonatal-resuscitation.name: Neonatal resuscitation
neonatal-resuscitation.scope: NRP algorithm, initial steps (warm, dry, stimulate), PPV indications (apnea, HR < 100), chest compressions (HR < 60), epinephrine, target SpO2
neonatal-resuscitation.core: At birth, effective ventilation drives heart-rate recovery; escalate support according to the response after each timed intervention.

rows.label: Definition
items: Apgar: appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration, each scored 0–2 at 1 and 5 min
Score 1: acrocyanosis, pulse <100, grimace, some flexion, irregular breathing

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Right-hand preductal pulse oximetry**; targets: 2 min 65–70%, 5 min 80–85%, 10 min 85–95%
Auscultate HR initially; ECG improves continuous measurement during advanced support
Oxygen start: ≥35 wk **21%**; 32–34 wk 21–30%; <32 wk 30–100%, titrated

rows.label: Use when
items: Vigorous term newborn → skin-to-skin, routine care; defer cord clamping ≥60 seconds
★ Poor tone/breathing → **warm, dry, position airway, stimulate**; initial assessment within first minute
Spontaneous breathing plus distress/cyanosis → oxygen titration; consider CPAP

rows.label: Compare
items: ★ Poor PPV → **reposition, reseal, open mouth, suction obstruction, raise pressure, alternate airway**
Compressions: two-thumb encircling technique, depth one-third chest; 90 compressions + 30 breaths/min
Epinephrine: **0.01–0.03 mg/kg IV/IO**; repeat every 3–5 min; umbilical venous access preferred

rows.label: Traps
items: No routine suction, including meconium; suction only suspected airway obstruction
★ **2025 PPV rate 30–60/min**; older teaching 40–60/min
Persistent bradycardia → check pneumothorax/hypovolemia; blood loss → saline or uncrossmatched blood

table.title: Timed escalation
rows: Stop compressions; continue ventilation if needed

neural-tube-defects.name: Neural tube defects
neural-tube-defects.scope: Anencephaly, spina bifida occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele, Chiari II malformation, maternal serum AFP, amniotic acetylcholinesterase, lemon and banana signs, folic acid prevention
neural-tube-defects.core: Neural tube closure failure by approximately 4 weeks after conception produces cranial or spinal defects; prevention must begin before pregnancy recognition.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low folate, prior affected pregnancy, maternal diabetes/obesity, valproate/carbamazepine, early-pregnancy hyperthermia

rows.label: Clues
items: Midline lumbosacral sac, lower-limb weakness, absent reflexes, bladder dysfunction with neural involvement
★ **Lemon skull and banana cerebellum** on fetal ultrasound suggest open spina bifida/Chiari II
Occult lesions: hair tuft, atypical deep dimple, hemangioma; normal skin does not guarantee normal cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failed neurulation leaves neural tissue unprotected; CSF leakage contributes to hindbrain herniation
Folate supports nucleotide synthesis during rapid embryonic cell division

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal serum **AFP at 15–22 weeks**; elevation → verify dating/number, detailed ultrasound
Open defects elevate AFP; closed occulta may not; cfDNA does not screen neural tube defects
★ Uncertain imaging → amniotic fluid **AFP and acetylcholinesterase**; target anatomy scan at 18–22 weeks
Postnatal spinal ultrasound in young infant or MRI for suspected occult dysraphism/tethered cord

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open spinal lesion: **prone positioning, sterile saline dressing**, avoid pressure/contamination; neonatal neurosurgery
Early closure; assess hydrocephalus, renal function and bladder emptying; intermittent catheterization when neurogenic
Selected prenatal myelomeningocele repair can improve motor outcomes/reduce shunting, with maternal and prematurity risks
Anencephaly → counseling, pregnancy options, and palliative neonatal care; no curative treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydrocephalus (Chiari II obstructs CSF), meningitis, orthopedic deformities, neurogenic bowel/bladder, recurrent UTI, kidney injury
Tethered cord may cause progressive weakness or continence changes during growth
Osteopenic insensate legs: new swelling → **X-ray** for occult fracture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Folic acid 400–800 µg/day** before conception through early pregnancy for average risk
Prior NTD pregnancy → **4 mg/day**, starting ≥1 month before conception through first 3 months
Optimize diabetes, review antiseizure drugs before pregnancy; avoid prolonged overheating

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: solid/cystic mass, not exposed neural placode
Abdominal wall defect: elevated AFP but bowel outside abdomen on ultrasound

table.title: Lesions
rows: Meninges/CSF herniate; cord remains within canal

neural-tube-defects.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [USPSTF 2023](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/ClinicalSummaryFinal/folic-acid-for-the-prevention-of-neural-tube-defects-preventive-medication); remaining content established teaching.

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.name: Neuromuscular junction disorders
neuromuscular-junction-disorders.scope: Myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, botulism, repetitive nerve stimulation, autoantibodies
neuromuscular-junction-disorders.core: Fluctuating or descending weakness with preserved sensation localizes to neuromuscular transmission; reflexes, pupils, and exercise response separate major causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: MG: autoimmune disease, thymoma; LEMS: smoking/small-cell lung carcinoma
Botulism: improperly canned foods, injection wounds, infant honey or environmental spores

rows.label: Clues
items: MG: diplopia, ptosis, nasal speech, chewing fatigue; worse late day or repeated activity
LEMS: proximal leg weakness, dry mouth, constipation; transient strength/reflex improvement after exertion
Botulism: cranial palsies → symmetric descending paralysis, autonomic dysfunction; infant constipation and floppy weakness
★ **Bulbar weakness or declining ventilation** → impending respiratory failure even with normal oxygen saturation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: MG: postsynaptic receptor/MuSK autoimmunity; LEMS: presynaptic voltage-gated calcium-channel autoimmunity
Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE proteins → impaired acetylcholine release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AChR antibodies**, then MuSK if negative; repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG
MG → chest CT for thymoma; bedside ice-pack improvement supports ocular disease
LEMS → P/Q calcium-channel antibodies and chest CT for cancer
★ Suspected crisis → serial **forced vital capacity/negative inspiratory force**; not pulse oximetry alone
Botulism → serum/stool/toxin testing via public health; treatment before confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: MG → pyridostigmine, steroid-sparing immunosuppression; thymectomy for thymoma or selected generalized AChR-positive disease
★ Myasthenic crisis → **airway support + IVIG or plasma exchange**, treat precipitant
LEMS → amifampridine and treatment of malignancy; immunotherapy for persistent autoimmune disease
★ Botulism → **heptavalent antitoxin**; infants → human botulism immune globulin; ventilatory support
Wound botulism → debridement/antibiotics; avoid aminoglycosides and magnesium with impaired junctional transmission

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, respiratory arrest; MG immunosuppression → infection; steroids may initially worsen weakness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review MG-exacerbating drugs; safe food preservation; no honey before age 1 year
LEMS → ongoing cancer surveillance if initial evaluation negative

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: usually ascending weakness and areflexia, possible sensory symptoms
Brainstem stroke: abrupt focal signs; motor neuron disease: fasciculations/UMN signs

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.evidence: Botulism checked 2026-10-30: [CDC clinical guidelines](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/70/rr/rr7002a1.htm); MG/LEMS: established teaching.

neutropenia.name: Neutropenia
neutropenia.scope: Benign ethnic neutropenia (Duffy-null), drug-induced neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, autoimmune neutropenia, ANC thresholds, evaluation and management
neutropenia.core: Infection risk tracks the depth and duration of neutrophil depletion; fever with severe neutropenia is an antibiotic emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cytotoxic chemotherapy, marrow malignancy, viral infection, autoimmune disease, B12/folate/copper deficiency
Clozapine, methimazole, propylthiouracil, TMP–SMX and other drugs can cause agranulocytosis
Duffy-null associated neutrophil counts: stable isolated reduction without increased infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral ulcers, gingivitis, recurrent bacterial/fungal infections; inflammatory signs and pus may be absent
Cyclic mouth ulcers/infections suggest cyclic neutropenia; multiple cytopenias suggest marrow disease
Drug-associated fever or sore throat → urgent CBC, especially with antithyroid drugs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced marrow production, peripheral destruction or splenic sequestration lowers circulating neutrophils
Mucosal barrier injury plus impaired innate defense permits rapid invasive bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANC = WBC × (% neutrophils + bands)/100**; repeat CBC with differential and smear
Mild: 1000–1500/µL; moderate: 500–1000; **severe <500**; profound <100
★ Febrile neutropenia: **≥38.3°C once or ≥38.0°C for ≥1 hour**, ANC <500 or expected decline
Obtain peripheral/line blood cultures, targeted cultures and imaging without delaying antibiotics
Persistent unexplained severe counts, abnormal smear or other cytopenias → marrow evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Febrile severe neutropenia → **IV cefepime**, piperacillin–tazobactam or meropenem promptly
Add vancomycin for shock, suspected line/skin infection, pneumonia or documented resistant gram-positive infection
★ Stop culprit drug; G-CSF for selected severe/drug-related cases and high-risk chemotherapy settings
Carefully selected low-risk stable patients → oral ciprofloxacin + amoxicillin–clavulanate with reliable close follow-up
High-risk persistent fever 4–7 days → fungal evaluation and empiric **caspofungin**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas sepsis, invasive candidiasis/aspergillosis, neutropenic enterocolitis; avoid rectal instrumentation
**Ecthyma gangrenosum**: bulla → painless black necrotic ulcer, Pseudomonas bacteremia; antipseudomonal drug, not steroids

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, oral care; selected prolonged profound neutropenia → antibacterial/antifungal prophylaxis
Stable Duffy-null pattern → reassurance after excluding other causes; no unnecessary G-CSF

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lymphopenia: opportunistic infection risk with preserved ANC
Acute leukemia: blasts and additional cytopenias

normal-pressure-hydrocephalus.name: Normal pressure hydrocephalus
normal-pressure-hydrocephalus.scope: Triad (gait apraxia/magnetic gait, cognitive impairment, urinary urgency/incontinence), ventriculomegaly on neuroimaging, high-volume lumbar puncture (Miller Fisher test), ventriculoperitoneal shunt
normal-pressure-hydrocephalus.core: An older adult develops a magnetic, short-stepped gait followed by slowed thinking and urinary urgency, with enlarged ventricles.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Often idiopathic in older adults; secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage, meningitis, head trauma

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Gait impairment first and most prominent**: initiation difficulty, broad base, unstable turns
Frontal-subcortical dysfunction: apathy, slowed processing, executive impairment rather than early isolated amnesia
Urinary urgency can precede incontinence; complete triad unnecessary
Prominent focal deficits, severe early memory loss, or resting tremor suggest another diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired CSF absorption → ventricular expansion and dysfunction of periventricular frontal-subcortical pathways
Lumbar opening pressure often normal despite disordered CSF dynamics

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Brain MRI or CT**: ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal atrophy; Evans index >0.3 supportive
MRI may show tight high-convexity sulci, enlarged Sylvian fissures and periventricular signal change
★ **High-volume LP, 30–50 mL**; compare standardized gait testing before and after drainage
Improvement supports shunt responsiveness; negative tap does not exclude—consider extended lumbar drainage
Exclude obstructive hydrocephalus and assess competing neurodegenerative/vascular disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Selected symptomatic candidates → **ventriculoperitoneal shunt**; gait most likely to improve
Rehabilitation, fall precautions, bladder support; counsel that advanced dementia improves less reliably
No established medication reverses idiopathic NPH

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated: falls, dependence; shunt infection, obstruction, overdrainage-related subdural hematoma
Recurrent symptoms after initial benefit → evaluate shunt malfunction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alzheimer disease: early episodic memory loss, proportional cortical atrophy
Parkinson disease: asymmetric bradykinesia/rigidity, resting tremor, levodopa response
Hydrocephalus ex vacuo: ventricles and sulci enlarge together from tissue loss

normal-pressure-hydrocephalus.evidence: Not checked online; established NPH evaluation and shunt-selection teaching.

nutritional-deficiencies.name: Nutritional deficiencies
nutritional-deficiencies.scope: Vegan diet nutrient risks, tea-and-toast diet, vitamin and mineral supplementation, clinical manifestations
nutritional-deficiencies.core: Restricted intake, malabsorption, or increased requirements produce characteristic mucocutaneous, neurologic, hematologic, and skeletal findings; identify the missing nutrient and its cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unsupplemented vegan diet: B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc risks
Tea-and-toast diet, alcohol misuse, food insecurity, restrictive eating, institutionalization
Bariatric surgery, pancreatic insufficiency, cholestasis, bowel disease → specific or fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor wound healing, bruising, oral changes, neuropathy, bone pain; mixed deficiencies commonly coexist
★ **Confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia** in malnutrition → thiamine deficiency; complete triad often absent
Night blindness → vitamin A; bleeding with prolonged PT → vitamin K
Dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia → niacin; periorificial/acral dermatitis, alopecia, dysgeusia → zinc (TPN, penicillamine)

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insufficient cofactors impair energy metabolism, collagen formation, hematopoiesis, or mineralization
Low intake differs from malabsorption: replacement route and lasting supplementation must match the mechanism
Vitamin D deficiency → ↓calcium absorption → **secondary hyperparathyroidism**: normal calcium at bone's expense

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diet and supplement history**, weight trend, oral/skin/neurologic examination; assess GI disease
CBC/ferritin, B12 ± methylmalonic acid, 25-OH vitamin D chosen by findings; avoid indiscriminate panels
Albumin is altered by inflammation/fluid status; not a stand-alone nutrition diagnostic test
Severely undernourished → baseline phosphate, Mg, K before nutritional rehabilitation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wernicke syndrome → **parenteral thiamine promptly**; do not await laboratory confirmation
B12 deficiency with neurologic signs/malabsorption → parenteral replacement; folate only after B12 assessment
Vitamin D/calcium for deficient intake or osteomalacia; iron replacement with evaluation for blood loss
Vitamin C for scurvy; oral balanced nutrition plus cause-directed supplementation and dietitian support
★ Severe malnutrition → **slow refeeding + thiamine**, close phosphate/K/Mg monitoring and replacement

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible B12 neurologic injury, fractures, anemia, infection susceptibility
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, arrhythmia, respiratory failure; excess vitamin A → hepatotoxicity/teratogenicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vegans → **reliable B12 supplementation**; fortified foods, calcium/vitamin D and iodine adequacy
Diversified diet, food access support, lifelong bariatric follow-up; avoid megadose supplementation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Scurvy versus vasculitis: perifollicular hemorrhage/corkscrew hairs, swollen bleeding gums, restricted produce intake
Hypothyroidism: fatigue and macrocytosis with elevated TSH

nutritional-deficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established nutritional deficiency and refeeding principles.

obsessive-compulsive-disorder.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
obsessive-compulsive-disorder.scope: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, ego-dystonic obsessions and compulsions, exposure and response prevention, SSRIs
obsessive-compulsive-disorder.core: Intrusive unwanted thoughts and ritualized acts consume time or impair function; treatment breaks the cycle of anxiety and neutralization.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Often begins in childhood/adolescence; family history, tic disorders, anxiety/depression comorbidity
Stress may worsen symptoms; intrusive harm/sexual thoughts do not alone imply intent

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Ego-dystonic obsessions**: contamination, doubt, symmetry, aggressive or taboo thoughts
Compulsions: washing, checking, counting or mental rituals aimed at preventing feared outcomes
Usually recognizes excessiveness, but insight ranges to absent; reassurance seeking can function as a ritual
Skin injury from washing, lateness or avoidance; severe cases markedly restrict eating or daily activity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical dysfunction; rituals transiently reduce distress and are negatively reinforced

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical interview**: obsessions/compulsions >1 hour daily or significant distress/impairment
Assess insight, functional effect, suicidality, tics and depression; Yale-Brown scale tracks severity
Exclude substances/medical causes and distinguish repetitive behaviors driven by other disorders

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT with exposure and response prevention**: graded feared-stimulus exposure without ritual completion
★ **SSRI**, e.g., sertraline/fluoxetine; mild-moderate pediatric OCD → ERP alone first; substantial impairment → combine
Often higher tolerated SSRI doses and 8–12-week trial needed; do not label failure after brief exposure
Persistent symptoms → optimize ERP/adherence, switch SSRI or clomipramine; selected resistant disease → risperidone
Reduce family accommodation/reassurance rituals; maintain effective treatment before gradual taper

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, suicidality, social/occupational disability; dermatitis from compulsive washing
Clomipramine → anticholinergic effects, arrhythmia and overdose risk; SSRI → sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Generalized anxiety: realistic everyday worries rather than intrusive obsession/neutralization cycle
Psychosis: fixed belief without typical resisted ritual; assess insight carefully

table.title: Related repetitive patterns
rows: Developmental social differences, soothing stereotyped routines
Brief involuntary movement/sound with premonitory urge

opioid-toxicity.name: Opioid toxicity
opioid-toxicity.scope: Opioid toxidrome, naloxone administration and titration, observation period, precipitated withdrawal
opioid-toxicity.core: Depressed consciousness, slow breathing, and pinpoint pupils after opioid exposure; ventilation takes priority over full awakening.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fentanyl or heroin exposure, dose escalation, renal dysfunction, long-acting opioids
Alcohol/benzodiazepine co-ingestion; lost tolerance after detoxification, hospitalization, or incarceration

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Bradypnea or apnea** with hypoxemia; reduced bowel sounds, bradycardia, hypotension
Miosis may be absent with severe hypoxia or co-ingestion; needle marks are not required
Pulmonary edema, aspiration, hypothermia, prolonged immobilization may accompany overdose
Chronic use: daytime sleepiness, constipation, apathy, falling grades, miosis, slow breathing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mu-receptor activation suppresses medullary ventilatory response to CO2
Naloxone competitively reverses opioid effects but often wears off before the causative opioid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; bedside glucose, pulse oximetry, capnography; do not await toxicology
Urine opiate immunoassay detects morphine/heroin/codeine; may miss fentanyl, methadone, and oxycodone
ECG for methadone-associated QT prolongation; acetaminophen level with uncertain combination-product ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open airway, **bag-mask ventilation**, oxygen; intubate if ventilation cannot be maintained
★ **Naloxone** IV titrated to adequate breathing; intranasal/IM route if IV unavailable
Dependent but breathing: start low; apnea/no response: prompt larger/repeated doses, especially fentanyl analogs
Repeated recurrence → naloxone infusion; coma despite repeated doses → evaluate additional causes
Short-acting reversal: observe ≥4 hours after last naloxone; long-acting/recurrent sedation → prolonged monitoring/admission

rows.label: Complications
items: Anoxic brain injury, aspiration pneumonia, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome
Precipitated withdrawal: agitation, vomiting, diarrhea, tachycardia; rare pulmonary edema after reversal

rows.label: Prevention
items: Take-home naloxone, overdose-response training, avoid sedative combinations; offer buprenorphine and addiction follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pontine hemorrhage: focal neurologic findings, no meaningful naloxone response
Clonidine poisoning: marked bradycardia with similar pupils
Sedative overdose: usually normal pupils; incomplete naloxone response

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.scope: Clinical diagnosis (Heberden/Bouchard nodes, activity-related pain), radiographic findings, nonpharmacologic therapy, oral and topical NSAIDs, injections
osteoarthritis.core: Activity-related joint pain with brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement suggests degenerative joint disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, **obesity** (strongest modifiable), prior trauma, malalignment, repetitive occupational loading
Family history, particularly hand disease; obesity affects both mechanical and metabolic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning stiffness generally **<30 minutes**; pain improves with rest early in disease
Knees, hips, first carpometacarpal, DIP and PIP commonly involved; MCP usually spared
Heberden nodes: DIP; Bouchard nodes: PIP; reduced motion and varus/valgus deformity
Hip disease: groin pain with restricted internal rotation; referred pain can localize to knee

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Articular cartilage loss, subchondral remodeling and osteophytes; low-grade synovial inflammation
Joint pain arises from innervated surrounding structures rather than aneural cartilage itself

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical presentation → **clinical diagnosis**; imaging unnecessary for straightforward mild disease
Weight-bearing radiographs if uncertain, severe or worsening: asymmetric joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts
★ Hot acutely swollen joint → **arthrocentesis**; not an OA flare; mild cool effusion → x-ray, simple analgesic
OA fluid noninflammatory: usually WBC <2000/µL; inflammatory markers generally normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **exercise, strengthening, weight loss**; cane contralateral to painful hip/knee
★ Knee/hand pain → **topical diclofenac**; oral NSAID if insufficient and renal/GI/CV risks acceptable
Acetaminophen if unable to use NSAIDs (older exam questions may expect it first); duloxetine for persistent pain
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for short-term relief; avoid routine opioids and hyaluronic acid injections
Severe pain/function loss despite conservative treatment → **joint replacement**

rows.label: Complications
items: Functional limitation, falls, reduced activity and secondary deconditioning
NSAIDs → GI bleeding, AKI, fluid retention; arthroplasty → infection or VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Weight loss** best prevents knee OA, beyond exercise alone; conditioning, injury prevention; no complete joint rest

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rheumatoid arthritis: prolonged stiffness, boggy symmetric MCP/wrist synovitis, marginal erosions, DIP spared
CPPD: acute inflammatory flares, chondrocalcinosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe painful passive motion, positive synovial culture
Trochanteric bursitis: lateral hip pain over greater trochanter, not groin pain
