osteoarthritis.evidence: Not checked online; established ACR/Arthritis Foundation principles.

osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis
osteoporosis.scope: DEXA scan T-score criteria, screening guidelines, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, bisphosphonates
osteoporosis.core: Fragility fracture or markedly reduced bone density identifies skeletal weakness, often silent until hip or vertebral fracture.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Postmenopause, older age, White/Asian ancestry, BMI <20, parental fragility hip fracture, smoking, alcohol >2 drinks/day
Glucocorticoids, early or surgical menopause, hypogonadism, malabsorption, hyperthyroidism, immobility, rheumatoid arthritis

rows.label: Clues
items: Height loss, kyphosis, acute back pain with **midline point tenderness** after trivial strain suggest vertebral compression
Neurologic deficits, fever, or nocturnal pain suggest alternative spinal pathology

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bone resorption exceeds formation; microarchitecture deteriorates despite normally mineralized remaining bone
Estrogen deficiency increases osteoclast activity; steroids suppress osteoblasts and reduce calcium balance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Hip/spine DXA**; use T-scores in postmenopausal women and men ≥50
★ Hip/vertebral low-trauma fracture establishes diagnosis regardless of DXA; acute vertebral pain → **spine x-ray** before DXA
CBC, calcium, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, 25-OH vitamin D; targeted secondary-cause testing
Younger adults: Z-score ≤−2 suggests below-age bone density; T-score alone insufficient

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Alendronate or zoledronic acid** for qualifying fracture, osteoporosis-range DXA, or high FRAX risk; raloxifene/estrogen contraindicated after VTE
Osteopenia: treat if 10-year hip risk ≥3% or major osteoporotic risk ≥20%
Oral bisphosphonate: fasting water, remain upright; avoid esophageal disease, hypocalcemia, severe kidney dysfunction
Very high risk → teriparatide/romosozumab then antiresorptive; stopping denosumab requires follow-on antiresorptive
Vertebral pain: analgesia, mobilization, short bracing; procedures reserved for selected refractory cases

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ **Hip fracture** → immobility, thromboembolism, excess mortality
Bisphosphonates: rare jaw osteonecrosis/atypical femur fracture; denosumab: hypocalcemia, rebound vertebral fractures

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen **women ≥65**, younger postmenopausal women at increased risk; evidence insufficient for routine male screening
**Smoking cessation**, less heavy alcohol outrank supplements; weight-bearing/resistance exercise, fall prevention, dietary calcium/vitamin D
Prednisone-equivalent ≥2.5 mg/day for >3 months → fracture-risk assessment; prevent with **alendronate**, not estrogen/raloxifene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomalacia: defective mineralization, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase
Myeloma: anemia, renal injury, lytic lesions; metastatic fracture: destructive focal lesion

osteoporosis.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2025](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/osteoporosis-screening%20); treatment: established fracture-risk framework.

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea permissible despite risks; reassess sedation/respiration
Codeine fails → morphine/oxycodone; pain mimics depression; wears off early → shorten interval

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids**, short-acting for breakthrough; constipation → keep dose, add stimulant laxative

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals
Advanced dementia refusing intake → comfort hand-feeding by mouth; no tubes or IV

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Hospice: unrelated conditions remain treatable; no DNR requirement; enrollment revocable if goals change
Cancer pain: escalating requests → tolerance/progression, not addiction; past OUD never limits analgesia

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

table.title: Care settings
rows: Adjust with hospice team; avoid readmission

pancreatic-cancer.name: Pancreatic cancer
pancreatic-cancer.scope: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, painless jaundice, Courvoisier sign, CA 19-9, neuroendocrine tumors (gastrinoma, insulinoma)
pancreatic-cancer.core: Older adult with weight loss and painless obstructive jaundice, or persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, chronic pancreatitis, obesity, increasing age; strong family history, hereditary cancer syndromes
New diabetes with unexplained weight loss can signal occult malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Head lesions: dark urine, pale stools, pruritus, nontender palpable gallbladder (**Courvoisier sign**)
Body/tail lesions: late presentation with pain and cachexia; migratory thrombophlebitis may occur

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ductal adenocarcinoma causes biliary obstruction, perineural invasion, and early metastatic spread
Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors arise from endocrine cells; may be functional or incidental

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pancreatic-protocol CT** for mass, vessels, metastases; ultrasound may show **double-duct** (bile + pancreatic) dilation
EUS biopsy before systemic treatment/uncertain diagnosis; not mandatory before straightforward resection
★ **CA 19-9** monitors disease; neither screening nor definitive diagnosis; obstruction can falsely elevate
Resectability depends on metastases and major vascular involvement; MRI clarifies indeterminate liver lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Resectable head tumor → **Whipple**; body/tail tumor → distal pancreatectomy; add systemic chemotherapy
Borderline resectable → neoadjuvant treatment; metastatic → systemic treatment and palliation
★ Cholangitis → **urgent ERCP**; unresectable symptomatic jaundice → biliary stent
Analgesia, pancreatic enzymes for malabsorption, nutritional support

rows.label: Complications
items: VTE, biliary infection, gastric outlet obstruction, exocrine insufficiency, diabetes
Resection → pancreatic fistula, delayed gastric emptying, malabsorption

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation; no average-risk population screening; selected hereditary high-risk patients → MRI/EUS surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Choledocholithiasis: colicky pain, ductal stone
Autoimmune pancreatitis: IgG4 elevation, diffuse pancreatic enlargement
Chronic pancreatitis: calcification, recurrent pain, prior inflammation

table.title: Functional neuroendocrine tumors
rows: ↑Insulin/C-peptide during supervised fast; negative sulfonylurea screen
Massive watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, achlorhydria, flushing

pancreatic-cancer.evidence: Not checked online; established pancreatic oncology teaching.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones (prior postprandial biliary colic), heavy alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease
Blunt abdominal trauma + epigastric mass/raised enzymes → contrast CT for pancreatic/duodenal injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue: ↓insulin, ↓glucagon, normal insulin sensitivity; lipase may normalize

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase or amylase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT: diagnostic doubt, high fever/marked leukocytosis (necrosis?), deterioration, no improvement by 48–72 hours; not routine early
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency
Recurrent, no gallstones/alcohol → EUS or MRCP for ductal anatomy; older exam questions may expect ERCP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, reassessment, IV opioid analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** by 48 hours if tolerated; else enteral; older exam questions may expect initial bowel rest
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Uncomplicated/sterile: no antibiotics; infected necrosis: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancrelipase, fat-soluble vitamins, pain control; islet-loss diabetes → **insulin**, not sulfonylureas

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; necrosis, hemorrhage; **splenic vein thrombosis** → isolated gastric varices, normal liver
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

parasitic-infections.name: Parasitic infections
parasitic-infections.scope: Strongyloidiasis, giardiasis, amebiasis, cryptosporidiosis, ascariasis, schistosomiasis, pinworm (enterobiasis), cysticercosis, eosinophilia workup, antiparasitic therapy
parasitic-infections.core: Exposure, organ pattern, and immune status identify the parasite; eosinophilia favors tissue-invasive helminths rather than intestinal protozoa.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Contaminated food/water, endemic travel, freshwater contact, barefoot soil exposure, household crowding
Steroids/HTLV-1 predispose to Strongyloides hyperinfection; advanced HIV predisposes to persistent cryptosporidiosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Ascariasis: transient cough/eosinophilic infiltrates during larval migration; later intestinal or biliary obstruction
Pinworm: nocturnal perianal/vulvar itch, dysuria with normal UA; household clustering
Cysticercosis: seizures or hydrocephalus; ingestion of **T. solium eggs**, not pork cysts
Cutaneous larva migrans: soil contact; pruritic **serpiginous tracks**; animal hookworm larvae → albendazole or ivermectin

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Giardia blunts microvilli → **fat/carbohydrate malabsorption**; invasive protozoa can affect liver, urinary tract, or CNS
Strongyloides autoinfection permits lifelong persistence and dissemination after immunosuppression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unexplained **eosinophilia** → travel/drug history, serial stool O&P, targeted Strongyloides serology
★ Steroids + eosinophilia or infiltrates → **Strongyloides hyperinfection**: **duodenal aspirate** larvae; stool O&P often misses
Diarrhea → stool antigen/PCR for protozoa; single routine O&P can miss infection
★ Pinworm → **morning tape test** before washing; stool testing insensitive
Brain MRI/CT for cysticercosis; eye examination before antiparasitics; assess lesion viability and location

rows.label: Tx
items: Rehydrate; ascariasis → albendazole; bowel obstruction → surgical evaluation before deworming
Pinworm → albendazole, mebendazole, or pyrantel; repeat after **2 weeks**, treat household simultaneously
★ Viable parenchymal cysticercosis → albendazole ± praziquantel with corticosteroids; seizures → levetiracetam
Calcified brain lesions → no antiparasitic; hydrocephalus → neurosurgical control before cysticidal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Strongyloides hyperinfection → gram-negative sepsis, respiratory failure; eosinophilia may disappear
Amebic liver abscess; schistosomiasis → portal hypertension or bladder squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen/treat Strongyloides before **immunosuppression** after endemic exposure
Safe water, sanitation, handwashing, footwear; avoid endemic freshwater and untreated swimming water
Neurocysticercosis household contacts → **stool O&P** to find egg-shedding T. solium tapeworm carrier

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea after infection excluded
Drug hypersensitivity: eosinophilia linked to new medication, rash or organ injury

table.title: Exposure → diagnosis and treatment
rows: Camping; greasy stool, bloating; stool antigen
Dysentery, flask-shaped ulcers; stool PCR; abscess → serology
Soil; larva currens, larvae in stool
Ivermectin; hyperinfection requires prolonged daily treatment
Freshwater; hematuria (haematobium), portal fibrosis (mansoni/japonicum); eggs, serology
Confirmed E. histolytica without invasive disease

parasomnias.name: Parasomnias
parasomnias.scope: REM sleep behavior disorder (polysomnography, clonazepam), sleep terrors, sleepwalking (somnambulism), nightmare disorder, isolated sleep paralysis, reassurance
parasomnias.core: Unusual behavior or experiences during sleep are classified by timing, recall, and whether REM muscle atonia is lost or persists.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sleep deprivation, stress, fever, alcohol, OSA precipitate NREM arousals
REM behavior disorder: older men, synucleinopathies, SSRIs; sleepwalking/terrors often childhood

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Dream enactment with injury** → ask bed partner about kicking, punching, falling from bed
Isolated sleep paralysis: conscious but briefly unable to move at sleep onset or awakening

rows.label: Pathophys
items: NREM disorders: incomplete arousal from deep sleep; REM behavior disorder: loss of normal skeletal atonia
Sleep paralysis: REM atonia persists into wakefulness

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected REM behavior disorder → **video polysomnography** demonstrating REM without atonia
Typical childhood NREM events: clinical; atypical stereotyped episodes → video EEG/PSG
Assess snoring, sleep schedule, drugs, trauma, daytime sleep attacks

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ REM behavior disorder: **immediate-release melatonin or clonazepam**; melatonin favored with falls/OSA concerns
Sleep terrors/walking: reassurance, adequate sleep, scheduled awakenings for predictable frequent events
Nightmares: imagery rehearsal; trauma-associated nightmares → assess PTSD
Isolated paralysis: reassurance, regular sleep; accompanying cataplexy → evaluate narcolepsy

rows.label: Complications
items: Injury to sleeper/partner; clonazepam can worsen sedation, balance, sleep-disordered breathing
REM behavior disorder may precede Parkinson disease, Lewy body dementia, or multiple system atrophy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Safe bedroom**: remove weapons, pad furniture, secure windows; separate sleeping if violent
Avoid sleep deprivation/alcohol; treat OSA; review triggering antidepressants

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nocturnal seizures: brief stereotyped clusters, possible postictal findings
OSA: gasping arousals tied to obstructive respiratory events

table.title: Timing and recall
rows: Awake, oriented, detailed frightening dream recall

patient-confidentiality.name: Patient confidentiality
patient-confidentiality.scope: HIPAA, exceptions to confidentiality, Tarasoff duty to protect, mandatory reporting vs law enforcement requests, substance use privacy, subpoena vs court order
patient-confidentiality.core: Protect identifiable health information unless authorized by the patient or a specific legal basis permits disclosure.

rows.label: Principle
items: HIPAA permits treatment, payment, and health care operations disclosures without authorization

rows.label: Do
items: Verify authority, document rationale, and disclose minimum necessary information when applicable

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Police request alone → no chart release; confirm a specific lawful basis

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Report suspected child abuse and designated infections under state law
★ Tarasoff: serious threat → warn target, notify police, or hospitalize as state law requires

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Court order** → specified records only; civil subpoena alone generally insufficient
★ **Part 2 SUD records**: legal use against patient requires consent or order plus subpoena
Adult with capacity controls routine disclosures to family

patient-confidentiality.evidence: Checked HHS HIPAA Privacy Rule and 42 CFR Part 2 final rule (2024).

pericardial-disease.name: Pericardial disease
pericardial-disease.scope: Acute pericarditis, pericardial effusion, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis
pericardial-disease.core: Pericardial inflammation, fluid accumulation, or fibrosis produces distinct chest-pain and impaired-filling syndromes; hemodynamic effect depends on accumulation rate.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Viral/idiopathic, autoimmune disease, uremia, malignancy, TB, radiation, cardiac surgery
Early post-MI inflammation or delayed immune-mediated Dressler syndrome; trauma/anticoagulation can cause hemopericardium

rows.label: Clues
items: Pericarditis: sharp pleuritic positional pain, better leaning forward; friction rub may be transient
★ Tamponade: **hypotension, elevated JVP, muffled sounds**, pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg; triad often incomplete
Constrictive disease: edema/ascites, Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, prominent y descent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflamed surfaces cause pain; fluid or scar limits diastolic filling and stroke volume
Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures; constriction exaggerates ventricular interdependence with respiration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pericarditis: ≥2 of **typical pain, rub, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, new effusion**
Troponin elevation suggests myocardial involvement; CRP supports inflammation; echo assesses fluid and ventricular function
★ **Urgent bedside echo** for suspected tamponade: right-sided chamber collapse, plethoric IVC
Constrictive suspicion → echo, CT/MRI for thickening/calcification; catheterization if diagnosis remains uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tamponade → **urgent pericardiocentesis**; IV fluids bridge; avoid diuresis/positive-pressure ventilation
Purulent, traumatic, malignant, or recurrent effusion → surgical drainage/window; antibiotics for bacterial cause
Stable effusion → treat cause, serial echo; low voltage alone never determines drainage
High-risk features → admit: fever, large effusion, immunosuppression, anticoagulation, subacute onset, NSAID failure
Early post-cardiac-surgery tamponade → **urgent mediastinal re-exploration**

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent inflammation, arrhythmia/myocarditis, obstructive shock; procedural drainage → cardiac injury
Rapid decompression can rarely cause ventricular dysfunction; NSAIDs → GI/renal injury, colchicine → diarrhea

rows.label: Prevention
items: Colchicine course: first episode 3 months; recurrence ≥6 months; taper anti-inflammatory drugs after remission
Exercise restriction until clinical/inflammatory resolution; optimize dialysis for uremic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: STEMI: regional ST elevation with reciprocal changes; urgent coronary evaluation if uncertain
Restrictive cardiomyopathy: myocardial disease, less respiratory ventricular discordance
PE: thrombotic risk, acute RV strain

table.title: Nonemergency definitive management
rows: Ibuprofen + colchicine; aspirin preferred after MI
Selected low-dose glucocorticoid or IL-1 blockade

perioperative-care.name: Perioperative care
perioperative-care.scope: Preoperative cardiac risk, pulmonary evaluation, surgical antibiotic prophylaxis, medication management, pain control
perioperative-care.core: Optimize active disease, estimate procedural and patient risk, and order testing only when the result could change perioperative management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **MI within 60 days**, decompensated HF → highest perioperative cardiac risk; older exam questions may expect MI within 6 months
Emergency, vascular or intrathoracic surgery; ischemic heart disease, heart failure, CKD, diabetes
Smoking, COPD, OSA, frailty, malnutrition and prior anesthesia complications

rows.label: Clues
items: Chest pain, new dyspnea, syncope or decompensated fluid overload require targeted evaluation
Poor functional capacity: inability to climb stairs or perform activities around 4 METs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Surgical stress raises myocardial oxygen demand; anesthesia can lower perfusion pressure
Sedation, pain and recumbency reduce ventilation and promote atelectasis and venous stasis
Surgical stress, pain, opioids → nonosmotic **ADH** release → transient oliguria with normal renal function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RCRI/NSQIP** plus functional assessment; no routine stress test for low-risk surgery
Elevated risk, poor/unknown capacity → stress test if management changes; cannot exercise → **pharmacologic stress imaging**
ECG for cardiovascular symptoms; echo for new/worsening HF or suspected significant valve disease
No routine chest radiograph/spirometry without respiratory findings; assess airway and OSA history
Lung resection: **predicted postoperative FEV1** best predictor of complications; predicted postoperative FEV1 <30–40% → high risk, exercise testing before deciding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Active ACS, decompensated HF or unstable arrhythmia → defer elective surgery and stabilize
★ Continue chronic **beta blockers/statins**; do not start beta blockade on surgery day
Hold **SGLT2 inhibitors 3–4 days**; individualize GLP-1 drugs by aspiration risk; continue reduced basal insulin
★ **Cefazolin within 60 minutes** before incision; MRSA or severe beta-lactam allergy → vancomycin within 120 minutes
Multimodal analgesia: acetaminophen, regional block, selective NSAID; add opioid by severity, respiratory monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Myocardial injury, AKI, delirium, pneumonia, VTE and surgical-site infection
Opioids aggravate OSA; excessive fluids can worsen pulmonary edema
New postoperative dyspnea, ↓basal breath sounds → chest radiograph first, before PE imaging or heparin

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, lung expansion exercises, early mobilization, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis
Anticoagulation interruption individualized; bridging reserved for highest thrombotic risk
Chronic steroid exposure with adrenal suppression → perioperative glucocorticoid coverage
Usable gut → **enteral feeding**, including distal jejunostomy, over TPN

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anxiety-related dyspnea: normal cardiopulmonary evaluation
Stable chronic disease: baseline symptoms alone do not mandate cancellation

table.title: Postoperative pain
rows: Severe pain after major abdominal surgery

pertussis.name: Pertussis
pertussis.scope: Bordetella pertussis, catarrhal, paroxysmal, and convalescent stages, posttussive emesis, inspiratory whoop, macrolide therapy, postexposure prophylaxis, Tdap vaccination
pertussis.core: Prolonged paroxysmal cough with posttussive emesis; infants may present with apnea and cyanosis without a whoop.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unvaccinated/undervaccinated children, waning immunity in adolescents/adults, infected household contacts
Young infants have greatest risk of severe disease; vaccinated individuals can still transmit infection

rows.label: Clues
items: Catarrhal stage: rhinorrhea, mild cough, little or no fever; greatest early infectiousness
Inspiratory whoop often absent in adolescents/adults; convalescence can last weeks with recurrent cough
★ Infant **marked lymphocytosis**, poor feeding, or respiratory compromise; minimal fever despite serious illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: B. pertussis adheres to respiratory cilia; toxin-mediated injury impairs mucus clearance
Pertussis toxin inhibits Gi signaling; impaired lymphocyte extravasation causes circulating lymphocytosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Nasopharyngeal PCR** during first 3–4 weeks of cough; posterior nasopharynx, not throat swab
Culture most useful in first 2 weeks; late illness → validated serology when available
Treat suspected high-risk cases before results; chest imaging for respiratory compromise or suspected pneumonia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Azithromycin** preferred; TMP-SMX alternative at age ≥2 months when macrolides unsuitable
Best symptom benefit early; later treatment mainly reduces transmission within infectious window
Treat age ≥1 year within 3 weeks of cough; infants/pregnancy up to 6 weeks
Hospitalize young infants or apnea/hypoxemia; oxygen, suction, hydration and cardiorespiratory monitoring
Infant macrolides carry pyloric stenosis risk, but benefit outweighs risk; monitor vomiting

rows.label: Complications
items: Pneumonia, seizures/encephalopathy, infant pulmonary hypertension and death
Adults: rib fractures, syncope, stress incontinence from forceful coughing

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Droplet isolation until **5 days of effective antibiotics**, or 21 days from cough onset untreated
Household contacts → azithromycin prophylaxis within 21 days of index cough; also target high-risk exposures
DTaP childhood series; Tdap adolescent booster and once for adults without prior Tdap
★ **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 weeks**, preferably early in that interval

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral bronchitis: improving ordinary cough without characteristic paroxysms or epidemiologic link
Asthma: recurrent wheeze/trigger pattern, reversible airflow obstruction
Chlamydial infant pneumonia: afebrile staccato cough, eosinophilia, often prior conjunctivitis

phobias.name: Phobias
phobias.scope: Specific phobia (flying, heights, blood-injection-injury), exposure therapy, situational benzodiazepines, social anxiety disorder (generalized vs performance-only), beta-blockers, agoraphobia
phobias.core: Persistent disproportionate fear leads to avoidance or endurance with intense distress, producing impairment despite recognition that danger is limited.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Temperamental inhibition, family anxiety, frightening experiences or learned fear; often childhood/adolescent onset

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fear reliably provoked by trigger; duration **≥6 months**, excessive relative to actual/cultural danger
Anticipatory anxiety and avoidance limit school, work, medical care or travel
Blood-injection-injury subtype may produce vasovagal syncope rather than persistent tachycardia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Conditioned threat response and avoidance prevent extinction; relief from escape reinforces fear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical assessment** of trigger, feared consequence, avoidance and impairment
Agoraphobia: fear in ≥2 categories—transport, open/enclosed spaces, crowds/lines, outside home alone
Exclude substances, hyperthyroidism, arrhythmia or pulmonary disease when bodily symptoms atypical
Symptoms only with feared trigger, normal exam → psychiatric evaluation, not pheochromocytoma/Holter workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Graded exposure-based CBT** first-line across phobic disorders
Blood-injection-injury: applied muscle tension during exposure reduces fainting
Generalized social anxiety: CBT or sertraline/escitalopram; venlafaxine alternative
★ Performance-only social anxiety → situational **propranolol**; asthma/bradycardia → short-acting benzodiazepine instead
Rare trigger (flight, MRI) → short-acting benzodiazepine (**↑GABA-A**); routine use risks dependence, impairs exposure

rows.label: Complications
items: Social/occupational restriction, depression, substance misuse; avoidance of necessary health care
Beta-blocker hypotension; benzodiazepine sedation, falls, impaired driving

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early treatment, repeated graduated practice and reduced avoidance help maintain gains
Avoid self-medication with alcohol; include relapse-prevention exposure plans

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: recurrent unexpected attacks; fear of further attacks
OCD: intrusive obsessions and rituals drive avoidance
Avoidant personality: pervasive longstanding inadequacy/rejection sensitivity, often coexists with social anxiety

phobias.evidence: Social anxiety care checked 2026-10-30: [NIMH](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/social-anxiety-disorder-more-than-just-shyness); established exposure-based care.

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced fremitus; large effusion shifts mediastinum away; unilateral + cancer history → malignant
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid/empyema
Bloody fluid: malignancy (prior cancer, mediastinal mass), embolism, trauma; milky → chyle
Foul-smelling pus after aspiration → **anaerobic empyema**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage
Heart-failure transudate: pleural protein <3 g/dL, low LDH and cell count; **glucose equals serum**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive Gram stain/culture, **pH <7.20** or glucose <60 → empyema/complicated: chest tube, antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

polycystic-ovary-syndrome.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.scope: Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovaries), metabolic risks, weight loss, oral contraceptives, ovulation induction (letrozole, clomiphene)
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.core: Hyperandrogenism and chronic ovulatory dysfunction after exclusion of alternative causes suggest PCOS; management follows metabolic, menstrual and fertility priorities.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, insulin resistance and obesity; lean patients can also have PCOS
Pubertal transition can mimic disease, requiring stricter adolescent diagnostic criteria

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/infrequent menses, episodic heavy bleeding, infertility, hirsutism, acne or androgenic alopecia
Acanthosis nigricans suggests hyperinsulinemia; obesity is supportive, not required
Rapid virilization, deep voice or markedly elevated androgens → investigate tumor rather than assume PCOS

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin resistance and ovarian androgen excess impair follicular maturation and ovulation
Absent cyclic progesterone permits persistent estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Adults: **2 of 3 Rotterdam** features—hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovarian morphology
Exclude mimics: **hCG, TSH, prolactin, morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone**; latter screens nonclassic CAH
Total/free testosterone; **clinical hirsutism/acne** suffices despite normal levels; DHEAS if adrenal source suspected
★ Irregular cycles plus hyperandrogenism → **ultrasound not required**; LH:FSH ratio not diagnostic
BP, lipid profile and **oral glucose tolerance test** assess metabolic risk; adolescent diagnosis avoids ultrasound criteria

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Lifestyle/weight management first for all; modest weight loss can restore ovulation in overweight patients
★ No pregnancy desired → **combined OCP** for cycles/androgen symptoms; cyclic progestin or LNG-IUD protects endometrium
Persistent hirsutism → spironolactone with reliable contraception; allow months for hair response
Metabolic risk/insulin resistance → metformin; less effective than OCP for androgen symptoms
★ Anovulatory infertility → **letrozole first-line**; clomiphene alternative, older exams may expect it; check other factors

rows.label: Complications
items: Endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, OSA and depression
Pregnancy → increased gestational diabetes and hypertensive-disorder risk
Gonadotropin ovulation induction → high multiple-gestation risk, so letrozole/clomiphene first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for prolonged amenorrhea; persistent abnormal bleeding → endometrial assessment
Periodic glycemic/BP/lipid reassessment; preconception metabolic optimization and folate

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen-secreting tumor: rapid progression, severe virilization
Nonclassic CAH: elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low estrogen with exercise/energy deficit

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

proteinuria.name: Proteinuria
proteinuria.scope: Transient proteinuria, orthostatic (postural) proteinuria, persistent proteinuria, split urine collection, spot protein-to-creatinine ratio, nephrology referral
proteinuria.core: Incidental urinary protein requires confirmation and quantification; persistence, sediment, renal function, and blood pressure distinguish benign variants from kidney disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Transient: fever, strenuous exercise, dehydration, seizures; orthostatic pattern common in adolescent males
Persistent: diabetes, hypertension, glomerulonephritis, systemic autoimmune disease, hereditary nephropathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic; foamy urine and periorbital/dependent edema suggest heavier losses
★ **Hematuria, hypertension, RBC casts, reduced eGFR**, or systemic rash/arthritis → pathologic renal process

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Glomerular permeability → albumin leakage; impaired tubular reabsorption → smaller proteins; overproduction → overflow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive dipstick → **first-morning UA/microscopy and spot urine protein:creatinine ratio (UPCR)**
Pediatric normal UPCR: age >2 years **≤0.2 mg/mg**; age 6–24 months ≤0.5
Nephrotic range: children UPCR ≥2 mg/mg; adults total protein ≥3.5 g/day
★ Postural uncertainty → **split upright/supine collection**; separate daytime activity from overnight recumbency
Persistent abnormality → creatinine, albumin, BP; nephritic → complement/ANA; adults: spot albumin:creatinine

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Protein plus active sediment, impaired filtration, marked edema, or systemic disease → **nephrology referral**
Biopsy selected persistent unexplained cases, especially nephritic findings; do not biopsy benign postural pattern
Proteinuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB when tolerated; treat diabetes/BP and underlying disease; monitor K/creatinine
Avoid empiric steroids before defining the syndrome; isolated low-grade protein does not establish nephrotic syndrome

rows.label: Complications
items: Sustained glomerular injury → CKD; heavy losses → hypoalbuminemia, thrombosis, infection
Benign transient/postural forms do not predict progressive renal failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control diabetes and hypertension, avoid nephrotoxins; assess family history and recurrent urinary abnormalities

rows.label: Mimics
items: False-positive dipstick: concentrated/alkaline urine, blood contamination; repeat clean specimen
Myeloma light chains: dipstick may be negative despite high total urine protein

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins
Immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis → irregular anovulatory cycles, normal for 2–3 years after menarche
Virilized boy with **prepubertal testes** → peripheral androgen, usually adrenal; central puberty enlarges testes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment
Pubertal gynecomastia, unilateral or bilateral, smooth subareolar → **reassurance**; no labs/biopsy; carcinoma very rare

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance
Normal puberty + moodiness, mild parent conflict → **puberty education** for child, parents; no drug testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up
Familial short stature: short parents, bone age matches chronologic age; constitutional delay: **delayed bone age**

table.title: Tanner staging anchors
rows: Further enlargement; menarche usually within 1–2 years

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

pulmonary-hypertension.name: Pulmonary hypertension
pulmonary-hypertension.scope: WHO groups 1-5 (PAH, left heart disease, lung disease/hypoxia, CTEPH, multifactorial), cor pulmonale, echocardiography, right heart catheterization, endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE-5 inhibitors
pulmonary-hypertension.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, syncope or right-heart failure with elevated pulmonary pressures requires hemodynamic classification before vasodilator treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Connective-tissue disease, congenital shunts, portal hypertension, HIV, methamphetamine → PAH
Left-heart disease, chronic lung disease/hypoxia or prior pulmonary embolism are common secondary contexts

rows.label: Clues
items: Loud P2, RV heave, tricuspid regurgitation murmur; exertional chest pain or presyncope
JVD, hepatomegaly and edema → right-heart failure/cor pulmonale
Severe dyspnea with relatively preserved spirometry or low DLCO suggests pulmonary vascular disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary vascular resistance or elevated left filling pressure increases RV afterload
Sustained pressure overload → RV hypertrophy, dilation, reduced output and systemic venous congestion
Chronic alveolar hypoxia (COPD, OSA) → **pulmonary vasoconstriction** and remodeling → raised vascular resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography** estimates probability and evaluates RV/left-heart function; not definitive pressure diagnosis
★ **Right-heart catheterization: mean PAP >20 mm Hg** at rest confirms PH
Precapillary: wedge ≤15 mm Hg and **PVR >2 Wood units**; postcapillary: wedge >15
★ **V/Q scan** screens CTEPH; normal perfusion essentially excludes chronic thromboembolic disease
PFT/DLCO, chest CT, sleep evaluation, HIV/autoimmune testing by history; vasoreactivity testing in selected PAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen for hypoxemia, diuresis for congestion; treat underlying disease and refer confirmed PAH/CTEPH
★ PAH → specialist **endothelin antagonist + PDE-5 inhibitor**; high-risk disease → parenteral prostacyclin
Vasoreactive idiopathic/heritable/drug-associated PAH → selected high-dose calcium-channel blocker; not empiric treatment
CTEPH → lifelong anticoagulation and pulmonary endarterectomy if operable; selected balloon angioplasty or riociguat
Do not routinely use PAH vasodilators for left-heart/lung-disease PH; PDE-5 drugs cannot combine with nitrates/riociguat

rows.label: Complications
items: RV failure, arrhythmia, syncope and death; pregnancy carries substantial maternal risk in PAH
Endothelin antagonists are teratogenic; some require liver monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid methamphetamine, address thromboembolic risk; vaccination, supervised exercise, pregnancy/contraception counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: HFpEF: elevated wedge pressure identifies postcapillary cause
Deconditioning/anemia: no catheter-confirmed pulmonary pressure elevation

research-ethics.name: Research ethics
research-ethics.scope: Institutional review board (IRB), vulnerable populations (prisoners, children), coercion and undue inducement, clinical equipoise, informed consent in research
research-ethics.core: Scientifically valid research requires independent oversight, fair selection, favorable risk-benefit balance, and voluntary informed participation with additional safeguards for vulnerability.

rows.label: Principle
items: Respect for persons, beneficence, justice: autonomy, minimize harm, equitable recruitment
★ **Clinical equipoise**: expert uncertainty about superior treatment; personal doubt insufficient
Vulnerability warrants safeguards, not automatic exclusion from scientifically justified studies

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **IRB approval before recruitment**; disclose conflicts, monitor harms, report unexpected problems
Explain purpose, randomization, risks, uncertain benefits, alternatives, privacy, injury care, contacts
★ **Ongoing consent**: check understanding, answer questions, update risks; withdrawal without penalty

rows.label: Don't
items: Coercion: threaten lost care, employment, grades, liberty for refusal; parole offer to prisoners
Undue influence: incentives distort voluntary judgment; reasonable reimbursement/payment permitted
Placebo causing serious harm by withholding proven care; disguise research as personalized treatment

rows.label: Exceptions
items: IRB waiver: minimal risk, impracticable otherwise, preserved rights/welfare; later disclosure when needed
Identifiable-data waiver: study also impracticable without identifiers
Emergency research: prior regulatory safeguards/approval; treatment emergency exception insufficient

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **IRB approval never replaces informed consent** unless an authorized waiver applies
Capable child's dissent generally respected despite parental permission
Therapeutic misconception: participant assumes every study decision maximizes personal clinical benefit

table.title: Additional safeguards
rows: Parental permission plus developmentally capable child's assent
Permitted research category; prisoner representative on IRB
Legally authorized representative; seek participant assent

rhabdomyolysis.name: Rhabdomyolysis
rhabdomyolysis.scope: Trauma, crush injury, prolonged immobilization, statins, seizures, elevated CK, myoglobinuria (blood on dipstick without RBCs), acute tubular necrosis, aggressive IV saline hydration
rhabdomyolysis.core: Acute skeletal muscle breakdown releases myoglobin and electrolytes; recognize pigment nephropathy early and restore renal perfusion before kidney failure develops.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Crush injury, prolonged immobilization**, compartment syndrome, ischemia/reperfusion
Seizures, strenuous exercise, heatstroke, cocaine; statins, especially with interacting drugs
Hypokalemia, infections, alcohol intoxication; pressure injury during unconsciousness

rows.label: Clues
items: Muscle pain, weakness, swelling; dark urine possible, but classic triad often incomplete
↑K, ↑phosphate, early ↓Ca; AST may rise from muscle rather than liver
Tense painful compartment, pain with passive stretch, sensory change → concurrent limb emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myocyte necrosis → pigment-mediated tubular injury and casts, amplified by hypovolemia and aciduria

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CK >5 times upper limit**, often >1,000 U/L; trend until clearly declining
★ Urine dipstick **heme positive with few/no RBCs** → myoglobin; negative result cannot exclude
Electrolytes, creatinine, ECG, urine output; CK magnitude supports risk assessment, not dialysis alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early **IV normal saline**; titrate to urine output 1–3 mL/kg/hour, avoiding overload
Stop culprit; treat heatstroke/seizures; compartment syndrome → emergency fasciotomy
Hyperkalemic ECG changes → IV calcium, insulin/dextrose; dialysis for refractory electrolyte/volume/acid-base disturbances
★ **No routine bicarbonate or mannitol** for AKI prevention; anuria → reassess fluids, renal consultation
Asymptomatic hypocalcemia → avoid replacement; symptomatic tetany or arrhythmia → calcium

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute tubular necrosis, dangerous arrhythmias, disseminated intravascular coagulation
Recovery phase → rebound hypercalcemia; excessive fluids with renal failure → pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration and gradual exercise progression; avoid exertion during severe heat or illness
Review statin interactions, especially macrolides/gemfibrozil; pressure relief during prolonged immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hematuria: numerous RBCs on microscopy
Hemolysis: heme-positive urine with anemia, ↑LDH, ↓haptoglobin rather than marked CK elevation
Inflammatory myopathy: subacute proximal weakness without acute toxic/traumatic trigger

rhabdomyolysis.evidence: Fluid targets and bicarbonate guidance checked 2026-10-30: [AAST consensus, 2022](https://tsaco.bmj.com/content/7/1/e000836.full.pdf).

rheumatoid-arthritis.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
rheumatoid-arthritis.scope: Symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis, anti-CCP and RF, DMARDs (methotrexate, biologics), extra-articular manifestations, Felty syndrome, cervical spine subluxation
rheumatoid-arthritis.core: Persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis with prolonged morning stiffness and improvement with activity; early disease-modifying treatment prevents erosions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Female sex, smoking, family history, HLA-DRB1 susceptibility; onset often middle adulthood

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Boggy swelling of **MCP, PIP, wrists**; DIP joints usually spared
Ulnar deviation, swan-neck/boutonnière deformities; subcutaneous nodules and constitutional symptoms
Extra-articular: pleuritis, interstitial lung disease, episcleritis/scleritis, pericarditis, neuropathy
★ **Felty syndrome**: established erosive disease + splenomegaly + neutropenia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Autoimmune synovial inflammation → pannus, cartilage destruction, marginal bone erosion
TNF and other inflammatory cytokines drive articular and systemic injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical synovitis → **anti-CCP, RF, ESR/CRP**; anti-CCP more specific, negative serology not exclusionary
Hand/foot radiographs: periarticular osteopenia, uniform narrowing, erosions; early films can be normal
Acute single hot joint → arthrocentesis to exclude infection or crystals before attributing symptoms
Neck pain, neurologic symptoms, or suspected instability before anesthesia → cervical imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Methotrexate + folate** first-line for moderate/high activity; hydroxychloroquine reasonable for low activity
Treat to remission/low activity; inadequate response → add biologic, often TNF inhibitor
NSAIDs relieve symptoms without preventing joint damage; glucocorticoid bridge only briefly when necessary
Methotrexate: avoid pregnancy, significant liver disease; monitor CBC, creatinine, LFTs
TNF inhibitors: avoid active infection, advanced heart failure, demyelinating disease

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ **Atlantoaxial subluxation** → cord compression; protect cervical spine during airway management
Accelerated cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, secondary amyloidosis; immunosuppression → serious infections

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, occupational/physical rehabilitation; assess bone and cardiovascular risk
Screen TB and hepatitis B before biologics; update vaccines before immunosuppression

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteoarthritis: bony DIP/first CMC enlargement, brief stiffness
Psoriatic arthritis: dactylitis, nail pitting, asymmetric or DIP involvement
SLE arthritis: usually nonerosive, rash/cytopenias, disease-specific autoantibodies

rickets.name: Rickets
rickets.scope: Nutritional vitamin D deficiency, X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets, metaphyseal cupping and fraying, elevated alkaline phosphatase, low phosphate, high PTH
rickets.core: Growing child with bowed legs, widened wrists, and delayed growth: evaluate defective growth-plate mineralization rather than treating the deformity alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ Nutritional: **unsupplemented breastfeeding**, low dietary calcium, limited sunlight, darker skin, malabsorption
Inherited phosphate wasting: X-linked dominant; affected fathers transmit to all daughters, no sons

rows.label: Clues
items: Rachitic rosary, craniotabes, delayed fontanelle closure, bone pain, hypotonia, delayed walking
Hypocalcemic tetany, seizures, prolonged QT, cardiomyopathy → urgent stabilization
Persistent short stature, lower-limb deformity, dental abscesses despite adequate vitamin D → phosphate-wasting disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nutritional deficiency → reduced intestinal calcium absorption → secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal phosphate loss
**PHEX mutation → excess FGF23**, renal phosphaturia and inappropriately low calcitriol

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Wrist/knee radiograph → **metaphyseal cupping, fraying, widened growth plates**
★ Check **calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, PTH, 25-OH vitamin D**, creatinine; ALP elevated, phosphate reduced
25-OH vitamin D <12 ng/mL supports deficiency; interpret with calcium intake and biochemical pattern
Normal vitamin D with hypophosphatemia → assess renal phosphate wasting; genetic evaluation if inherited pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic hypocalcemia → **IV calcium gluconate with ECG monitoring**, then oral calcium
During repletion → repeat calcium/phosphate/ALP; assess radiographic healing
Burosumab must not accompany oral phosphate/active vitamin D; specialist monitoring prevents excess phosphate
Persistent renal disease/acidosis → treat cause; orthopedic correction only for residual deformity after metabolic control

rows.label: Complications
items: Fractures, permanent deformity, impaired growth; severe hypocalcemia → arrhythmia
Phosphate/calcitriol: ↑PTH, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis → urine calcium and renal ultrasound monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Infants: **vitamin D 400 IU/day**; after 12 months, total intake 600 IU/day plus calcium-rich foods
Maternal nutrition, supplementation during malabsorption, and family counseling for inherited disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Physiologic bowing: symmetric toddler legs, normal growth plates/laboratory studies
Blount disease: focal medial tibial growth disturbance, often obesity; normal mineral studies
Osteogenesis imperfecta: fragile collagen, blue sclerae; no characteristic growth-plate changes

salivary-gland-disorders.name: Salivary gland disorders
salivary-gland-disorders.scope: Acute suppurative sialadenitis, sialolithiasis, mumps parotitis, salivary tumors
salivary-gland-disorders.core: Salivary swelling may reflect infection, obstructed flow, viral parotitis, or a neoplasm; meal association, duct drainage, and focality guide the branch.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, postoperative state, poor oral hygiene, anticholinergic drugs reduce salivary flow
Submandibular gland predisposed to stones; unvaccinated close-contact exposure favors mumps
Prior radiation and smoking increase selected salivary tumor risks; older age raises neoplasm concern

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Purulence from Stensen or Wharton duct** supports acute bacterial sialadenitis
Painful unilateral gland with fever; airway symptoms, trismus, toxic appearance → deep infection/abscess
★ **Facial weakness, fixation, rapid growth**, cervical nodes with parotid mass → malignancy warning
Dry eyes/dry mouth and recurrent bilateral swelling suggest autoimmune sicca disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis permits ascending oral bacteria; S aureus common in suppurative infection
Ductal calculus blocks secretion; mumps causes viral gland inflammation; most parotid tumors benign

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Examine oral ducts and facial nerve; **ultrasound** first for stone or focal gland lesion
Contrast CT for abscess/deep extension; culture expressed pus if present
Mumps suspicion → buccal swab RT-PCR, public health notification; serology supplements selected cases
★ Persistent solid mass → **fine-needle aspiration**, imaging and ENT assessment; avoid open diagnostic biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suppurative disease → **hydration, warm compresses, gland massage, sialogogues + amoxicillin-clavulanate**
Systemic toxicity/poor oral intake → admit, IV ampicillin-sulbactam; abscess → drainage
Obstruction → stimulate flow and remove persistent stone via sialendoscopy or selected surgery
Mumps → analgesia/hydration, isolate through 5 days after swelling onset; no antibiotic benefit
Tumor → specialist surgical excision; avoid simple enucleation of pleomorphic adenoma

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, deep neck infection, recurrent sialadenitis; parotid surgery → facial nerve injury, gustatory sweating
Mumps → orchitis, meningitis, pancreatitis, hearing loss; longstanding pleomorphic adenoma may transform

rows.label: Prevention
items: Oral hygiene, hydration, minimize xerogenic drugs; MMR vaccination for mumps prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dental abscess: focal tooth tenderness, odontogenic collection
Sjögren syndrome: chronic sicca, autoimmune features rather than acute ductal pus

table.title: Presentation patterns
rows: Unilateral meal-triggered painful swelling; obstructive sialadenitis
Older smoker; sometimes bilateral parotid masses

salivary-gland-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established salivary disease and mumps isolation teaching.

schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.name: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.scope: Brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, mesolimbic dopamine
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.core: Psychosis with impaired reality testing: distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum disorders by duration, functional decline, and the relationship between mood episodes and psychosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, neurodevelopmental vulnerability; adolescent cannabis exposure increases risk
Typical onset late adolescence/early adulthood; exclude stimulant, hallucinogen, medication, and neurologic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior; negative symptoms: avolition, alogia, flat affect
★ At least **two core symptoms**, including delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, for active-phase diagnosis
Suicidality, dangerous commands or inability to eat → urgent safety assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **↑Mesolimbic dopamine** → positive symptoms; mesocortical → negative symptoms, early working-memory deficits
D2 blockade reduces psychosis but nigrostriatal/tuberoinfundibular effects cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia
Structural correlate: **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, reduced cortical volume

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical history, collateral information, mental status; assess mood timeline and substance exposure
First episode → CBC/CMP, TSH, toxicology; HIV/syphilis or neuroimaging for relevant risks/atypical neurologic findings
★ **Schizoaffective**: ≥2 weeks psychosis without mood episode; mood episodes occupy most illness duration

rows.label: Tx
items: Safety crisis → hospitalization; acute agitation → de-escalation, then medication if needed
★ **Risperidone, aripiprazole or olanzapine** + coordinated specialty care, family education, CBT, supported employment
Schizoaffective depressive/bipolar subtype → add antidepressant or mood stabilizer according to mood syndrome
★ Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials or persistent substantial suicide risk → **clozapine**
Adherence difficulty → long-acting injectable (haloperidol decanoate); catatonia → lorazepam, then ECT if refractory

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, homelessness, substance use, cardiometabolic disease; antipsychotics → metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, NMS
Clozapine → neutropenia, myocarditis, severe constipation; monitor ANC and symptoms

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid cannabis/stimulants; maintenance medication, relapse planning reduce recurrence
Monitor weight, BP, glucose, lipids; address tobacco use and cardiovascular risk
**High expressed emotion** (family criticism, hostility) → relapse; family therapy reduces recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mood disorder with psychosis: psychosis occurs exclusively during mood episodes
Delirium: fluctuating attention/awareness and acute medical cause
Delusional disorder: ≥1 month delusions with otherwise relatively preserved function, limited other psychotic symptoms
Substance/medication-induced psychosis: recent stimulants (mydriasis, tremor) or corticosteroids, intact orientation

scoliosis.name: Scoliosis
scoliosis.scope: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, Cobb angle measurement, forward bend test, bracing indications, spinal fusion surgery, natural history and adult progression
scoliosis.core: Adolescent with asymmetric shoulders or rib prominence from a structural lateral curve with vertebral rotation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, female sex and rapid growth increase progression risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually painless; waist asymmetry, uneven scapulae or pelvic tilt
★ Significant pain, neurologic deficits, rapid progression, or left thoracic curve → evaluate secondary cause
Assess gait, strength, reflexes and skin stigmata for underlying neuromuscular or spinal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Vertebral rotation pushes ribs posteriorly on convex thoracic side; growth amplifies susceptible curves

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Adam forward bend test** accentuates rib hump; scoliometer quantifies trunk rotation
★ Standing full-spine radiographs: **Cobb angle ≥10°**, measured using most tilted end vertebrae
Skeletal maturity by Risser or Sanders stage; MRI if atypical features or neurologic abnormalities

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Observe stable moderate curves after skeletal maturity
★ Bracing slows progression during growth; success depends on adherence
Surgery aims to halt progression and correct deformity while preserving functional motion segments

rows.label: Complications
items: Curves ≥50° at maturity often progress in adulthood; very severe thoracic curves can impair ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leg-length discrepancy: flexible curve resolves when pelvis leveled
Congenital scoliosis: vertebral segmentation anomaly on radiographs

table.title: Management during growth
rows: Observe with serial exams and radiographs

scoliosis.evidence: Checked Scoliosis Research Society guidance on observation, bracing and surgery.

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Renal stenosis: older smoker → atherosclerotic **lipid plaque**; young/middle-aged woman → **fibromuscular dysplasia** (medial hyperplasia, renal + carotid)
Renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis** → aldosterone excess, primary or renovascular; normal K does not exclude it
**Abdominal bruit**, diffuse atherosclerosis, late abrupt worsening, small unilateral kidney → renal artery stenosis
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
**Episodic headache, sweating, palpitations** → pheochromocytoma; cushingoid appearance, upper-body hypertension guide testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion → juxtaglomerular **renin** → RAAS; ACE inhibitor removes efferent constriction → ↓renal flow, ↓GFR across stenosis
Autonomous aldosterone → distal sodium absorption, potassium loss, low renin; pressure natriuresis escape prevents edema
Adrenal medullary catecholamine or cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.name: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis
septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.scope: Ovarian vein thrombosis, deep septic pelvic thrombophlebitis, persistent postpartum fever, unresponsive to broad-spectrum antibiotics, CT with IV contrast, therapeutic anticoagulation and IV antibiotics
septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.core: Persistent spiking postpartum fever despite adequate broad-spectrum antibiotics suggests infected pelvic venous thrombosis after other sources are excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cesarean delivery, postpartum endometritis, pelvic surgery, prolonged labor, maternal hypercoagulability
Right ovarian vein more often involved because of anatomy and venous stasis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fever persisting **48–72 hours or longer** despite treatment, with relatively well appearance between spikes
Ovarian vein involvement may cause flank/lower abdominal pain; deep pelvic branch disease may be painless
Tachycardia and tenderness variable; blood cultures often negative, especially after antibiotics
Dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hypoxemia → assess pulmonary embolism

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Venous endothelial injury, postpartum stasis, and hypercoagulability produce thrombus with local infection
Infected clot remains an inflammatory focus despite initially suitable uterine antibiotic coverage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**: enlarged thrombosed ovarian vein or pelvic venous filling defect
MRI alternative when CT unsuitable; small pelvic branch thromboses may evade imaging
Reassess wound, urine, breasts, blood cultures; ultrasound/CT for retained products or pelvic abscess
Imaging-negative deep disease remains exclusion diagnosis; fever response to heparin is not a definitive diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Continue **IV broad-spectrum antibiotics**, e.g., clindamycin + gentamicin; add ampicillin for enterococcal concern
★ Confirmed symptomatic ovarian vein thrombosis → **therapeutic LMWH/UFH** plus antibiotics
Postpartum provoked ovarian vein thrombosis often anticoagulated about 3 months; extend if persistent risks
Imaging-negative deep SPT: anticoagulation individualized; evidence weaker than classic empiric-heparin board teaching
Persistent illness → revisit resistant organisms, abscess needing drainage, or alternative noninfectious fever source

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary embolism, extension to renal vein/IVC, sepsis; anticoagulation-associated hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cesarean antibiotic prophylaxis, early mobilization, VTE-risk-based prophylaxis, prompt endometritis treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pelvic abscess: localized collection on imaging; source control needed
Retained products: bleeding, subinvolution, intrauterine material; evacuation when clinically indicated
Drug fever: temporal medication relationship, unrevealing source evaluation

septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.evidence: Anticoagulation checked 2026-10-30: [ASH postpartum ovarian-vein review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6142588/); imaging-negative practice uncertainty distinguished from classic board teaching.

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk
Procedure bleeding: thoracentesis → intercostal artery, hemothorax; splenectomy → hemoperitoneum, left shoulder pain

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: **lost sympathetic tone** → hypotension, bradycardia or no tachycardia, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid
Warm sepsis: high output, **high mixed venous O2**; pump failure: low contractility, congestion; hypovolemia: low preload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
**Serial lactate**: hypoperfusion, best predicts course and mortality; trend with capillary refill, urine output
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation
CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, IV access; **isotonic crystalloid** (balanced, 0.9% saline) before imaging; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + blood products** (emergency O-negative); crystalloid as bridge; no vasopressors
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone
Pulmonary edema after fluids → stop boluses, **inotrope**; children: epinephrine preferred, older exams may expect dopamine

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose
Isolated head injury: hypertension + bradycardia (Cushing); trauma hypotension + tachycardia → assume hemorrhage

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

sickle-cell-disease.name: Sickle cell disease
sickle-cell-disease.scope: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis, acute chest syndrome, splenic sequestration, aplastic crisis, stroke, sickle cell trait, hemoglobin electrophoresis
sickle-cell-disease.core: HbS polymerization causes chronic hemolysis and episodic vascular occlusion; fever, hypoxemia and focal neurologic deficits require urgent escalation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive β-globin disease; dehydration, hypoxemia, cold and infection trigger sickling
Functional asplenia → encapsulated infection from early childhood; **S. pneumoniae** leads pneumonia and fulminant sepsis

rows.label: Clues
items: Baseline anemia, reticulocytosis, jaundice; childhood dactylitis or recurrent severe bone pain
Acute chest syndrome: **new pulmonary infiltrate** plus fever, respiratory symptoms or hypoxemia
Sequestration: sudden splenomegaly, falling hemoglobin, shock; aplasia: **low reticulocyte count**, often parvovirus

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes → rigid erythrocytes, endothelial injury, ischemia and shortened RBC survival
Acute chest trigger: **infection** most common; in situ thrombosis and fat embolism less often
Severe anemia → low viscosity, vasodilation, ↓afterload → **↑cardiac output** preserves oxygen delivery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC confirms genotype; newborn screen detects disease before symptoms
Crisis → CBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin; fever → blood cultures; respiratory symptoms → chest radiograph
New focal deficit → emergency brain imaging, without delaying transfusion preparation
Distinguish osteomyelitis from infarction using cultures and MRI when focal fever/pain persists

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain crisis → prompt **IV opioid**, morphine (AKI: lower dose or hydromorphone); no meperidine; NSAID only if kidneys normal
Pain crisis support: euvolemic hydration; oxygen only for hypoxemia; no routine transfusion
★ Acute chest → oxygen, **ceftriaxone + azithromycin**, incentive spirometry; transfuse for significant anemia
Severe acute chest, stroke → **urgent exchange transfusion**; sequestration (cautious) or aplasia → simple transfusion
Fever → immediate **IV ceftriaxone/cefotaxime**, despite daily penicillin prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, avascular necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, nephropathy, retinopathy
Repeated transfusions → alloimmunization and iron overload; delayed hyperhemolysis can worsen anemia
Chronic hemolysis → ↑folate demand → **folate deficiency**, macrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hydroxyurea** raises HbF, reduces crises; monitor CBC
Penicillin prophylaxis through age 5 in HbSS; pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib and influenza vaccines
Annual transcranial Doppler ages 2–16 in HbSS/HbSβ0; abnormal → chronic transfusion program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: persistent localized pain, fever; Salmonella or S. aureus
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, no hemolytic pattern

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.name: Skin and soft tissue infections
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.scope: Cellulitis, erysipelas, folliculitis, furuncles, carbuncles, lymphangitis, necrotizing fasciitis
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.core: Skin infection management depends on purulence, systemic illness, and signs of deep tissue destruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin breaks, tinea pedis, edema/lymphedema, diabetes, obesity, injection drug use
Prior MRSA, crowding, recent hospitalization; surgery or penetrating trauma raises deep-infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Warmth, tenderness, erythema; rapidly expanding margins or systemic toxicity require urgent reassessment
★ **Pain out of proportion**, bullae, anesthesia, crepitus, shock → necrotizing infection
