Perineal infection, especially diabetes → Fournier gangrene/necrotizing fasciitis; saltwater exposure → Vibrio, freshwater → Aeromonas

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonpurulent infection usually streptococcal, S aureus possible; purulent lesions usually S aureus
Fascial spread, toxins → necrosis, sepsis; minor trauma, no crepitus → **GAS**; crepitus → Clostridium/polymicrobial
Tinea pedis = portal of entry: acute fever/cellulitis is bacterial (S aureus/streptococcal) superinfection, not Trichophyton

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical diagnosis; **bedside ultrasound** if occult fluid collection suspected
Culture drained pus for severe, recurrent, or resistant infection; blood cultures for systemic toxicity
Suspected necrotizing disease → immediate surgical evaluation; imaging must not delay exploration
Low laboratory risk score or absent gas does not exclude necrotizing fasciitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Deep infection → **urgent debridement + vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam**, add clindamycin for toxin suppression
Confirmed group A streptococcal necrotizing infection → penicillin + clindamycin
Moderate cellulitis (systemic signs) → IV cefazolin; MRSA risk or cephalexin failure → vancomycin; severe → + pip-tazo
★ Abscess: add **antibiotics** for systemic signs, immunocompromise, extensive disease, or failed drainage
Pregnancy + suspected MRSA → clindamycin or vancomycin; **no doxycycline or fluoroquinolones**

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, osteomyelitis, septic thrombophlebitis; tissue loss and amputation
Toxic shock, multiorgan failure; recurrent cellulitis worsens lymphatic dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat interdigital fungal infection, manage edema, skin hygiene, protect wounds
Recurrent staphylococcal infections → consider nasal mupirocin + chlorhexidine decolonization; avoid shared razors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Stasis dermatitis: chronic, often bilateral, itchy
DVT: deep swelling without superficial spreading infection; contact dermatitis: pruritic exposure-pattern rash
Superficial thrombophlebitis: palpable indurated venous cord, not lymphatic streaks

table.title: Superficial patterns
rows: Incision and drainage; TMP-SMX if needed
Tender red streaks from skin break toward nodes
Usually S pyogenes; cephalexin; IV if systemic
Itchy follicular pustules on trunk/thighs after hot tub

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established IDSA-based infection management.

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

smoking-cessation.name: Smoking cessation
smoking-cessation.scope: Mortality reduction, 5 As counseling, pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement, bupropion, varenicline), behavioral programs
smoking-cessation.core: Stopping tobacco lowers cardiovascular, cancer (lung, oral cavity, bladder), pulmonary, and all-cause mortality at any age; counseling plus drugs produces the best quit rates.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Ask every adult** about tobacco, vaping, dependence, prior attempts; include pregnancy
No readiness to quit → motivational interviewing; connect personal goals to cessation benefits
★ Smoking = **strongest modifiable** coronary, mortality risk; cessation beats statin, BP, glucose drugs

rows.label: Start/stop
items: 5 As: **Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, Arrange**; agree quit date, identify triggers
Arrange early follow-up, behavioral program, quitline; relapse → reassess triggers and renew treatment

rows.label: Test
items: Cigarettes/day, time to first cigarette, withdrawal; no routine biochemical confirmation
Check pregnancy, renal function, seizure/eating-disorder history before selecting drugs

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Nonpregnant adults → **varenicline or combination nicotine replacement** plus behavioral support
Pregnancy → counseling first; if unsuccessful, discuss drugs individually, evidence uncertain
COPD: **cessation alone slows FEV1 decline**, not inhaled steroids; oxygen helps only resting hypoxemia

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Psychiatric history alone does not contraindicate varenicline; monitor mood changes
E-cigarettes: insufficient USPSTF evidence for cessation; avoid recommending during pregnancy
Stopping smoke exposure reverses CYP1A2 induction → ↑clozapine/theophylline; nicotine not responsible

table.title: Drug selection
rows: Nausea, vivid dreams; renal dose adjustment
Irritation; safe in stable CAD; caution unstable ACS
Avoid seizures, eating disorders, abrupt alcohol withdrawal

spinal-cord-compression.name: Spinal cord compression
spinal-cord-compression.scope: Neoplastic spinal cord compression (epidural metastases, dexamethasone, emergent MRI), spinal epidural abscess (fever, IV drug use, empiric antibiotics), cauda equina syndrome, surgical decompression
spinal-cord-compression.core: Back pain with new weakness, sensory changes or sphincter dysfunction requires urgent MRI to identify reversible neural compression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Known breast, prostate, lung, renal cancer or myeloma → epidural metastases
IV drug use, bacteremia, diabetes, spinal procedure or immunosuppression → epidural abscess
Large lumbar disc herniation, trauma or spinal stenosis → cauda equina compression
Anticoagulation + epidural catheter placement/removal → **spinal epidural hematoma**: acute paraplegia, incontinence

rows.label: Clues
items: Progressive nocturnal pain, pain with cough/strain, radicular symptoms; deficits may be initially subtle
Cord lesion: sensory level, spastic weakness, hyperreflexia below lesion after acute phase
★ Cauda equina: **saddle anesthesia, urinary retention**, reduced anal tone, asymmetric flaccid leg weakness
Epidural abscess: fever/back pain ± deficit; classic triad often incomplete

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Epidural tumor, infection or disc material compresses neural tissue and impairs blood supply
Longstanding compression produces irreversible ischemic injury; bladder dysfunction signals advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urgent contrast MRI** of suspected region; whole spine for suspected metastatic compression
Postvoid residual supports retention assessment but normal result does not exclude early cauda equina syndrome
Suspected abscess → blood cultures, CBC, ESR/CRP; image before LP
MRI unavailable/contraindicated → CT myelography; ordinary radiographs cannot exclude epidural pathology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Malignant compression with deficit → **dexamethasone immediately**, urgent neurosurgery/radiation consultation
Tumor → decompression/stabilization ± radiotherapy; choice depends on stability, neurologic function and prognosis
★ Epidural abscess → **vancomycin + cefepime**, cultures; urgent decompression for deficits or instability
Cauda equina syndrome → emergency spinal surgical assessment and **decompression**
Immobilize if instability suspected; bladder drainage and analgesia during definitive treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent paralysis, bowel/bladder dysfunction, sexual dysfunction, pressure injuries and VTE
Abscess → sepsis; steroids can worsen uncontrolled infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rapid assessment of cancer-associated new back pain; sterile procedures and prompt bacteremia treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mechanical strain: normal neurologic exam, no sphincter symptoms
Transverse myelitis: intrinsic cord lesion without external compression
Peripheral neuropathy: distal symmetric findings without sensory level

spinal-cord-compression.evidence: Not checked online; established neurologic and oncologic emergency principles.

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea or exertional indigestion may be anginal equivalents
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
Stable on medical therapy, low-risk ischemia → no repeat testing or mandatory catheterization; respect informed refusal
Sedentary, risk factors, starting vigorous exercise: no routine stress test; older exam questions may expect exercise ECG

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up
Drug-eluting stent → **aspirin + clopidogrel**, not anticoagulant; stable CAD 6 months; older exam questions may expect 12

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness
Variant (Prinzmetal) vasospasm: rest/nocturnal pain, **transient ST elevation**, nitrate relief, normal angiography → calcium-channel blocker

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC chronic coronary disease guideline summary (2023)](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2023/07/17/19/06/2023-guideline-for-chronic-coronary-disease-gl-ccd/).

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

systemic-lupus-erythematosus.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.scope: Diagnostic criteria (serositis, arthritis, lupus nephritis), neonatal lupus (congenital AV block), autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith), pharmacotherapy (hydroxychloroquine, glucocorticoids)
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.core: Multisystem autoimmunity combining inflammatory joint, skin, serosal, renal, hematologic, or neurologic disease; flares often lower complement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive-age women; family history; UV exposure, infections, estrogen-related triggers

rows.label: Clues
items: Photosensitive malar rash sparing nasolabial folds; painless oral ulcers; nonscarring alopecia
Symmetric nonerosive arthritis, pleuritic pain, pericarditis; leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hemolysis
★ **Proteinuria, RBC casts**, edema or hypertension → renal involvement
Neonatal lupus: maternal anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB; congenital AV block may be permanent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-complex deposition activates **classical complement**, consuming C3/C4; autoantibody-mediated blood-cell destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANA** sensitive entry test; anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm more specific
Anti-dsDNA titers, C3/C4, CBC, urinalysis, urine protein/creatinine, creatinine assess activity
★ Proteinuria **>0.5 g/g** or unexplained renal dysfunction → kidney biopsy
Classification: ANA ≥1:80, weighted score ≥10 with clinical criterion; clinical diagnosis remains contextual

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydroxychloroquine** broadly; NSAIDs for mild arthritis/serositis, glucocorticoids for flares
Organ-threatening flare → IV methylprednisolone; nephritis → mycophenolate plus belimumab/calcineurin inhibitor
Cyclophosphamide alternative for severe renal/CNS disease; taper glucocorticoids after disease control
Pregnancy → continue hydroxychloroquine; avoid mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Complications
items: Accelerated atherosclerosis, infection, CKD; antiphospholipid antibodies → thrombosis or pregnancy loss
Hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity; chronic steroid osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Sun protection; vaccines, cardiovascular risk control, retinal monitoring
Plan pregnancy during quiescence; anti-Ro/La positivity → fetal cardiac surveillance discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced lupus: antihistone antibodies, usually no renal/CNS disease
Rheumatoid arthritis: erosions; fibromyalgia: pain without inflammatory findings

testicular-cancer.name: Testicular cancer
testicular-cancer.scope: Seminoma, nonseminomatous germ cell tumors, sex cord-stromal tumors (Leydig cell, Sertoli cell), tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH), scrotal ultrasound, radical inguinal orchiectomy
testicular-cancer.core: A solid intratesticular lesion requires urgent evaluation for malignancy; an inguinal approach preserves proper staging and lymphatic drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Cryptorchidism**, prior contralateral germ cell tumor, family history, testicular dysgenesis
Most germ cell tumors arise in young adults; older men also require consideration of lymphoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually painless firm enlargement or heaviness; pain does not exclude malignancy
Gynecomastia from hormone production; back pain may indicate retroperitoneal nodes
Cough/dyspnea, supraclavicular nodes suggest dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Most adult tumors germ cell-derived; mixed tumors managed as nonseminomatous
Lymphatic spread follows gonadal vessels to retroperitoneal para-aortic nodes rather than initial inguinal drainage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler** first distinguishes intratesticular from extratesticular lesions
★ **AFP, β-hCG, LDH before orchiectomy**; repeat afterward for staging and response
CT abdomen/pelvis + chest imaging for metastases; normal markers do not exclude cancer
Avoid transscrotal needle biopsy or scrotal orchiectomy; disrupted lymphatics complicate treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Radical inguinal orchiectomy** for suspicious solid mass; discuss sperm banking before gonadotoxic treatment
Stage I seminoma: surveillance preferred when reliable; carboplatin or radiation selected alternatives
Stage I nonseminoma: surveillance, cisplatin-based chemotherapy, or retroperitoneal node dissection according to risk
★ Metastatic germ cell tumor → cisplatin-based **BEP**; residual nonseminomatous mass may require resection
Sex cord-stromal tumors: surgery; monitor endocrine manifestations and malignant features

rows.label: Complications
items: Infertility, hypogonadism; assess contralateral function
BEP: bleomycin pulmonary toxicity; cisplatin nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity; etoposide-associated leukemia
Retroperitoneal node surgery may cause retrograde ejaculation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Orchiopexy reduces cryptorchid-associated risk but does not eliminate it; no routine population screening
Strict stage-specific surveillance with examination, markers, and imaging after treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hydrocele: transilluminates; ultrasound needed if testis not palpable
Epididymitis: tender epididymis, urinary/infectious symptoms
Torsion: abrupt severe pain, absent cremasteric reflex; immediate exploration when strongly suspected

thoracic-trauma.name: Thoracic trauma
thoracic-trauma.scope: Blunt and penetrating chest trauma, blunt cardiac injury, blunt aortic injury, diaphragmatic rupture, pulmonary contusion
thoracic-trauma.core: Chest trauma with respiratory or circulatory compromise requires immediate treatment of life-threatening injuries before definitive imaging.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, steering-wheel impact, crush injuries, penetrating wounds
Lower chest wounds can cross diaphragm and injure abdominal organs

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral absent breath sounds, shock, distended neck veins → tension pneumothorax
Flail segment: paradoxical movement; associated lung injury drives hypoxemia
Hypoxemia hours after impact + focal alveolar infiltrate, worsening to 24–48 h, afebrile → **pulmonary contusion**
Left thoracic bowel sounds/loops, **NG tip in left chest**, obscured hemidiaphragm → diaphragmatic rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pleural pressure or pericardial blood impairs venous return → obstructive shock
Alveolar hemorrhage and edema impair gas exchange; rapid deceleration shears the aortic isthmus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Primary survey with **eFAST** and portable chest radiograph; unstable injuries treated clinically
★ Deceleration + **widened mediastinum** → aortic injury; stable → **CT angiography**; normal radiograph cannot exclude
Blunt cardiac injury → ECG and troponin; both normal effectively exclude significant injury
Sternal/anterior rib fractures + new arrhythmia/↑troponin → telemetry; persistent shock → echocardiography
Large persistent air leak, subcutaneous air despite working chest tube → **tracheobronchial rupture**; bronchoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension pneumothorax → immediate needle/finger decompression → **chest tube**; no imaging delay
Open pneumothorax → vented seal and tube; hemothorax → tube and blood resuscitation
★ Initial tube blood >1500 mL or persistent >200 mL/h → operative exploration
Tamponade with shock/arrest → surgical drainage; pericardiocentesis only temporizing
Contusion/flail chest → oxygen, regional/multimodal analgesia, pulmonary hygiene; intubate for respiratory failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Contusion → ARDS; retained hemothorax → empyema
Rib fractures → splinting, atelectasis, pneumonia; cardiac injury → arrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seat belts, vehicle safety systems and protective equipment reduce injury risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myocardial contusion: ventricular ectopy, rising wedge pressure, pulmonary edema after fluids; no pericardial compression
Abdominal hemorrhage: free intraperitoneal fluid; may coexist with thoracic injury
Massive hemothorax: **opacified hemithorax**, flat neck veins; tension pneumothorax: hyperlucent
ARDS: bilateral opacities after 24–48 h; fat embolism: long-bone fracture, petechiae, confusion

thoracic-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established ATLS-based teaching.

table.title: Definitive associated-injury management
rows: IV esmolol if tolerated; endovascular repair

thrombotic-microangiopathies.name: Thrombotic microangiopathies
thrombotic-microangiopathies.scope: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (ADAMTS13, pentad, plasma exchange), hemolytic uremic syndrome (shiga toxin, supportive care), atypical HUS, schistocytes, MAHA
thrombotic-microangiopathies.core: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia plus thrombocytopenia and organ injury: urgently distinguish TTP, Shiga toxin-associated HUS, and complement-mediated HUS.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immune TTP: acquired ADAMTS13 autoantibody; autoimmune disease, pregnancy, HIV can trigger episodes
STEC-HUS: contaminated food/water, often children; recurrent episodes suggest inherited complement susceptibility
Secondary TMA: severe hypertension, pregnancy complications, transplant, calcineurin inhibitors or other drugs

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Schistocytes**, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin, reticulocytosis; direct antiglobulin test usually negative
TTP often neurologic/cardiac-predominant; HUS often renal-predominant, with substantial overlap
Classical TTP pentad: hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, fever, neurologic changes, renal dysfunction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet-rich microthrombi shear passing erythrocytes and obstruct small-vessel perfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC/smear, hemolysis studies, creatinine, urinalysis, PT/aPTT/fibrinogen; coagulation usually normal unlike DIC
★ **High PLASMIC score** supports empiric TTP management while awaiting definitive testing
ECG/troponin and neurologic examination assess otherwise occult organ injury
Normal complement levels do not exclude atypical HUS

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected immune TTP → **treat immediately**; do not await full pentad or confirmatory result
★ STEC disease: **avoid antibiotics/antimotility drugs**; RBC transfusion for symptomatic anemia
TTP: no platelets unless life-threatening bleeding; plasma infusion only if exchange unavoidably delayed

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, myocardial ischemia, seizures, renal failure, death; survivors may develop CKD or cognitive impairment
Caplacizumab → bleeding; complement inhibition → meningococcal infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: TTP remission → monitor ADAMTS13/relapse symptoms; treat marked recurrent deficiency with hematology
★ Before complement blockade: **MenACWY + MenB**; urgent start before vaccine protection → penicillin prophylaxis
Food safety and hand hygiene reduce STEC exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: DIC: prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen, systemic coagulation activation
HELLP: pregnancy-associated hypertension, elevated liver enzymes; delivery central to treatment
B12 deficiency: macrocytosis, low reticulocyte response despite striking LDH

table.title: Decisive subtype branches
rows: Urgent plasma exchange + steroids, caplacizumab, rituximab
Shiga injury; often after bloody diarrhea

thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.name: Thyroid nodules and cancer
thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.scope: Evaluation (TSH, ultrasound, FNA), benign goiter (multinodular goiter, compressive symptoms), thyroid cancer types
thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.core: A thyroid nodule requires functional assessment and ultrasound risk stratification; suspicious nonfunctioning nodules require cytologic evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childhood head/neck irradiation, familial thyroid cancer, MEN 2
Multinodular goiter: iodine deficiency, age; multiple nodules do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Hard fixed lesion, cervical nodes, rapid growth or persistent hoarseness increase cancer concern
Large benign goiter → dysphagia, positional dyspnea, tracheal compression
Anaplastic cancer: older adult with rapidly enlarging invasive neck mass

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Follicular-derived tumors differ in differentiation and spread; C-cell tumors produce calcitonin
Autonomous nodules synthesize hormone without pituitary stimulation and rarely contain malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable nodule → **TSH and thyroid ultrasound** first; document cervical nodes and suspicious features
★ Low TSH → radionuclide scan; hot nodule generally **no FNA**
Normal/high TSH → ultrasound-guided FNA by sonographic risk and size
High/intermediate suspicion ≥1 cm → FNA; low suspicion ≥1.5 cm; very low suspicion ≥2 cm
★ Follicular neoplasm on FNA → diagnostic lobectomy; **capsular/vascular invasion** requires histology

rows.label: Tx
items: Benign asymptomatic nodule → ultrasound follow-up; compressive or substernal goiter → surgery
Differentiated cancer → lobectomy/thyroidectomy by risk; selected higher-risk cases → radioactive iodine
★ Medullary cancer → thyroidectomy; evaluate **pheochromocytoma before surgery**
Anaplastic disease → airway planning, multidisciplinary systemic/local treatment; radioiodine ineffective

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury → hoarseness; bilateral injury → airway obstruction
Post-thyroidectomy hypoparathyroidism → hypocalcemia; expanding hematoma → emergency decompression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary neck radiation; RET-positive families → counseling and preventive thyroidectomy planning
Asymptomatic adult: **no routine ultrasound**; USPSTF against average-risk screening; older questions may expect palpation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Thyroiditis: tenderness or inflammatory history, transient dysfunction
Thyroglossal cyst: midline mass moves with tongue protrusion

table.title: Cancer signatures
rows: Orphan Annie nuclei; psammoma bodies; lymphatic spread

thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.evidence: Not checked online; established ATA nodule evaluation and board-level management.

toxic-shock-syndrome.name: Toxic shock syndrome
toxic-shock-syndrome.core: Abrupt fever, hypotension and multiorgan dysfunction from toxin-producing staphylococci or streptococci; remove the source, resuscitate, and suppress toxin production immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Retained tampon, nasal packing, postoperative wound, burns, postpartum infection; no foreign body required
GAS invasive soft-tissue infection, skin break or recent varicella; diabetes and immunosuppression increase severity

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Diffuse erythroderma + shock**, vomiting/diarrhea, myalgias, mucosal hyperemia suggest staphylococcal disease
Palmar/plantar desquamation typically delayed 1–2 weeks; its absence early cannot exclude diagnosis
★ **Severe focal pain out of proportion**, rapid tissue progression → streptococcal necrotizing infection
Renal/hepatic injury, thrombocytopenia, confusion, hypoxemia; rash less consistent with streptococcal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Superantigens activate T cells outside normal antigen specificity → massive cytokine release, capillary leak
Staphylococcal disease often toxin-mediated from local colonization; GAS usually invasive with bacteremia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; CBC, metabolic/liver tests, lactate, coagulation studies assess organ injury
Blood cultures + source/wound cultures before antibiotics if no meaningful delay
Staphylococcal blood cultures often negative; GAS blood/tissue cultures frequently positive
Concern for necrotizing fasciitis → surgical exploration; CT must not delay debridement

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV crystalloids, norepinephrine**, ICU support; remove tampon/packing, drain abscesses, debride infected tissue
Empiric **vancomycin + clindamycin**; add piperacillin-tazobactam if polymicrobial deep infection possible
★ Confirmed GAS → **penicillin G + clindamycin**; clindamycin suppresses toxin synthesis
Confirmed MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin plus initial toxin suppression; MRSA → continue vancomycin
Refractory severe streptococcal shock → consider IVIG with specialists; survival benefit uncertain

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, ARDS, acute kidney injury, cardiomyopathy, limb loss, death
Staphylococcal recurrence possible because protective immunity may be incomplete

rows.label: Prevention
items: Use lowest-absorbency tampon, change regularly; avoid prolonged intravaginal retention and retained surgical packing
After menstrual TSS, counsel alternative menstrual products; meticulous wound care and prompt infection treatment
Routine household antibiotic prophylaxis for invasive GAS generally unnecessary; public-health exceptions depend on risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic shock: similar physiology without characteristic toxin-associated rash or source
Meningococcemia: petechiae/purpura, meningitis, positive blood cultures
Kawasaki disease: prolonged pediatric fever and mucocutaneous findings; coronary disease, usually no shock

toxic-shock-syndrome.evidence: GAS management checked 2026-10-30: [CDC streptococcal TSS guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/group-a-strep/hcp/clinical-guidance/streptococcal-toxic-shock-syndrome.html); staphylococcal management: established infectious-disease teaching.

transfusion-reactions.name: Transfusion reactions
transfusion-reactions.scope: Acute hemolytic, febrile nonhemolytic, TRALI, TACO, anaphylactic, delayed hemolytic, massive transfusion complications
transfusion-reactions.core: New symptoms during transfusion require stopping the transfusion immediately and evaluating hemolysis, infection and cardiopulmonary compromise.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior transfusion/pregnancy → alloantibodies; IgA deficiency with anti-IgA → anaphylaxis
Heart/kidney failure, rapid infusion, older age → circulatory overload

rows.label: Clues
items: Delayed hemolysis: hemoglobin falls, jaundice days–weeks after compatible transfusion; **DAT positive**, ↑indirect bilirubin
Bacterial contamination: high fever, rigors, profound hypotension; platelets particularly vulnerable
Isolated urticaria without systemic symptoms suggests mild allergic reaction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ABO mismatch → **preformed antibodies** → intravascular complement lysis; anamnestic → delayed extravascular hemolysis
TRALI: inflammatory pulmonary capillary leak; TACO: hydrostatic pressure from excess circulating volume
Febrile nonhemolytic: **cytokines accumulated in stored donor blood**; recipient anti-leukocyte antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Keep IV access with saline; **recheck patient/unit identity**, notify blood bank
Hemolysis: **DAT** shows coated RBCs; LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin; send unit/blood samples
Fever/shock → patient and product cultures; dyspnea → chest radiograph, oxygenation, volume assessment
Suspected febrile nonhemolytic reaction remains diagnosis of exclusion after hemolysis/sepsis evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute hemolysis → IV saline, support renal perfusion, treat shock/DIC; **never restart unit**
★ Anaphylaxis → **IM epinephrine**, airway support; future washed or IgA-deficient products
TRALI → supportive oxygen/ventilation; diuretics generally unhelpful unless concomitant overload
TACO → upright positioning, oxygen, **IV furosemide**; slow future transfusions
Contamination → broad IV antibiotics; isolated allergy → diphenhydramine; febrile nonhemolytic → **acetaminophen**

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute hemolysis → AKI, DIC; severe pulmonary reactions → respiratory failure
Massive transfusion → citrate hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, dilutional thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Bedside identification and crossmatch; leukoreduction reduces febrile reactions
Massive hemorrhage → balanced blood components, temperature and ionized calcium monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Underlying sepsis: symptoms may precede infusion; cultures clarify
Aspiration: event-linked infiltrate without transfusion-specific mechanism

transfusion-reactions.evidence: Not checked online; established transfusion-medicine definitions.

tuberculosis.name: Tuberculosis
tuberculosis.scope: Latent TB infection screening (PPD, IGRA), treatment regimens, active pulmonary TB, acid-fast bacilli smear and culture, RIPE therapy, extrapulmonary TB (Pott disease)
tuberculosis.core: Chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, and upper-lobe cavitation suggest contagious pulmonary tuberculosis; latent infection has no active disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Close contact, endemic residence, incarceration, homelessness, crowding, **long-term care** work/volunteering
HIV, TNF inhibitors, transplant, silicosis, diabetes → progression/reactivation risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Hemoptysis, prolonged fever; primary disease may cause hilar adenopathy or pleural effusion
★ **Back pain with vertebral destruction** → Pott disease; miliary spread causes diffuse micronodules
Tuberculous pleurisy: **lymphocytic exudate**, high protein, low glucose

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Airborne bacilli survive in macrophages; T-cell granulomas contain infection; T-cell dysfunction → reactivation, skin-test anergy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screening: **IGRA** preferred after BCG; TST read induration at 48–72 hours
Positive screening → symptoms + chest radiograph; neither test distinguishes latent from active infection
★ Active suspicion → **sputum NAAT, AFB smear, culture and susceptibility**; collect serial specimens
Negative smear, TST or IGRA does not exclude active TB, especially with immunosuppression or malnutrition
Pott suspicion → spinal MRI, biopsy/culture; assess cord compression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected contagious disease → **airborne isolation** and public-health notification
Drug-susceptible active TB: 2 months isoniazid/rifampin/pyrazinamide/ethambutol → 4 months isoniazid/rifampin
Eligible pulmonary cases ≥12 years: 4-month isoniazid/rifapentine/moxifloxacin/pyrazinamide-based regimen alternative
Latent, no RIPE: 3-month isoniazid/rifapentine or 4-month rifampin; older questions may expect **isoniazid** alone, still acceptable
Isoniazid → pyridoxine prevents neuropathy, sideroblastic anemia; Pott with deficit/instability → urgent spinal surgery evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Meningitis, adrenal destruction, spinal cord compression, bronchiectasis
INH/rifampin/pyrazinamide: hepatotoxicity; ethambutol: optic neuropathy; rifampin: enzyme induction, orange secretions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Contact investigation**, latent-treatment completion; directly observed active treatment improves adherence
Review drug interactions and baseline liver risk; monitor visual acuity/color vision with ethambutol

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung cancer: focal malignant biopsy
Fungal infection: geographic exposure; nontuberculous mycobacteria: species identification distinguishes

table.title: Positive TST thresholds
rows: HIV, close contacts, transplant, substantial immunosuppression
Healthcare workers, exposure-risk groups, comorbidities, young children

tympanic-membrane-perforation.name: Tympanic membrane perforation
tympanic-membrane-perforation.scope: Traumatic perforation, blast injury, barotrauma, secondary infection, hearing loss, management
tympanic-membrane-perforation.core: Sudden ear pain followed by bleeding, hearing reduction or tinnitus after trauma or pressure change; most uncomplicated perforations heal with dry-ear precautions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cotton swabs/ear instrumentation, slap/blast, head trauma; diving or air travel with impaired pressure equalization
Otitis media can cause spontaneous rupture; contaminated water entry increases secondary infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Visible membrane defect, bloody otorrhea; conductive loss usually exceeds pain after initial event
★ **Severe vertigo, sensorineural loss, facial weakness** → inner-ear, ossicular or temporal-bone injury
Purulent discharge or increasing pain after contamination suggests superimposed infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Membrane disruption reduces sound transmission; persistent major loss may indicate ossicular chain discontinuity
Middle-ear exposure to water/bacteria predisposes to infection; healing requires epithelial migration across defect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Gentle otoscopy** confirms defect; avoid irrigation and pneumatic pressure with suspected acute perforation
Weber lateralizes toward affected ear in conductive loss; Rinne may show bone >air conduction
**Audiometry** quantifies loss; early testing for marked deficit; repeat after healing
Blast/head injury with neurologic signs → urgent ENT ± temporal-bone CT; assess for CSF leak

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clean uncomplicated injury → **observation, dry ear, analgesia**; antibiotics not routinely needed
Contamination or purulent otorrhea → **ofloxacin or ciprofloxacin ear drops**
★ Avoid **aminoglycoside drops**, alcohol/acidifying solutions, further instrumentation; potential ototoxicity or irritation
Large defect, major hearing deficit, ongoing vertigo or facial weakness → prompt ENT evaluation
Persistent defect around 2–3 months or ossicular disruption → ENT patching/tympanoplasty or reconstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic perforation, recurrent suppurative otitis media, persistent conductive loss
Associated labyrinthine injury → permanent sensorineural loss or vestibular symptoms; epithelial ingrowth → cholesteatoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Petrolatum-coated cotton at bathing**, no swimming until healed; avoid forceful nose blowing
Avoid inserting objects into ear; pressure equalization during descent, avoid diving with congestion
Follow-up examination and hearing assessment confirm closure and identify residual deficit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Otitis externa: canal edema and tragal tenderness; membrane may be intact
Hemotympanum: blood behind intact membrane, often after trauma
Acute otitis media rupture: preceding fever/earache with bulging infected membrane, pain relief after drainage

tympanic-membrane-perforation.evidence: Antibiotic/referral decisions checked 2026-10-30: [CMAJ traumatic perforation review, 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10833100/).

type-1-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
type-1-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Autoimmune islet destruction, honeymoon phase, diabetic nephropathy screening, microalbuminuria, intensive insulin
type-1-diabetes-mellitus.core: Autoimmune beta-cell destruction causing absolute insulin deficiency; onset at any age, sometimes initially mistaken for type 2 diabetes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childhood/adolescent onset common but any age possible; family history, HLA-associated autoimmune susceptibility
Associated autoimmune thyroid disease and celiac disease; immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause insulin-deficient diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, nocturia, weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision
★ **Vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, dehydration** → evaluate DKA immediately
Honeymoon: temporary partial beta-cell recovery after diagnosis → lower insulin requirement, not cure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: T-cell-mediated islet destruction → impaired peripheral glucose uptake, hepatic glucose output and lipolysis/ketogenesis
Absent endogenous insulin → low C-peptide; glycemic variability worsened by inconsistent carbohydrate intake/exercise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Symptoms + **random glucose ≥200 mg/dL**; otherwise A1c ≥6.5%, fasting ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200
Without unequivocal hyperglycemia/crisis → confirm with second abnormal result; never delay insulin in suspected DKA
GAD65, IA-2 or ZnT8 antibodies help classify uncertain cases; antibody negativity does not exclude
★ Adults: annual **urine albumin/creatinine ratio + eGFR after 5 years**; eye examination within 5 years
Albuminuria ≥30 mg/g: confirm 2 of 3 samples over 3–6 months; exclude exercise/infection-related elevations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Basal-bolus insulin or pump + CGM**; carbohydrate-based mealtime dosing; automated delivery preferred when feasible
DKA → isotonic fluids, potassium-guided replacement, IV insulin after excluding severe hypokalemia
Typical adult A1c goal <7%, individualized for hypoglycemia/comorbidity
Hypoglycemia awake → rapid oral glucose; impaired consciousness → glucagon or IV dextrose
Hypertension + albuminuria → ACE inhibitor/ARB; no preventive RAAS blockade with normal BP/UACR/eGFR

rows.label: Complications
items: DKA, treatment-associated hypoglycemia; retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, accelerated atherosclerosis
Repeated injections into same site → lipohypertrophy and erratic absorption
Periconception hyperglycemia → **congenital heart defects** most common anomaly

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Never omit basal insulin**; sick-day glucose/ketone checks, hydration, rescue glucagon and medical identification
Foot care, BP/lipid control, vaccination; TSH; celiac serology soon after diagnosis or with symptoms
Preconception: **tight glycemic control, A1c <6.5%** → fewer anomalies, pregnancy loss; folate alone insufficient

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 2 diabetes: insulin resistance, usually preserved C-peptide; obesity does not exclude type 1
MODY: multigenerational young-onset diabetes, negative antibodies, preserved endogenous insulin
Diabetes insipidus: polyuria with dilute urine, normal glucose, often hypernatremia

type-1-diabetes-mellitus.evidence: Screening/diagnosis checked 2026-10-30: [ADA CKD Standards, 2026](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-s011); [ADA diagnosis Standards, 2026](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926); other care: established diabetes teaching.

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired glucose uptake + excess hepatic output; early compensatory **↑serum insulin**, later relative secretory failure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin; **lactic acidosis**: avoid eGFR <30, AKI/sepsis, hypoxia; no new start <45; reduce 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**
Otherwise GLP-1 RA before insulin; older exam questions may expect **basal insulin** once two orals fail
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain
Metformin: GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; pioglitazone: edema, HF; sulfonylureas: labeled caution with sulfa allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot and dilated eye examinations** (eye spacing by findings)
★ Albuminuria + hypertension → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**, never both; efferent dilation ↓intraglomerular pressure
BP ≥130/80 → antihypertensive; older exam questions may expect ACE inhibitor, also normotensive albuminuria
Statin age 40–75; glycemic control slows **neuropathy**, retinopathy, nephropathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection
Pregnancy: progesterone ureteral relaxation + uterine compression → **stasis**; physiologic right-sided ureteral dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; pyelonephritis → heavy pyuria, WBC clumps/casts; negative nitrites don't exclude
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics
Febrile non-toilet-trained child → **catheterized** urinalysis/culture; bag/clean-catch contaminate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized
Febrile infant → **cefotaxime/ceftriaxone**; first-generation cefazolin inadequate

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen
Recurrence ≥3/year or ≥2 in 6 months → postcoital or daily nitrofurantoin/TMP-SMX
Sporadic postcoital cystitis → **void before/after intercourse**; stop diaphragm/spermicide; condoms don't prevent

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV fluids + ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

uveitis.name: Uveitis
uveitis.scope: Anterior uveitis (iritis), posterior uveitis, HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathies, sarcoidosis, infectious etiologies, hypopyon, topical glucocorticoids, cycloplegic drops
uveitis.core: Painful photophobic red eye suggests anterior uveitis; painless floaters and blurred vision suggest posterior involvement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathies, sarcoidosis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, Behçet disease
Infection: HSV/VZV, syphilis, TB, toxoplasmosis; CMV with advanced immunosuppression

rows.label: Clues
items: Ciliary flush and consensual photophobia suggest anterior inflammation
Hypopyon indicates severe inflammation and can accompany infectious or sterile disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Blood-ocular barrier disruption permits inflammatory cells and protein into ocular compartments

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Slit lamp** and dilated fundus exam localize inflammation
Check visual acuity, IOP and fluorescein; urgent ophthalmology for vision loss or hypopyon
Target testing to recurrent, bilateral, granulomatous or posterior disease; consider syphilis serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Noninfectious anterior: topical **prednisolone acetate** under ophthalmology supervision
★ **Cyclopentolate** or atropine for ciliary spasm and prevention of posterior synechiae
★ Suspected infection → pathogen-directed therapy; avoid empiric steroid monotherapy
Noninfectious posterior: periocular, intravitreal or systemic anti-inflammatory therapy with specialist guidance

rows.label: Complications
items: Synechiae, cataract, glaucoma, cystoid macular edema and permanent vision loss

rows.label: Prevention
items: Routine slit-lamp screening for asymptomatic uveitis in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute angle closure: fixed mid-dilated pupil and markedly elevated IOP
Keratitis: corneal infiltrate or fluorescein-positive epithelial defect
Endophthalmitis: severe vision loss after surgery or injection, often with vitreous inflammation

table.title: Anatomic localization
rows: Cells and flare; small irregular pupil

uveitis.evidence: Checked AAO clinical resources on acute anterior uveitis.

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states
Prepubertal: hand inoculation of respiratory pathogens during URI

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy
★ Prepubertal **foul purulent/bloody discharge** → retained vaginal **foreign body**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel—discharge, ↑pH, clue cells, amine odor; Gardnerella culture unhelpful (normal flora)
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin, **no routine partner treatment**, ACOG: treat if recurrent; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole/nystatin or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure
Sarcoma botryoides: girl with bleeding, grape-like polypoid vaginal mass

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trileaflet calcification, age >70 → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Bicuspid valve: murmur from youth, premature calcific AS (40s–60s); childhood **endocarditis**; adult aortic dissection
AR: endocarditis, dissection, **root dilation** (Marfan, hypertension; murmur along right sternal border)
MR: ischemia, myxomatous prolapse (connective tissue laxity), chamber dilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva → earlier MVP click, squatting → later

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output
Mitral stenosis: ↑LA pressure, ↑PCWP, ↑pulmonary artery pressure; **LVEDP normal**; AF abolishes presystolic accentuation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration
Prosthetic dysfunction/paravalvular leak → new murmur, **schistocytes**, hemolytic anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Crescendo-decrescendo, carotids; soft A2; pulsus parvus et tardus
Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Loud S1, opening snap, apical mid-diastolic rumble
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy
LLSB holosystolic, louder on inspiration; right HF

valvular-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established echo thresholds and intervention framework.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, inherited thrombophilia
**Previous VTE** is the strongest predictor of recurrence; remote surgery months ago adds little
**Central venous catheter** → main cause of upper-extremity DVT

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload
Massive PE: high RA/PA pressure, low PCWP, low output; RV infarct: PA pressure normal/low

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week
Low-probability V/Q + high clinical suspicion is nondiagnostic → **CT angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; cancer → LMWH/DOAC; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible
Acute proximal DVT/PE without DOAC → immediate **heparin**; warfarin alone never initial; inferior in cancer

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Aspirin or 1 month inadequate; DOACs now preferred, older exam questions may expect warfarin 3–6 months
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization
Hip arthroplasty → LMWH, warfarin or DOAC; aspirin now accepted, older exam questions may expect anticoagulant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
Amniotic fluid embolism: peripartum collapse with **DIC/low fibrinogen**

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

wrist-and-hand-injuries.name: Wrist and hand injuries
wrist-and-hand-injuries.scope: Scaphoid fracture, distal radius fracture (Colles), boxer fracture, gamekeeper thumb, de Quervain tenosynovitis
wrist-and-hand-injuries.core: Mechanism and focal anatomy guide hand injury care; normal initial radiographs do not exclude a clinically important occult fracture.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fall on outstretched hand → carpal/distal radius injury; osteoporosis increases fragility-fracture risk
Closed-fist strike → fifth metacarpal; forced thumb abduction → ulnar collateral ligament injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Focal swelling, bruising, deformity, reduced grip; compare cascade and rotation with fingers flexed
★ **Numb thumb/index/middle fingers** after wrist trauma → acute median compression
Open wound, severe passive-stretch pain, pallor, or tense swelling → urgent surgical evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Carpal vascular supply and ligament stability determine ischemia/nonunion risk after injury
Displaced bone or swelling can compress nerves; rotational deformity disproportionately impairs hand function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP/lateral/oblique radiographs**; dedicated scaphoid views for suspected occult carpal fracture
Neurovascular and tendon examination before/after reduction; document capillary refill, sensation, motor function
★ **Scaphoid suspicion despite negative films** → **immobilize**, repeat in 10–14 days or early MRI
Lateral wrist view assesses carpal alignment; thumb stress instability may require radiograph/ultrasound or MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Displacement/dislocation → **analgesia, reduction, splint**; instability/neurovascular compromise → urgent orthopedics
Thumb UCL complete tear/Stener lesion → repair; partial stable tear → thumb immobilization
Inspect knuckle wounds: fight bite → irrigation, amoxicillin-clavulanate, hand-surgery evaluation if deep
Remove rings early; open fracture → sterile dressing, IV cefazolin, tetanus assessment, urgent debridement

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ Scaphoid proximal pole → **avascular necrosis/nonunion**; missed carpal dislocation → chronic instability/arthritis
Malrotation, stiffness, tendon injury, complex regional pain syndrome; Colles fracture may cause delayed extensor rupture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective sports equipment, fall prevention, osteoporosis evaluation after low-trauma fracture
Early finger motion when safe; splint-care counseling and reassessment for increasing pain/numbness

rows.label: Mimics
items: De Quervain tenosynovitis: first dorsal compartment; radial styloid pain with Finkelstein, no acute bony injury
Carpal tunnel syndrome: chronic nocturnal symptoms without traumatic deformity
Septic flexor tenosynovitis: fusiform digit, flexed posture, sheath tenderness, passive-extension pain

wrist-and-hand-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established hand-injury diagnosis and stabilization.
